entries.title: 这河所到之处,百物生长
entries.title_en: Wherever the River Goes, Everything Will Live
entries.verse: 以西结书四十七章九节
entries.content:
在以西结所见新殿的异象里,有一幅极其优美的画面:有一道河,从圣殿的门槛下流出来。这河很特别:起初只到脚踝,再往前到膝,再往前到腰,最后成了一道「不能趟的河」,深到必须泅水而过。这河一路流淌,流向死气沉沉的旷野,流入又咸又死的死海。而它所到之处,所发生的事,令人惊叹。

「这河水所到之处,凡滋生的动物都必生活,并且因这流来的水必有极多的鱼,海水也变甜了。这河水所到之处,百物都必生活。」(结47:9)请留意这河的性质:它是「生命」之河。它流到哪里,哪里就从死亡变为生机——死海的咸水变甜了,不能存活鱼类的地方有了极多的鱼,荒凉的旷野两岸长出结果子的树。这道河所经之处,一切枯死、荒凉、无生命的,都活了过来、结出果子来。而这河的源头,不在别处,正在「圣殿」——在神同在的地方。

这道从神殿中流出的生命之河,是一幅极深的属灵图画。真正的生命,不在我们自己里面,乃在神的同在里;它像一道河,从神那里流出,流到哪里,哪里就有生命。这也道破了一个属灵的原则:我们无法凭自己「制造」生命——无法靠自己叫枯干的心复苏、叫荒凉的境况开花、叫周围死气沉沉的人得着生命。我们所能做的,是让自己被这道从神而来的生命之河所充满、所漫过,然后作一个「河道」,让这生命借着我们,流向那些死寂、荒凉之处。生命不是我们的,是神的;我们不是源头,只是管道。

而这道生命之河的源头与实体,主耶稣亲自向我们指明了。祂说:「人若渴了,可以到我这里来喝……从他腹中要流出活水的江河来」——约翰解释说,这是指着信祂之人将要受的圣灵说的(约7:37-39)。以西结所见那从殿中流出、叫百物生长的生命之河,如今借着基督、藉着圣灵,要从每一个信徒的里面涌流出去。而在启示录的末了,这河汇成了「生命水的河,明亮如水晶」,从神和羔羊的宝座流出(启22:1)。今天,你是想靠自己去「制造」生命(却总觉枯干无力),还是先来到神面前,被那从祂而来的生命之河漫过,再作管道让它流向你周围死寂之处?

默想:我是否想靠自己去「制造」生命——叫枯干的心复苏、叫周围的人得生命,结果总觉枯干无力?我是否看见,真生命不在我里面,乃是从神的同在里流出的一道河?我是那源头,还是那管道?我有没有先让自己被这生命之河漫过?

应用:今天不靠自己去「挤出」生命与果效;先安静来到神面前,求那从祂而来的生命之河(圣灵)充满、漫过你;然后甘心作一个「河道」,让这生命借着你,流向一个你身边死寂、荒凉、需要生命的人或处境。

祷告:生命之河的源头,你叫那从殿中流出的河,所到之处百物都生活,连死海也变甜。我承认,我常想靠自己制造生命,却总枯干无力,忘了生命不在我里面,乃从你的同在流出。谢谢主耶稣,你叫信你的人腹中流出活水的江河。求你先用你生命的河漫过我,再叫我作管道,让这生命流向我周围死寂之处。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
In Ezekiel’s vision of the new temple, there is an extremely beautiful picture: a river flowing out from under the threshold of the temple. This river is peculiar: at first it reaches only to the ankles, then further on to the knees, then further on to the waist, and finally it becomes “a river that could not be crossed,” deep enough that one must swim. This river flows on, flowing into the lifeless wilderness, flowing into the salty, dead Dead Sea. And wherever it goes, what happens there is astonishing.

“And wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish. For this water goes there, that the waters of the sea may become fresh; so everything will live where the river goes” (Ezekiel 47:9). Notice the nature of this river: it is a river of “life.” Wherever it flows, that place turns from death into vitality — the salty water of the Dead Sea becomes fresh, a place unable to support fish teems with abundant fish, trees bearing fruit grow along the banks of the desolate wilderness. Everywhere this river passes, everything withered, desolate, lifeless comes alive, bears fruit. And this river’s source is nowhere else but the “temple” — the place of God’s presence.

This river of life flowing out from God’s temple is an extremely profound spiritual picture. True life is not within us, but in God’s presence; it is like a river, flowing out from God, and wherever it flows, there is life. This also reveals a spiritual principle: we cannot, by ourselves, “manufacture” life — we cannot, by our own strength, revive a withered heart, make a desolate situation bloom, give life to the lifeless people around us. What we can do is let ourselves be filled and overflowed by this river of life that comes from God, and then be a “riverbed,” letting this life flow, through us, to those dead, desolate places. Life is not ours; it is God’s; we are not the source, only the channel.

The Lord Jesus himself has pointed us to the source and reality of this river of life. He said: “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink... out of his heart will flow rivers of living water” — John explains this refers to the Spirit believers in him were to receive (John 7:37-39). That river of life Ezekiel saw flowing out from the temple, making everything grow, is now, through Christ, through the Holy Spirit, meant to flow out from within every believer. And at the end of Revelation, this river converges into “the river of the water of life, bright as crystal,” flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb (Revelation 22:1). Today, do you want to “manufacture” life by yourself (yet always feel withered and powerless), or come before God first, be overflowed by that river of life that comes from him, and then be a channel letting it flow to the lifeless places around you?

Meditation: Do I want to “manufacture” life by myself — reviving a withered heart, giving life to the people around me — only to always feel withered and powerless? Do I see that true life is not within me, but a river flowing out from God’s presence? Am I the source, or the channel? Have I let myself be overflowed by this river of life first?

Application: Today, don’t try to “squeeze out” life and results by yourself; first quietly come before God, asking that river of life that comes from him (the Holy Spirit) to fill and overflow you; then willingly be a “riverbed,” letting this life, through you, flow to a lifeless, desolate person or situation near you.

Prayer: Source of the river of life, you made the river flowing out from the temple bring everything to life wherever it went, even sweetening the Dead Sea. I confess I often want to manufacture life by myself, yet always feel withered and powerless, forgetting life is not within me, but flows out from your presence. Thank you, Lord Jesus, for making rivers of living water flow out from the hearts of those who believe in you. Overflow me first with your river of life, then let me be a channel, letting this life flow to the lifeless places around me. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 即或不然
entries.title_en: But If Not
entries.verse: 但以理书三章十八节
entries.content:
尼布甲尼撒王造了一个金像,下令全国的人一听见音乐,就要俯伏敬拜;不拜的,必被扔进烈火的窑中。在举国俯伏的一片人海中,有三个人挺立不跪:但以理的三个朋友——沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌。王大怒,把他们叫来,给他们最后一次机会,又威吓说:有何神能救你们脱离我手呢?这三个青年的回答,成了信心史上最铿锵有力的宣告之一。

他们说:我们所事奉的神,能将我们从烈火的窑中救出来;「即或不然,王啊,你当知道我们决不事奉你的神,也不敬拜你所立的金像。」(但3:18)请细品「即或不然」这四个字的分量。他们先宣告:我们的神能救我们。但他们的信心,并没有停在「神一定会救我」这个条件上;他们接着说「即或不然」——即使神选择不救我们、即使我们真被烧死在窑中,我们仍然决不妥协、决不下拜。他们对神的忠诚,不以「神必按我所要的搭救我」为前提;哪怕神不搭救,他们仍要忠于神。

这「即或不然」的信心,是信仰最纯、也最受考验的高度。有一种信,是「因为神会救我、会祝福我、会给我好处,所以我信、我事奉」——这种信,一旦神没有照我所要的行,就立刻动摇、甚至崩塌;它爱的,其实是神的搭救与祝福,而非神自己。而这三个青年所显出的,是一种更高的信:我信神、事奉神、忠于神,不是因为祂保证按我的意思搭救我,乃是因为祂配得——祂是神,我就当单单敬拜祂、忠于祂,无论结局如何。这种「即或不然」的信,才是真正认识神、以神为神的信;它不把神当作满足自己的工具,而是把神当作那配得一切、超乎一切结局的主。

这样的信心从何而来?它来自对神真实的、超越处境的认识。一个真认识神之伟大、圣洁、配得的人,才能在生死关头说出「即或不然」;因为在他心中,忠于这位神本身,已经比自己的性命更重、更值得。而这信心的最高榜样,是主耶稣自己:祂在客西马尼,面对十字架的烈火,说「然而,不要照我的意思,只要照你的意思」——那是「即或不然」信心的极致,而祂真的走上了那条不被「救离」的路,为要救我们。今天,你对神的信与忠,是否也悄悄地以「神必按我所要的搭救我、祝福我」为条件?求神把「即或不然」的信心赐给你——叫你无论祂搭救与否,都单单忠于祂、敬拜祂,因为祂配得。

默想:我对神的信与忠,是否悄悄地以「神必按我所要的搭救我、祝福我」为条件——一旦祂没照我的意思行,就动摇、崩塌?我爱的,究竟是神的搭救与祝福,还是神自己?我能否像那三个青年一样,说出「即或不然,我仍决不妥协、单单忠于神」?

应用:今天在一件你正指望「神必照我所要的成全」的事上,操练「即或不然」的信心——向神宣告:即使你不照我所求的行,我仍要忠于你、敬拜你、不妥协;把你对神的忠诚,从「祂必满足我」这条件上,挪到「祂配得」这根基上。

祷告:配得敬拜的主,那三个青年在烈火窑前宣告:我们的神能救我们,即或不然,我们决不下拜。我省察自己,我对你的信与忠,常悄悄以「你必按我所要的搭救、祝福我」为条件,一旦不如意就动摇。谢谢主耶稣在客西马尼说「只要照你的意思」,并真的为救我走上十字架。求你把「即或不然」的信赐给我——无论你搭救与否,我都单单忠于你,因为你配得。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden image, and commanded that everyone in the kingdom, upon hearing the music, must fall down and worship it; whoever refused would be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire. In the midst of a whole nation prostrate, three men stood upright and refused to kneel: Daniel’s three friends — Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. The king was furious, summoned them, gave them one last chance, and threatened: what god will be able to deliver you out of my hands? These three young men’s answer became one of the most resounding declarations in the history of faith.

They said: the God we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; “but if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image that you have set up” (Daniel 3:18). Consider carefully the weight of these four words, “but if not.” They first declared: our God is able to save us. But their faith did not stop at the condition of “God will certainly save me”; they went on to say “but if not” — even if God chooses not to save us, even if we truly are burned to death in the furnace, we still absolutely will not compromise, will not bow down. Their loyalty to God was not premised on “God must deliver me according to what I want”; even if God did not deliver them, they would still be faithful to God.

This “but if not” faith is the purest, most tested height of faith. There is a kind of faith that says “because God will save me, will bless me, will give me good things, I believe, I serve” — this kind of faith, the moment God doesn’t act according to what I want, immediately wavers, even collapses; what it loves is actually God’s deliverance and blessing, not God himself. What these three young men displayed instead is a higher faith: I believe in God, serve God, am faithful to God, not because he guarantees to deliver me according to my wishes, but because he is worthy — he is God, and I ought to worship him alone, be faithful to him alone, whatever the outcome. This kind of “but if not” faith is the faith that truly knows God, that treats God as God; it does not treat God as a tool to satisfy oneself, but treats God as the Lord who is worthy of everything, transcending every outcome.

Where does such faith come from? It comes from a real knowledge of God that transcends circumstances. Only a person who truly knows how great, how holy, how worthy God is can say “but if not” at a moment of life and death; because in their heart, being faithful to this God himself has already become weightier, more valuable, than their own life. And the supreme example of this faith is the Lord Jesus himself: in Gethsemane, facing the fire of the cross, he said, “yet not what I will, but what you will” — that is the extreme of “but if not” faith, and he truly walked that road not being “delivered from,” in order to save us. Today, is your faith and loyalty to God also secretly conditioned on “God must deliver me, bless me according to what I want”? Ask God to give you “but if not” faith — that whether he delivers you or not, you would still be faithful to him alone, worship him alone, because he is worthy.

Meditation: Is my faith and loyalty to God secretly conditioned on “God must deliver me, bless me according to what I want” — wavering, collapsing the moment he doesn’t act according to my wishes? What do I love — God’s deliverance and blessing, or God himself? Can I, like those three young men, say “but if not, I will still absolutely not compromise, will be faithful to God alone”?

Application: Today, in something you’re hoping “God will surely accomplish according to what I want,” practice “but if not” faith — declare to God: even if you don’t act according to what I ask, I will still be faithful to you, worship you, not compromise; move your loyalty to God from the condition of “he must satisfy me” onto the foundation of “he is worthy.”

Prayer: Lord worthy of worship, those three young men declared before the fiery furnace: our God is able to save us, but if not, we will not bow down. I examine myself, and my faith and loyalty to you are often secretly conditioned on “you must deliver, bless me according to what I want,” wavering the moment things don’t go my way. Thank you, Lord Jesus, for saying in Gethsemane “yet your will be done,” and truly walking the road to the cross to save me. Give me “but if not” faith — that whether you deliver me or not, I would be faithful to you alone, because you are worthy. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 至高者掌权
entries.title_en: The Most High Rules
entries.verse: 但以理书四章卅五节
entries.content:
尼布甲尼撒,是当时天下最有权势的君王。他站在巴比伦王宫的顶上,环顾自己所建的辉煌帝国,心中充满了骄傲,说:「这大巴比伦不是我用大能大力建为京都,要显我威严的荣耀吗?」话还在口中,天上就有声音临到他:你的国位离开你了。他随即失去了心智,被赶出人群,与野兽同住,吃草如牛,长达七年之久,直到他学会了一件事——那也是他病愈后所承认的。

「世上所有的居民都算为虚无;在天上的万军和世上的居民中,他都凭自己的意旨行事。无人能拦住他手,或问他说:你做什么呢?」(但4:35)这位曾不可一世的君王,在被彻底折服之后,承认了这个宇宙最根本的真相:真正掌权的,不是他,乃是那位至高的神。神在天上的万军、在地上的万民中,都「凭自己的意旨行事」;祂的旨意,没有任何权势能拦阻;祂的作为,没有任何人有资格质问。列国的君王、地上的强权,在祂面前,不过如虚无、如微尘;唯有祂,是那位真正的、绝对的主宰。

这真理,对活在一个「人以为自己主宰一切」时代的我们,既是当头棒喝,也是极大的安稳。当头棒喝的是:我们和尼布甲尼撒一样,极容易在稍有成就时,就把荣耀归给自己——「这是我用大能大力建成的」;把神所赐的、神所掌管的一切,当作自己的功劳与主权。神有时容许我们经历「尼布甲尼撒式」的谦卑——让我们尝到自己的无能与有限,好把我们从「我作自己的主」的幻觉中,叫醒过来。极大的安稳则是:既然是那位美善、智慧的至高者在掌权,而非盲目的命运、也非地上的强权,那么无论世界多么动荡、我个人的处境多么失控,我都可以安息——因为坐在宝座上的,是我天父,祂凭自己的美意行事,无人能拦。

这位「凭自己意旨行事、无人能拦」的至高者,在基督里,成了我们可以亲近、可以称之为「父」的神。祂绝对的主权,不是叫我们惧怕的暴政,而是叫我们安息的保障——因为掌管万有的,正是那位为我们舍了独生子、又叫万事互相效力叫爱祂的人得益处的神(罗8:28、32)。今天,你是像病中的尼布甲尼撒一样,把荣耀归给自己、以为自己主宰一切,还是像病愈后的他一样,俯伏承认「至高者掌权」?求神折服你骄傲、也除去你惧怕的心,叫你在祂绝对的主权里,既谦卑,又安息。

默想:我是否像尼布甲尼撒一样,在稍有成就时就把荣耀归给自己(「这是我大能大力建成的」),把神所掌管的一切当作自己的主权?我是否真承认「至高者掌权」——那位凭自己意旨行事、无人能拦的,是神,不是我、也不是地上的强权?这真相叫我惧怕,还是安息?

应用:今天在一处你正把荣耀归给自己、或以为「一切都得靠我掌控」的地方,刻意俯伏承认「至高者掌权」——把荣耀归还给神,把你想掌控的结局交在那位凭美意行事、无人能拦的至高者手中,在祂的主权里安息。

祷告:至高掌权的主,尼布甲尼撒骄傲自夸,被你折服七年,才承认你在天上万军、地上万民中都凭自己的意旨行事,无人能拦你的手。我承认,我常像他一样把荣耀归给自己、以为自己主宰一切。谢谢你这位掌管万有的至高者,竟是为我舍了爱子、叫万事效力的天父。求你折服我的骄傲、除去我的惧怕,叫我在你绝对的主权里,既谦卑又安息。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Nebuchadnezzar was the most powerful king on earth at the time. Standing atop the royal palace of Babylon, surveying the magnificent empire he had built, his heart filled with pride, he said: “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built by my mighty power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty?” The words were still in his mouth when a voice came from heaven to him: the kingdom has departed from you. He immediately lost his mind, was driven out from among men, dwelt with the beasts, ate grass like an ox, for seven years, until he learned one thing — the very thing he acknowledged after his recovery.

“All the inhabitants of the earth are accounted as nothing, and he does according to his will among the host of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth; and none can stay his hand or say to him, ‘What have you done?’” (Daniel 4:35). This once unrivaled king, after being utterly humbled, acknowledged this most fundamental truth of the universe: it is not he who truly rules, but the Most High God. God does “according to his own will” among the host of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth; his will, no power can obstruct; his actions, no one has the right to question. The kings of the nations, the powers of the earth, before him are nothing but emptiness, but dust; he alone is the true, absolute Sovereign.

This truth, for us living in an age where “man thinks himself master of everything,” is both a jolting wake-up call and a tremendous stability. The wake-up call: we, like Nebuchadnezzar, are extremely prone, the moment we achieve something, to give the glory to ourselves — “this I built by my own mighty power”; treating everything God has given, everything God governs, as our own credit and sovereignty. God sometimes permits us to experience a “Nebuchadnezzar-style” humbling — letting us taste our own incapacity and finitude, to wake us from the illusion of “I am my own master.” The tremendous stability is: since it is that good, wise Most High who rules, not blind fate, nor earthly power, then however turbulent the world, however out of control my own circumstances, I can rest — because the one seated on the throne is my Heavenly Father, and he acts according to his own good pleasure, and none can stop him.

This Most High, who “does according to his own will, and none can stay him,” has, in Christ, become the God we can draw near to, and call “Father.” His absolute sovereignty is not a tyranny that makes us afraid, but the guarantee that gives us rest — because the one who governs all things is exactly the God who gave up his only Son for us, and who causes all things to work together for the good of those who love him (Romans 8:28, 32). Today, are you, like the sick Nebuchadnezzar, giving glory to yourself, thinking you master everything, or, like him after recovery, bowing down to acknowledge that “the Most High rules”? Ask God to humble your pride, and also remove your fear, so that you would, in his absolute sovereignty, be both humble and at rest.

Meditation: Do I, like Nebuchadnezzar, give glory to myself the moment I achieve something (“this I built by my own mighty power”), treating everything God governs as my own sovereignty? Do I truly acknowledge that “the Most High rules” — that the one who does according to his own will, whom none can stop, is God, not me, and not any earthly power? Does this truth make me afraid, or does it give me rest?

Application: Today, in a place where you’re giving glory to yourself, or thinking “everything depends on my control,” deliberately bow down and acknowledge that “the Most High rules” — give the glory back to God, and hand the outcome you want to control over into the hands of that Most High who acts according to his good pleasure, whom none can stop, resting in his sovereignty.

Prayer: Sovereign Most High, Nebuchadnezzar was proud and boastful, and you humbled him for seven years, until he acknowledged that you, among the host of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth, do according to your own will, and none can stay your hand. I confess I often, like him, give glory to myself, thinking I master everything. Thank you that you, this Most High who governs all things, are the Father who gave up your beloved Son for me, and cause all things to work together for good. Humble my pride, and remove my fear, so that I would, in your absolute sovereignty, be both humble and at rest. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 一位像人子的
entries.title_en: One Like a Son of Man
entries.verse: 但以理书七章十四节
entries.content:
但以理在夜间的异象中,看见了四个可怕的巨兽,从海中上来——它们代表着地上一个接一个兴起、又一个接一个败亡的帝国。地上的权势,是这样凶猛、暂时、不断更替的。然而,异象没有停在这些巨兽上。但以理接着看见,亘古常在者坐着施行审判;而后,一位极其尊贵的位格,驾着天云而来。

「见有一位像人子的,驾着天云而来……得了权柄、荣耀、国度,使各方、各国、各族的人都事奉他。他的权柄是永远的,不能废去;他的国必不败坏。」(但7:13-14)请注意这位「像人子的」所得的国,与那四个巨兽的国截然不同。巨兽的国,是凶猛却短暂的、是一个取代一个、终必败亡的;而这位「人子」的国,是「永远的」、「不能废去」、「必不败坏」的。地上一切的帝国终必成为过去,唯有这一个国,存到永永远远。

「人子」这个称号,极其重要。当主耶稣在世时,祂最常用来称呼自己的,正是「人子」;当大祭司问祂是不是基督时,祂回答说:「你们要看见人子……驾着天上的云降临」——祂分明是在引用但以理书七章,宣告自己就是那位驾云而来、要得着永远国度的「人子」。所以,但以理在几百年前的夜间异象中所看见的那一位,正是道成肉身的耶稣基督;那永不败坏的国,正是基督的国。地上的政权更迭、强权兴衰,都不过是那四个巨兽的延续;而在这一切之上、也在这一切之后,有一个国要存到永远——就是我们的主基督的国。

这异象,给活在动荡时代的我们极大的定见与盼望。我们容易被眼前的「巨兽」——那些强横的政权、席卷的潮流、看似不可一世的势力——吓住,以为它们就是历史的主宰、就是终局。但但以理让我们看见得更远:这些巨兽,无论多凶猛,都是暂时的、都要过去的;真正得着永远国度、真正说了算的,是那位「像人子的」基督。所以,不要把你的盼望、你的安全感,押在任何一个终必败亡的地上「巨兽」上;把它押在那位国度永不败坏的人子身上。祂的国必要完全降临,而凡属祂的,都要在祂永远的国里有份。今天,你效忠的、盼望的,是哪一个国?

默想:我是否被眼前的「巨兽」(强横的政权、席卷的潮流、不可一世的势力)吓住,以为它们就是历史的主宰与终局?我是否看见,这些巨兽都是暂时的、必过去的,唯有那位「像人子的」基督,得着永不败坏的国?我效忠、盼望的,是终必败亡的地上之国,还是基督永远的国?

应用:今天当你为世界的动荡、某个强权或潮流而惧怕、忧虑时,刻意把眼光从那必过去的「巨兽」,抬向那位得着永远国度的人子基督;把你的盼望与效忠,从地上之国,重新钉在祂永不败坏的国上。

祷告:得着永远国度的人子主耶稣,但以理在异象中看见地上的巨兽凶猛却短暂,唯有你的国永远、不能废去、必不败坏。我承认,我常被眼前不可一世的「巨兽」吓住,把盼望押在终必败亡的地上之国上。谢谢你就是那位驾云而来、说了算的人子。求你叫我不惧怕必过去的巨兽,把盼望与效忠,单单钉在你永不败坏的国上。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
In a night vision, Daniel saw four terrifying beasts rising out of the sea — representing empires on earth rising one after another, and falling one after another. Earthly power is like this — fierce, temporary, constantly changing hands. Yet the vision did not stop at these beasts. Daniel went on to see the Ancient of Days seated, executing judgment; and then, one figure of extreme dignity, coming with the clouds of heaven.

“And behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man... and to him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him; his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed” (Daniel 7:13-14). Notice how utterly different the kingdom this “one like a son of man” received is from the kingdoms of the four beasts. The beasts’ kingdoms are fierce yet temporary, one replacing another, ultimately doomed to fall; but this “Son of Man’s” kingdom is “everlasting,” “shall not pass away,” “shall not be destroyed.” Every earthly empire will surely become the past; only this one kingdom endures forever and ever.

The title “Son of Man” is extremely significant. When the Lord Jesus was on earth, the title he most often used for himself was exactly “Son of Man”; when the high priest asked him if he was the Christ, he answered: “you will see the Son of Man... coming with the clouds of heaven” — he was clearly quoting Daniel 7, declaring himself to be the very one who comes with the clouds and receives the everlasting kingdom, the “Son of Man.” So the one Daniel saw in his night vision hundreds of years earlier is exactly Jesus Christ made flesh; that never-perishing kingdom is exactly Christ’s kingdom. The changing of earthly regimes, the rise and fall of powers, are nothing but the continuation of those four beasts; and above all of this, and after all of this, there is one kingdom that will endure forever — the kingdom of our Lord Christ.

This vision gives us, living in a turbulent age, tremendous certainty and hope. We’re easily frightened by the “beasts” before our eyes — those fierce regimes, sweeping trends, seemingly unrivaled powers — thinking they are the masters of history, the final word. But Daniel lets us see further: these beasts, however fierce, are temporary, all doomed to pass; the one who truly receives the everlasting kingdom, who truly has the final say, is that Christ who is “like a son of man.” So don’t stake your hope, your security, on any earthly “beast” doomed to fall; stake it on the Son of Man whose kingdom never perishes. His kingdom will surely come in fullness, and everyone who belongs to him will surely have a share in his everlasting kingdom. Today, which kingdom are you loyal to, hoping in?

Meditation: Am I frightened by the “beasts” before my eyes (fierce regimes, sweeping trends, seemingly unrivaled powers), thinking they are the masters and final word of history? Do I see that these beasts are all temporary, all doomed to pass, and only that Christ who is “like a son of man” receives the never-perishing kingdom? Am I loyal to, hoping in, the earthly kingdom doomed to fall, or Christ’s everlasting kingdom?

Application: Today, when you’re afraid or anxious over the world’s turbulence, some power, or some trend, deliberately lift your gaze from that “beast” doomed to pass, to the Son of Man Christ who has received the everlasting kingdom; re-anchor your hope and loyalty from the earthly kingdom onto his never-perishing kingdom.

Prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of Man who has received the everlasting kingdom, Daniel saw in his vision that the earthly beasts are fierce yet temporary, and only your kingdom is everlasting, shall not pass away, shall not be destroyed. I confess I’m often frightened by the unrivaled “beasts” before my eyes, staking my hope on the earthly kingdom doomed to fall. Thank you for being the Son of Man who comes with the clouds and has the final say. Let me not fear the beasts that will pass, but anchor my hope and loyalty solely on your never-perishing kingdom. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 智慧人必发光如星
entries.title_en: Those Who Are Wise Shall Shine Like the Stars
entries.verse: 但以理书十二章三节
entries.content:
但以理书的末了,是关于末后与结局的预言。神向但以理揭示,将来必有大艰难的日子,但神的百姓必蒙拯救;更宣告了那明确的复活盼望:「睡在尘埃中的,必有多人复醒。其中有得永生的,有受羞辱永远被憎恶的。」(但12:2)死亡不是终局;将来必有复活,有永远的结局。而紧接着这复活的宣告,神说了一句关乎「什么样的人生最有价值」的话。

「智慧人必发光如同天上的光;那使多人归义的,必发光如星,直到永永远远。」(但12:3)请注意神在这里如何定义「有价值、有荣耀」的人生。在永恒的光中回望,那真正「发光如星、直到永永远远」的,不是那些今生最有权势、最有财富、最有名望的人;乃是两种人:「智慧人」——就是敬畏神、认识神、按神的真理而活的人;以及「使多人归义的」——就是把别人领到神面前、领向那使人称义之救恩的人。神所看为永恒荣耀的人生,不是自己活得多风光,而是活出神的智慧、又把别人带向神。

这彻底颠覆了世界衡量「成功人生」的标准。世界告诉我们,一个有价值的人生,是要出人头地、要功成名就、要留下自己的名声与财富。可但以理书从永恒的角度告诉我们:今生这一切的荣耀,都要随死亡烟消云散;唯有两样存到永远、发光如星——认识神的智慧,和使人归义的果子。你若把一生都投资在那些「今生发光、永恒里却熄灭」的东西上,到头来是一场空;唯有把生命投资在「认识神」和「领人归神」上的,才在永恒里真正发光。这不是叫我们轻看今生的责任,而是叫我们用永恒的眼光,重新衡量什么才真正值得我们倾注一生。

而这「使多人归义」的荣耀,归根究底,是分享了基督的荣耀。因为唯有基督,是那位真正使多人成为义的(罗5:19);我们所能做的,不过是作祂的器皿、见证祂、把人领到祂面前。当我们这样做,我们就是在参与那存到永远、发光如星的工作。所以,不要问「我这一生怎样才能出人头地」;要问「我这一生怎样才能更认识神、又把更多人领到神面前」。因为唯有这样的人生,在永恒的光中,发光如星,直到永永远远。今天,你正把一生,投资在什么上面?

默想:我是否用世界的标准(出人头地、功成名就、名声财富)来衡量「有价值的人生」?但从永恒回望,唯有「智慧人」(认识神、按真理而活)与「使多人归义的」(领人归神),才发光如星、直到永远——我正把一生投资在哪一类事上?

应用:今天用永恒的眼光重新衡量你的人生投资:在一件你正倾注心力、却「今生发光、永恒里却熄灭」的事上,把一部分心力挪向那存到永远的——更深地认识神,并采取一个具体行动,把一个人领向神(分享、代祷、关怀、见证)。

祷告:赐永恒眼光的主,你说唯有智慧人与使多人归义的,必发光如星,直到永永远远。我承认,我常用世界的标准衡量成功,把一生投资在那些今生发光、永恒里却熄灭的东西上。谢谢基督,唯有你使多人成为义;求你叫我作你的器皿,把生命投资在认识你、领人归你上,好在永恒的光中,发光如星。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The end of Daniel is prophecy concerning the last things and the final outcome. God reveals to Daniel that a time of great trouble will surely come, but God’s people will surely be delivered; and he declares the clear resurrection hope: “many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt” (Daniel 12:2). Death is not the end; there will surely be a resurrection, an eternal outcome. And right after this declaration of resurrection, God speaks a sentence about “what kind of life is truly valuable.”

“And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky above; and those who turn many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever” (Daniel 12:3). Notice how God defines a “valuable, glorious” life here. Looking back in the light of eternity, those who truly “shine like the stars forever and ever” are not those with the most power, wealth, and fame in this life; they are two kinds of people: “the wise” — those who fear God, know God, and live by God’s truth; and “those who turn many to righteousness” — those who lead others before God, toward that salvation which justifies. The life God counts as eternal glory is not one lived brilliantly for oneself, but one that lives out God’s wisdom, and leads others toward God.

This completely overturns the world’s standard for measuring a “successful life.” The world tells us a valuable life is one that stands out, achieves great success, and leaves behind its own fame and wealth. But Daniel tells us, from an eternal perspective: all this life’s glory will vanish with death; only two things endure forever, shining like stars — the wisdom of knowing God, and the fruit of turning people to righteousness. If you invest your whole life in things that “shine in this life, yet go out in eternity,” in the end it will all come to nothing; only investing your life in “knowing God” and “leading people to God” truly shines in eternity. This is not to say we should belittle this life’s responsibilities, but to call us to re-measure, with eternal eyes, what is truly worth pouring our whole life into.

And this glory of “turning many to righteousness,” traced to its root, is sharing in Christ’s glory. Because only Christ is the one who truly makes many righteous (Romans 5:19); all we can do is be his vessel, testify to him, and lead people before him. When we do this, we are participating in that work which endures forever, which shines like the stars. So don’t ask “how can I stand out in this life”; ask “how can I know God more deeply, and lead more people before God in this life.” Because only such a life, in the light of eternity, shines like the stars, forever and ever. Today, what are you investing your life in?

Meditation: Do I use the world’s standard (standing out, achieving success, fame and wealth) to measure a “valuable life”? But looking back from eternity, only “the wise” (knowing God, living by the truth) and “those who turn many to righteousness” (leading people to God) shine like the stars, forever and ever — what am I investing my life in?

Application: Today, re-measure your life’s investments with eternal eyes: in something you’re pouring your heart into that only “shines in this life, yet goes out in eternity,” move a portion of that effort toward what endures forever — knowing God more deeply, and take one concrete action to lead a person toward God (sharing, praying for them, caring for them, testifying to them).

Prayer: Lord who gives eternal perspective, you say only the wise and those who turn many to righteousness shall shine like the stars, forever and ever. I confess I often measure success by the world’s standard, investing my life in things that shine in this life, yet go out in eternity. Thank you, Christ, that only you make many righteous; let me be your vessel, investing my life in knowing you and leading people to you, so as to shine like the stars in eternal light. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 主是怜悯饶恕人的——数算恩典
entries.title_en: To the Lord Our God Belong Mercy and Forgiveness — Counting Your Blessings
entries.content:
主是怜悯饶恕人的——数算恩典

「主－我们的 神是怜悯饶恕人的,我们却违背了他。」(但以理书 9:9)

这一周,我们看见神要与人永远同住、生命之河从祂殿中流出、至高者在列国中掌权、人子得着永远的国。而但以理在为百姓认罪时,道出了这一切背后神的性情:祂是「怜悯饶恕人的」。

今天安息日,请把这句话反复咀嚼。但以理不是在百姓行为良善时说这话的——他正在为百姓的悖逆、违背、犯罪痛切认罪;恰恰在承认「我们却违背了他」的同一口气里,他宣告:主是「怜悯饶恕人的」。这就是福音的次序:我们的失败,从不叫神的怜悯枯竭;恰恰是在我们最不配、最悖逆之处,神怜悯饶恕的性情显得最亮。今天,数算祂向你所施的怜悯与饶恕——一次次不该得的赦免、一次次悖逆后仍被接纳。祂的本性,就是怜悯饶恕人;安息在这样一位神的恩典里。

"To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him." (Daniel 9:9)
entries.content_en:
To the Lord Our God Belong Mercy and Forgiveness — Counting Your Blessings

"To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him." (Daniel 9:9)

This week, we saw that God will dwell with man forever, that a river of life flows out from his temple, that the Most High rules among the nations, and that the Son of Man has received an everlasting kingdom. And as Daniel confessed sin on behalf of his people, he revealed the character of God behind all of it: he is one "to whom belong mercy and forgiveness."

Today, on the Sabbath, chew on this sentence again and again. Daniel did not say this when the people’s conduct was good — he was in the midst of grieving over the people’s rebellion, disobedience, and sin; and in that very same breath of confessing "we have rebelled against him," he declared: to the Lord belong mercy and forgiveness. This is the order of the gospel: our failure never causes God’s mercy to run dry; it is exactly in the place of our greatest unworthiness, our greatest rebellion, that God’s character of mercy and forgiveness shines brightest. Today, count the mercy and forgiveness he has shown you — undeserved pardon after undeserved pardon, being received again and again after rebellion. His very nature is to show mercy and to forgive; rest in the grace of such a God.

"To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him." (Daniel 9:9)

entries.title: 你再去爱那不忠的
entries.title_en: Go Again, Love a Woman Who Is Unfaithful
entries.verse: 何西阿书三章一节
entries.content:
神吩咐先知何西阿,做了一件极不寻常、甚至叫人费解的事:去娶一个淫妇为妻。何西阿娶了歌篾,生了孩子;然而歌篾却离开他,回到淫乱里,委身于别的情人,最终甚至沦落到被卖为奴的地步。这是一段何等痛的婚姻。而神为什么要祂的先知,亲身经历这样一段被背叛的婚姻?因为神要借着何西阿的痛,让以色列、也让我们,看见祂自己的心——祂对那背弃祂之百姓那份不可思议的爱。

「耶和华对我说:你再去爱一个淫妇,就是她情人所爱的;好像以色列人,虽然偏向别神,喜爱葡萄饼,耶和华还是爱他们。」(何西阿书3:1)请听神的吩咐——「你再去爱」。歌篾已经背叛了、已经离开了、已经沦落为奴了,按人的一切道理,何西阿都有充分的理由弃绝她、休了她、任凭她自作自受。神却说:你再去爱她。而且经文特意点明:何西阿要用银子、用大麦,把已经沦为奴隶的歌篾,亲自赎买回来。他不是被动地等她回头,他是主动地、付上代价地,把那个背叛了他、如今一无所有的妻子,重新买赎回家。这幅图画,让我们看见神的爱是何等一种爱——它爱的,是那不可爱的;它追的,是那背弃祂的;它甚至付上代价,把那已经沦为奴隶的,亲自赎买回来。

这就彻底地颠覆了我们对「爱」和「恩典」的天然理解。我们以为,爱是给那可爱的、值得的、忠心的;可神对以色列、对我们的爱,却是「你再去爱那淫妇」式的爱——它临到的,恰恰是那不忠的、背弃的、沦落的、一无可取的。这也拆穿了我们心里那个隐秘的谎言:「我一定要先变好、先值得被爱,神才会爱我。」不。神的爱,不是因你可爱才临到你;正相反,是在你还是「淫妇」、还是「罪人」、还毫无可取之时,神就爱了你,并付上代价买赎了你。

而这「用银子赎买淫妇」的图画,在各各他得着了完全的应验。何西阿用大麦银子赎回歌篾,预表着基督用祂自己的宝血,把我们这些「灵里行淫、背弃神」的人,从罪与死的奴役中赎买回来。「惟有基督在我们还作罪人的时候为我们死,神的爱就在此向我们显明了」(罗5:8)。你我今天蒙爱,不是因为我们忠贞、可爱、值得;而是因为有一位主,在我们还悖逆、还不配的时候,就「再去爱」了我们,并付上祂性命的代价,把我们买赎回家。今天,你是否还以为「要先变好、先值得,神才会爱我」?来看何西阿的婚姻:祂爱你,不是因你可爱;祂在你还是「淫妇」时,就付代价爱了你、赎了你。安息在这不讲条件的爱里。

默想:我心里是否藏着一个谎言——「我要先变好、先值得被爱,神才会爱我」?何西阿「再去爱那淫妇、用银子把她赎回」的图画,如何拆穿这谎言?我是否真看见,神爱的、赎的,恰恰是那不忠、背弃、一无可取时的我?

应用:今天不再靠「我够不够好、够不够值得」来衡量神对你的爱;单单支取「神在我还是淫妇、还不配时,就付代价爱了我、赎了我」这不讲条件的爱;并去向一个「不值得你善待、甚至亏待过你」的人,效法这份「再去爱」的爱。

祷告:再去爱那不忠之人的主,你吩咐何西阿再去爱那背叛他的淫妇、用银子把她赎回,好显明你怎样爱那偏向别神的以色列。我承认,我常以为要先变好、先值得,你才会爱我。谢谢你,在我还作罪人、灵里行淫、一无可取时,就付上基督宝血的代价,爱了我、赎了我。求你叫我安息在这不讲条件的爱里,也照样去爱那不配的人。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
God commanded the prophet Hosea to do an extremely unusual, even bewildering thing: go marry a prostitute. Hosea married Gomer, and they had children; yet Gomer left him, returning to prostitution, giving herself to other lovers, ultimately even falling so low as to be sold into slavery. What a painful marriage this was. And why would God have his prophet personally experience such a betrayed marriage? Because God wanted, through Hosea’s pain, to let Israel, and let us, see his own heart — that incredible love he had for the people who forsook him.

“And the LORD said to me, ‘Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, even as the LORD loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods’” (Hosea 3:1). Hear God’s command — “go again, love.” Gomer had already betrayed, already left, already fallen into slavery; by every human logic, Hosea had every reason to reject her, divorce her, let her reap what she sowed. But God said: go again, love her. And the text specifically notes that Hosea would use silver and barley to personally redeem Gomer, now fallen into slavery, buying her back. He was not passively waiting for her to turn back — he actively, at a cost, bought back home that wife who had betrayed him and now had nothing. This picture lets us see what kind of love God’s love is — it loves the unlovable; it pursues the one who has forsaken it; it even pays a price to personally redeem the one who has fallen into slavery.

This completely overturns our natural understanding of “love” and “grace.” We think love is given to the lovable, the deserving, the faithful; but God’s love toward Israel, toward us, is a “go again, love that prostitute” kind of love — it comes precisely to the unfaithful, the betraying, the fallen, the utterly unworthy. This also exposes a hidden lie in our hearts: “I must first become good, first be deserving, before God will love me.” No. God’s love does not come to you because you’re lovable; on the contrary, while you were still a “prostitute,” still a “sinner,” still utterly unworthy, God already loved you, and paid a price to redeem you.

And this picture of “redeeming a prostitute with silver” found its complete fulfillment at Golgotha. Hosea redeeming Gomer with barley and silver foreshadows Christ, with his own precious blood, redeeming us who have “committed spiritual adultery, forsaken God” from the slavery of sin and death. “But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us” (Romans 5:8). You and I are loved today not because we’re faithful, lovable, deserving; but because there is a Lord who, while we were still rebellious, still unworthy, “went again to love” us, and paid the price of his own life, redeeming us home. Today, do you still think “I must first become good, first be deserving, before God will love me”? Come and see Hosea’s marriage: he loves you not because you’re lovable; he loved you and redeemed you at a cost while you were still a “prostitute.” Rest in this unconditional love.

Meditation: Is there a lie hidden in my heart — “I must first become good, first be deserving, before God will love me”? How does the picture of Hosea “going again to love that prostitute, redeeming her with silver” expose this lie? Do I truly see that what God loves, what he redeems, is exactly me at my most unfaithful, betraying, utterly unworthy?

Application: Today, stop measuring God’s love toward you by “am I good enough, deserving enough”; simply draw on this unconditional love — “while I was still a prostitute, still unworthy, God paid a price to love me and redeem me”; and go, toward someone “undeserving of your kindness, who has even wronged you,” emulate this love of “going again to love.”

Prayer: Lord who goes again to love the unfaithful, you commanded Hosea to go again and love the prostitute who betrayed him, redeeming her with silver, to show how you love Israel, who turned to other gods. I confess I often think I must first become good, first be deserving, before you will love me. Thank you for, while I was still a sinner, still committing spiritual adultery, still utterly unworthy, paying the price of Christ’s precious blood, loving me and redeeming me. Let me rest in this unconditional love, and likewise go love the undeserving. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 我喜爱良善,不喜爱祭祀
entries.title_en: I Desire Steadfast Love and Not Sacrifice
entries.verse: 何西阿书六章六节
entries.content:
以色列人并没有完全放弃宗教。他们照样献祭、照样守节、照样有一套敬拜神的外在形式。然而,神却对他们的这一切「敬虔」深感厌烦。因为他们的心,早已远离了神:他们的爱心「如同早晨的云雾,又如速散的甘露」,转瞬即逝;他们外面照旧献祭,里面却充满了虚谎、流血、拜偶像。神借何西阿,一针见血地道出了祂所真正看重的。

「我喜爱良善,不喜爱祭祀;喜爱认识神,胜于燔祭。」(何西阿书6:6)请注意神在这里所作的对比。「祭祀」「燔祭」,代表着一切外在的宗教行为——献祭、聚会、奉献、事奉;这些本是神所设立的,本身并没有错。可神说,祂所「喜爱」的,首先不是这些外在的宗教活动,而是「良善(慈爱)」与「认识神」——是一颗真正爱神、也真实认识神、并因此爱人的心。神所要的,从来不是没有心的宗教仪式;祂要的,是那颗心本身。一套完美的、却没有真爱与真认识作里子的宗教外壳,在神眼中,不但没有价值,反而叫祂厌烦。

这话,是对一切「有宗教、没生命」之信仰的当头棒喝,也是对我们每个人的省察。我们太容易把信仰,活成一套外在的「宗教行为」:主日按时聚会、灵修按表打卡、奉献按例照给、事奉尽职尽责——这些都不错,可我们里面那颗心,是否真的在爱神、在认识神,还是早已冷淡、麻木,只剩下一套惯性运转的宗教流程?神在这里提醒我们:你可以样样「祭祀」都做到无可挑剔,而里面却没有「良善」与「认识神」;这样的敬虔,是空的。神先要的,不是你的献祭,是你的心;不是你为祂做了多少,是你是否真认识祂、爱祂。

主耶稣在世时,曾两次引用这节经文,来责备那些外面严守律法、里面却没有怜悯与真认识的法利赛人(太9:13;12:7)。祂来,不是要人多一套宗教;祂来,是要把人从「有宗教、没生命」里救出来,赐给人一颗真认识神、真爱神的新心。而真正的「认识神」,唯独在基督里:「认识你独一的真神,并且认识你所差来的耶稣基督,这就是永生」(约17:3)。今天,省察你的信仰:是一套惯性运转、却没有心的「祭祀」,还是一颗真爱神、真认识神的心?神先要的,是你的心。求祂把你从空洞的宗教外壳里救出来,重新认识祂、爱祂。

默想:我的信仰,是否活成了一套外在的「宗教行为」——按表聚会、打卡灵修、照例奉献、尽职事奉,里面那颗心却早已冷淡麻木?神说祂「喜爱认识神,胜于燔祭」——我为神做的这一切背后,是否有一颗真爱祂、真认识祂的心?

应用:今天省察一项你一直「按惯性」在做、却没了心的属灵操练(读经、祷告、聚会、事奉);不只把它「做完」,而是刻意带着一颗真渴慕认识神、爱神的心去做,把重心从「为神做事」转回「真认识神」。

祷告:鉴察人心的主,你说你喜爱良善与认识你,胜过祭祀燔祭。我承认,我常把信仰活成一套惯性运转的宗教行为,样样都做,里面那颗心却冷淡麻木,失了对你真实的爱与认识。谢谢主耶稣来,要把我从「有宗教、没生命」里救出来。求你把我从空洞的外壳里救出,赐我一颗真认识你、真爱你的心。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The Israelites had not completely abandoned religion. They still offered sacrifices, still kept the feasts, still had a whole external form of worshiping God. Yet God was deeply weary of all this “godliness” of theirs. Because their hearts had long since drifted from God: their love was “like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away,” vanishing in an instant; outwardly they still offered sacrifices as usual, but inwardly were full of lies, bloodshed, and idolatry. Through Hosea, God plainly reveals what he truly values.

“For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings” (Hosea 6:6). Notice the contrast God makes here. “Sacrifice” and “burnt offerings” represent all outward religious activity — offerings, gatherings, giving, service; these were things God himself instituted, and there is nothing inherently wrong with them. But God says what he “desires” is first of all not these outward religious activities, but “steadfast love” and “the knowledge of God” — a heart that truly loves God, truly knows God, and therefore loves people. What God wants has never been religious ritual without a heart; what he wants is the heart itself. A perfect religious shell, without true love and true knowledge as its substance, is not only worthless in God’s eyes, but actually wearies him.

This word is a jolting wake-up call for every faith that has “religion but no life,” and a self-examination for each of us. We too easily live our faith as a set of outward “religious behaviors”: attending Sunday service on time, checking off devotions on schedule, giving as usual, serving diligently — none of this is wrong, but is that heart within truly loving God, truly knowing God, or has it already grown cold, numb, left with nothing but an inertial religious routine? God reminds us here: you can do every “sacrifice” impeccably, while having no “steadfast love” and “knowledge of God” within; such godliness is empty. What God wants first is not your sacrifice, but your heart; not how much you’ve done for him, but whether you truly know him, love him.

The Lord Jesus, when he was on earth, quoted this verse twice, to rebuke the Pharisees who outwardly kept the law strictly, yet had no mercy and true knowledge within (Matthew 9:13; 12:7). He came not to give people another religion; he came to save people out of “religion without life,” giving people a new heart that truly knows God, truly loves God. And truly “knowing God” is found solely in Christ: “this is eternal life, that they know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent” (John 17:3). Today, examine your faith: is it a set of inertially running “sacrifices” without a heart, or a heart that truly loves God, truly knows God? What God wants first is your heart. Ask him to save you out of an empty religious shell, to know him and love him afresh.

Meditation: Has my faith become a set of outward “religious behaviors” — attending on schedule, checking off devotions, giving as usual, serving diligently — while the heart within has long since grown cold and numb? God says he “desires the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings” — behind all I do for God, is there a heart that truly loves him, truly knows him?

Application: Today, examine a spiritual discipline you’ve always done “out of inertia,” without heart (Bible reading, prayer, attending, service); don’t just “get it done,” but deliberately do it with a heart that truly longs to know God and love God, shifting the focus from “doing things for God” back to “truly knowing God.”

Prayer: Lord who examines the heart, you say you desire steadfast love and the knowledge of you more than sacrifice and burnt offerings. I confess I often live my faith as a set of inertially running religious behaviors, doing everything, while the heart within has grown cold and numb, losing true love and knowledge of you. Thank you, Lord Jesus, for coming to save me out of “religion without life.” Save me from the empty shell, and give me a heart that truly knows you, truly loves you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 开垦你们的荒地
entries.title_en: Break Up Your Fallow Ground
entries.verse: 何西阿书十章十二节
entries.content:
以色列在属灵上,已经硬化、荒芜了。他们「栽种的是罪孽,收割的是罪孽」;他们的心,像一块久未耕耘、长满荆棘蒺藜的荒地。就在这一片属灵的荒凉中,神借何西阿,向他们发出了一个恳切的呼召——不是绝望的宣判,而是回转的邀请。

「你们要为自己栽种公义,就能收割慈爱。现今正是寻求耶和华的时候;你们要开垦荒地,等他临到,使公义如雨降在你们身上。」(何西阿书10:12)请注意神呼召中那个关键的动作:「开垦荒地」。一块荒地,若不先经过开垦——不先把板结的硬土翻松、把荆棘蒺藜除去——无论撒下多好的种子、降下多丰的雨水,都长不出庄稼来。我们的心,也是如此。属灵的荒凉、枯干、不结果子,往往不是因为神没有降雨,而是因为我们的心「板结」了——被罪、被冷淡、被世俗、被日积月累的硬化,变成了一块生不出果子的荒地。

神说:「现今正是寻求耶和华的时候。」这话里有一份紧迫,也有一份恩典。紧迫的是:不要再拖了,现今就是回转、就是开垦你心中荒地的时候;荒地拖得越久,硬得越厉害。恩典的是:荒地是可以被开垦的——你那颗看似硬化、荒芜、无可救药的心,神并没有放弃;祂正呼召你,趁着现今,把它重新翻松、除去荆棘、向祂敞开。而「开垦荒地」,是需要「用力」的——它意味着我们要认真地对付心中的罪、除去缠累、破碎那自满与刚硬;这不是消极地等,而是主动地、恳切地寻求神,松开自己板结的心,预备好领受神的雨。

然而要记得:我们「开垦荒地」,不是靠自己的努力去「挣得」神的恩雨;开垦,是「预备领受」,而非「换取」。我们松土、除荆棘、寻求神,神就照祂的应许「临到」,「使公义如雨降在我们身上」——那使荒地变良田、使枯干结果子的,始终是从神而来的雨,不是我们的力气。这正是福音的次序:我们尽心地回转、敞开、预备,神就丰丰富富地降下祂的恩典。今天,你的心,是否也成了一块久未开垦、硬化荒芜的地?听神恳切的呼召:现今正是寻求耶和华的时候。趁着现今,用力开垦你心中的荒地——除去缠累,向神敞开,等候祂的公义如雨降下。

默想:我的心,是否也成了一块久未开垦、板结荒芜、长满荆棘的荒地,以致属灵枯干、不结果子?我的枯干,是因为神没降雨,还是因为我的心硬化、没有「开垦」?「现今正是寻求耶和华的时候」——我是否一直在拖延回转与开垦?

应用:今天就「开垦」你心中的一块荒地——具体地对付一处你一直放任、使你心硬化的罪或缠累(除去它、认它、断开它),用力松开你板结的心,向神敞开;然后等候、领受神的公义如雨降下。

祷告:降恩雨的主,你呼召荒芜的百姓:现今正是寻求耶和华的时候,你们要开垦荒地,等我使公义如雨降下。我承认,我的心已板结荒芜、长满荆棘,以致枯干不结果子,又一再拖延回转。求你叫我趁着现今,用力开垦心中的荒地,除去缠累、向你敞开;然后照你的应许,使你的公义如雨,降在我这预备好的心田上。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Israel had, spiritually, hardened and grown desolate. They “have plowed iniquity” and “reaped injustice”; their hearts were like a field long uncultivated, overgrown with thorns and briers. Right in the midst of this spiritual desolation, God, through Hosea, issues them an earnest call — not a despairing sentence, but an invitation to turn back.

“Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap steadfast love; break up your fallow ground, for it is the time to seek the LORD, that he may come and rain righteousness upon you” (Hosea 10:12). Notice the key action in God’s call: “break up your fallow ground.” A fallow field, if not first broken up — if the hardened, compacted soil is not first loosened and the thorns and briers not first removed — however good the seed sown, however abundant the rain that falls, no crops will grow. Our hearts are the same. Spiritual desolation, dryness, fruitlessness, is often not because God has not sent rain, but because our hearts have grown “hardened” — compacted, by sin, by coldness, by worldliness, by accumulated hardening, into a fallow field that cannot produce fruit.

God says: “it is the time to seek the LORD.” This word carries both urgency and grace. The urgency: don’t delay any longer — now is the time to turn back, the time to break up the fallow ground of your heart; the longer the fallow ground is left, the harder it becomes. The grace: fallow ground can be broken up — that heart of yours, which seems hardened, desolate, beyond hope, God has not given up on; he is calling you, now, to loosen it afresh, remove the thorns, and open it to him. And “breaking up fallow ground” requires “effort” — it means seriously dealing with the sin in your heart, removing entanglements, breaking self-satisfaction and hardness; this is not passively waiting, but actively, earnestly seeking God, loosening your own compacted heart, preparing to receive God’s rain.

Yet remember: our “breaking up the fallow ground” is not earning God’s rain of grace through our own effort; breaking it up is “preparing to receive,” not “exchanging for.” We loosen the soil, remove the thorns, seek God, and God, according to his promise, “comes” and “rains righteousness upon us” — what turns fallow ground into fertile field, what makes the withered bear fruit, is always the rain that comes from God, not our own strength. This is exactly the order of the gospel: we wholeheartedly turn back, open up, prepare, and God abundantly pours down his grace. Today, has your heart too become a fallow field, long uncultivated, hardened and desolate? Hear God’s earnest call: now is the time to seek the LORD. While it is still “now,” work to break up the fallow ground of your heart — remove entanglements, open up to God, and wait for his righteousness to rain down.

Meditation: Has my heart too become a fallow field, long uncultivated, compacted and desolate, overgrown with thorns, so that I’m spiritually dry, fruitless? Is my dryness because God has not sent rain, or because my heart has hardened, not been “broken up”? “It is the time to seek the LORD” — have I been delaying turning back and breaking up the ground?

Application: Today, “break up” one fallow field in your heart — concretely deal with a sin or entanglement you’ve always let go unchecked, that has hardened your heart (remove it, confess it, break with it), working to loosen your compacted heart, opening it to God; then wait for and receive God’s righteousness to rain down.

Prayer: Lord who sends the rain of grace, you call your desolate people: now is the time to seek the LORD; break up your fallow ground, and I will make my righteousness rain down. I confess my heart has become hardened and desolate, overgrown with thorns, so that I’m dry and fruitless, and I keep delaying turning back. Let me, while it is still now, work to break up the fallow ground of my heart, removing entanglements, opening up to you; then, according to your promise, let your righteousness rain down on this prepared soil of my heart. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 我怎能舍弃你
entries.title_en: How Can I Give You Up
entries.verse: 何西阿书十四章四节
entries.content:
何西阿书的末了,神的心肠向我们完全敞开了。以色列一再地背道、拜偶像、离弃神,按公义,他们早该被弃绝、被灭尽。神也确实宣告了审判。然而,就在审判的话语之间,神的心却像被撕裂一般,发出了一声几乎不像审判者、倒像慈父的哀叹:「以法莲哪,我怎能舍弃你?以色列啊,我怎能弃绝你?……我回心转意,我的怜爱大大发动。」神对这背道之民的爱,竟浓烈、深切到这个地步。

而在这份不肯舍弃的爱中,神发出了一个满有医治的应许:「我必医治他们背道的病,甘心爱他们;因为我的怒气向他们转消。」(何西阿书14:4)请细品「背道的病」这几个字。神把以色列的背道、离弃、反复的不忠,看作一种「病」——一种他们自己无力医治的顽疾。而神的回应,不是任凭他们在这病中死去,也不是仅仅定他们的罪,乃是「我必医治」。祂要亲自作那位医生,医好他们那一再背道、总是回转不了、总是好了又犯的顽疾。更美的是那句「甘心爱他们」——神的爱,不是勉强的、不是被迫的、不是「看在祂自己应许的份上」不得不爱;祂是「甘心」地、乐意地、从心底涌流地,爱这些一再伤祂心的人。

这份「医治背道之病」的应许,触及了我们许多人最深的挣扎。我们里面,常有一种「背道的病」:某个反复跌倒的罪、某种总也戒不掉的习性、某个一次次悔改又一次次回去的软弱。我们为它痛恨自己、灰心丧志,甚至怀疑神是不是早已厌烦了这样反复无常的我。神却在这里说:你那反复背道的病,不是靠你自己咬牙就能治好的;让我来医治。祂不是站在远处,冷眼看你在同一个坑里反复跌倒;祂是那位甘心俯身、要亲自医治你那顽疾的大医生。你的反复,没有耗尽祂的爱;祂对你的怜爱,仍在「大大发动」。

神「甘心爱、亲自医治背道之病」的心肠,在基督里得着了完全的成全。祂差来的,正是那位「为病人来」的大医生(太9:12);祂在十字架上,不但赦免了我们背道的罪,更藉着祂的灵,着手医治我们背道的病根,叫我们渐渐脱离那反复的辖制。今天,你是否正被某个「背道的病」缠累、灰心,以为神早已厌烦了反复的你?听神甘心的应许:我必医治你背道的病,甘心爱你。不要只靠自己咬牙去治;把这顽疾,带到那位甘心医治你的大医生面前。

默想:我里面是否有一种「背道的病」——某个反复跌倒的罪、总戒不掉的习性、一次次悔改又回去的软弱?我是否为它痛恨自己、灰心,甚至以为神早已厌烦了反复无常的我?神说「我必医治你背道的病,甘心爱你」——这如何改变我?

应用:今天把一个你一直反复跌倒、靠自己咬牙却治不好的「背道的病」,带到那位甘心医治你的大医生面前;不只靠自己的决心去戒,而是求神亲自动手医治那病根,并支取「祂仍甘心爱我、怜爱大大发动」的确据,不再灰心。

祷告:甘心医治我的大医生,你对一再背道的以色列哀叹「我怎能舍弃你」,又应许「我必医治他们背道的病,甘心爱他们」。我承认,我里面有反复跌倒的顽疾,为它灰心,又以为你早已厌烦了反复的我。谢谢你差来那为病人来的大医生基督。求你亲自医治我背道的病根,叫我支取你甘心不变的爱,不再靠自己咬牙,而是让你医治我。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
At the end of Hosea, God’s heart is fully opened to us. Israel had repeatedly turned away, worshiped idols, forsaken God; by justice, they should long ago have been rejected, utterly destroyed. God indeed pronounced judgment. Yet right in the midst of these words of judgment, God’s heart seems as if torn apart, letting out a lament that sounds almost more like a loving father than a judge: “How can I give you up, O Ephraim? How can I hand you over, O Israel?... My compassion grows warm and tender.” God’s love for this apostate people is intense, deep, to this degree.

And in this love that refuses to give up, God issues a promise full of healing: “I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them” (Hosea 14:4). Consider carefully the phrase “their apostasy.” God views Israel’s apostasy, forsaking, and repeated unfaithfulness as a kind of “sickness” — a stubborn ailment they themselves have no power to heal. And God’s response is not to leave them to die in this sickness, nor merely to condemn them, but “I will heal.” He will personally be that physician, healing them of that stubborn ailment of repeated apostasy, always failing to turn back, always healed only to sin again. Even more beautiful is the phrase “love them freely” — God’s love is not reluctant, not forced, not something he must give merely “for the sake of his own promise”; he “freely,” gladly, from the depths of his heart, loves these people who have repeatedly wounded him.

This promise of “healing the sickness of apostasy” touches the deepest struggle many of us face. Within us, there is often a kind of “sickness of apostasy”: some repeatedly stumbled sin, some habit we just can’t quit, some weakness we repent of again and again and go back to again and again. We hate ourselves for it, grow discouraged, even doubt whether God has already grown weary of this fickle, ever-recurring self. But God says here: your recurring sickness of apostasy cannot be healed by gritting your teeth alone; let me heal it. He is not standing at a distance, coldly watching you stumble again and again into the same pit; he is the great Physician who willingly stoops down, personally intending to heal your stubborn ailment. Your recurrence has not exhausted his love; his compassion for you is still “growing warm and tender.”

God’s heart of “loving freely, personally healing the sickness of apostasy” has found its complete fulfillment in Christ. He sent exactly that great Physician who “came for the sick” (Matthew 9:12); on the cross, he not only forgave the sin of our apostasy, but through his Spirit, sets about healing the root of our apostasy, gradually freeing us from that recurring dominion. Today, are you burdened, discouraged by some “sickness of apostasy,” thinking God has already grown weary of your recurring self? Hear God’s willing promise: I will heal your sickness of apostasy; I will love you freely. Don’t just try to cure it by gritting your teeth alone; bring this stubborn ailment before the great Physician who willingly heals you.

Meditation: Is there a “sickness of apostasy” within me — some repeatedly stumbled sin, some habit I just can’t quit, some weakness I repent of again and again and go back to again and again? Do I hate myself for it, grow discouraged, even think God has already grown weary of my fickle, recurring self? God says “I will heal your sickness of apostasy; I will love you freely” — how does this change me?

Application: Today, bring a “sickness of apostasy” you’ve repeatedly stumbled over, that you’ve gritted your teeth but cannot cure, before the great Physician who willingly heals you; instead of relying solely on your own resolve to quit it, ask God to personally set about healing that root of sickness, and draw on the certainty that “he still loves me freely, his compassion still growing warm and tender,” no longer discouraged.

Prayer: Great Physician who willingly heals me, you lamented over apostate Israel, “how can I give you up,” and promised, “I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely.” I confess there is a recurring, stubborn ailment within me, over which I grow discouraged, even thinking you have grown weary of my recurring self. Thank you for sending Christ, the great Physician who came for the sick. Personally heal the root of my apostasy, let me draw on your unchanging, willing love, no longer relying on my own gritted teeth, but letting you heal me. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 我要将我的灵浇灌
entries.title_en: I Will Pour Out My Spirit
entries.verse: 约珥书二章廿八节
entries.content:
约珥书的背景,是一场毁灭性的蝗灾——蝗虫铺天盖地而来,把田间的出产啃食一空,举国陷入饥荒与哀哭。神借这场灾,呼召百姓「撕裂心肠,归向耶和华」。然而,约珥书没有停在审判与哀哭里。神应许,祂不但要挽回蝗虫所吃的年岁,更要在末后的日子,倾倒下一份远超物质丰收的、属灵的大恩。

「以后,我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的。你们的儿女要说预言;你们的老年人要做异梦,少年人要见异象。」(约珥书2:28)请留意这应许的浩大。在旧约的时代,神的灵通常只临到少数被特别拣选的人——君王、先知、祭司;而神在这里应许的,是一个截然不同的新时代:祂要把祂的灵,「浇灌凡有血气的」——不分男女、老少、尊卑,凡属神的人,都要被神的灵充满。「浇灌」这个词,更是何等丰盛的图画:不是一点一滴地分配,而是像倾盆大雨一样,丰丰富富地、毫无保留地倾倒下来。

这个应许,在五旬节那一天,应验了。当门徒聚集时,圣灵如同大风、如同火焰降临,充满了他们;使徒彼得站起来,向众人宣告的第一句话,正是引用约珥书:「这正是先知约珥所说的:神说,在末后的日子,我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的」(徒2:16-17)。约珥所预言那圣灵浇灌的新时代,已经因着基督的死、复活、升天而开启了;如今,凡真心信靠基督的人,无论是谁,都领受了这浇灌下来的圣灵,成为神的灵所居住的殿。

这对每一个信徒,是何等大的恩典与提醒。你若在基督里,那使门徒得着能力、叫他们从胆怯变为刚强、叫初代教会翻转世界的同一位圣灵,也已经浇灌在你身上、住在你里面了!你事奉神、胜过罪、结出果子,靠的从来不是自己咬牙挤出来的一点力气,而是里面这位被丰丰富富浇灌下来的圣灵的大能。我们常常活得枯干、软弱、无力,不是因为神的灵不够,而是因为我们没有支取、没有倚靠那已经浇灌在我们里面的圣灵。今天,你是在靠自己的血气苦苦挣扎,还是倚靠那已经浇灌在你里面的圣灵而活?求神叫你不再靠自己,而是被祂的灵充满、支取祂的大能。

默想:我是否真意识到,那使门徒从胆怯变刚强、翻转世界的同一位圣灵,已经浇灌在我身上、住在我里面?我事奉神、胜过罪、结果子,是靠自己咬牙挤出的血气,还是倚靠里面那被丰丰富富浇灌下来的圣灵?我常枯干无力,是否因为没有支取这已赐下的大能?

应用:今天在一件你一直靠自己血气苦苦挣扎的事上(胜过某个罪、完成某项事奉、爱一个难爱的人),停止靠自己;刻意求那已浇灌在你里面的圣灵充满你、赐你能力,倚靠祂而非倚靠自己去面对。

祷告:浇灌圣灵的主,你应许要将你的灵浇灌凡有血气的;这应许已在五旬节应验,你的灵也已浇灌在每一个信你的人身上。我承认,我常靠自己的血气苦苦挣扎,活得枯干无力,却没有支取那已浇灌在我里面的圣灵。求你叫我不再靠自己,而是被你的灵充满,倚靠祂的大能事奉你、胜过罪、结出果子。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The backdrop of Joel is a devastating locust plague — locusts came covering the land, devouring every crop in the field, plunging the whole nation into famine and mourning. Through this disaster, God calls the people to “rend your hearts, and turn to the LORD.” Yet the book of Joel does not stop at judgment and mourning. God promises he will not only restore the years the locusts have eaten, but will, in the last days, pour out a spiritual blessing far exceeding material harvest.

“And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions” (Joel 2:28). Notice the vastness of this promise. In Old Testament times, God’s Spirit usually came only upon a few specially chosen people — kings, prophets, priests; but what God promises here is an utterly different new era: he will pour out his Spirit “on all flesh” — regardless of male or female, old or young, high or low status, everyone belonging to God will be filled with God’s Spirit. The word “pour out” is even more a picture of such abundance: not distributed drop by drop, but poured down abundantly, without reservation, like a torrential downpour.

This promise was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost. When the disciples were gathered, the Holy Spirit descended like a mighty rushing wind, like tongues of fire, filling them; the apostle Peter stood up, and the very first thing he declared to the crowd was exactly a quotation of Joel: “this is what was uttered through the prophet Joel: ‘And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh’” (Acts 2:16-17). That new era of the Spirit being poured out, which Joel foretold, has already been opened through Christ’s death, resurrection, and ascension; now, everyone who truly believes and trusts Christ, whoever they are, has received this poured-out Holy Spirit, becoming a temple in which God’s Spirit dwells.

This is such tremendous grace and reminder for every believer. If you are in Christ, that same Holy Spirit who empowered the disciples, turned them from timid to bold, and turned the early church upside down the world, has already been poured out on you, dwells within you! Your serving God, overcoming sin, and bearing fruit have never depended on a bit of strength squeezed out by gritting your teeth, but on the mighty power of this Holy Spirit, poured out abundantly within you. We often live withered, weak, and powerless, not because God’s Spirit is insufficient, but because we haven’t drawn on, haven’t relied on, the Holy Spirit already poured out within us. Today, are you struggling painfully by your own strength, or living by relying on the Holy Spirit already poured out within you? Ask God to let you no longer rely on yourself, but be filled by his Spirit, drawing on his mighty power.

Meditation: Do I truly realize that the same Holy Spirit who turned the disciples from timid to bold, and turned the world upside down, has already been poured out on me, dwells within me? Do I serve God, overcome sin, and bear fruit by my own gritted-teeth strength, or by relying on the Holy Spirit abundantly poured out within me? Am I often withered and powerless because I haven’t drawn on this already-given power?

Application: Today, in something you’ve been struggling painfully by your own strength (overcoming some sin, completing some service, loving a hard-to-love person), stop relying on yourself; deliberately ask the Holy Spirit already poured out within you to fill you and give you power, relying on him rather than on yourself to face it.

Prayer: Lord who pours out the Holy Spirit, you promised to pour out your Spirit on all flesh; this promise has already been fulfilled at Pentecost, and your Spirit has already been poured out on everyone who believes in you. I confess I often struggle painfully by my own strength, living withered and powerless, without drawing on the Holy Spirit already poured out within me. Let me no longer rely on myself, but be filled by your Spirit, relying on his mighty power to serve you, overcome sin, and bear fruit. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 为银子卖了义人
entries.title_en: They Sell the Righteous for Silver
entries.verse: 阿摩司书二章六节
entries.content:
阿摩司,是一个从犹大来的牧人,神差他去向北国以色列说预言。那时的以色列,正值国势强盛、经济繁荣的鼎盛期;人们生活富足,宗教活动也照常兴旺。表面上,一切都欣欣向荣。然而,神借阿摩司所发的信息,却揭开了这繁荣底下,一个叫神震怒的溃烂——他们如何对待社会中最弱小、最无助的人。

「耶和华如此说:以色列人三番四次地犯罪,我必不免去他们的刑罚;因他们为银子卖了义人,为一双鞋卖了穷人。」(阿摩司书2:6)神所控告的,不是拜偶像这类「宗教」的罪,而是社会中的不公与欺压:他们「为银子卖了义人」——为一点钱财,就出卖公义、枉屈无辜;「为一双鞋卖了穷人」——为区区一双鞋那样微不足道的利益,就把穷苦人踩在脚下、盘剥净尽。在一个宗教兴旺、经济繁荣的社会里,神的眼目,却盯住了那些被人践踏的穷人与义人;祂宣告:你们怎样对待最弱小的,我都看见了,我必追讨。

这信息,拆穿了一种极其危险的属灵幻觉:以为只要我宗教活动做得足、只要我个人道德还过得去,神就满意了,至于社会公义、至于怎样对待那些无助的人,那是「另一回事」。神却借阿摩司,把这两件事紧紧地绑在了一起:你若一面按时献祭、敬拜神,一面却欺压穷人、枉屈公义、对身边的不义视而不见,那么你所有的宗教,在神眼中都是虚假的、可憎的。因为神是公义的神,祂特别看顾那些无助的、被欺压的、发不出声音的人;凡践踏他们的,就是与神为敌。真实的敬虔,从来不能与公义、与怜悯穷人分家。

这位「为穷人伸冤」的神,在基督里向我们显明得更清楚。主耶稣宣告祂来是要「传福音给贫穷的人……叫那受压制的得自由」(路4:18);祂又说,我们怎样对待那些「最小的弟兄」——饥饿的、作客的、赤身的、被囚的——就是怎样对待祂(太25:40)。所以,一个真被福音改变的人,他的信仰绝不会只停在个人的敬虔与宗教活动里;它必然流露为对公义的看重、对弱者的怜悯、对身边不义的不再视而不见。今天,神也在鉴察:在你的生活里,你怎样对待那些比你弱小、无助、发不出声音的人?你是否也曾「为一点利益」而枉屈公义、践踏他人?求神叫你的敬虔,不与公义和怜悯分家。

默想:我是否以为,只要宗教活动做得足、个人道德过得去,神就满意了,至于社会公义、怎样对待无助的人,是「另一回事」?神却把敬拜与公义紧紧绑在一起——我怎样对待那些比我弱小、无助、发不出声音的人?我是否曾为一点利益而枉屈公义、践踏他人?

应用:今天在你的生活圈里,留意一个「比你弱小、无助、容易被忽略或践踏」的人;拒绝为自己的利益而亏待他,反而刻意以公义待他、以怜悯帮他,让你的敬虔流露为对弱者的看顾。

祷告:公义又怜悯的主,在以色列宗教兴旺、经济繁荣时,你却盯住他们为银子卖义人、为一双鞋卖穷人的不义。我承认,我常以为只要宗教做足、道德过得去就好,却对身边的不公与弱者视而不见。谢谢主耶稣来,为贫穷受压制的人传福音,又说善待最小的弟兄就是善待你。求你叫我的敬虔不与公义、怜悯分家,以公义与怜悯善待身边的弱小者。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Amos was a shepherd from Judah, whom God sent to prophesy to the northern kingdom of Israel. Israel at that time was at the peak of national strength and economic prosperity; people lived in abundance, and religious activity flourished as usual. On the surface, everything was thriving. Yet the message God delivered through Amos exposed something rotting beneath this prosperity that provoked God’s fury — how they treated the weakest, most helpless people in society.

“Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not revoke the punishment, because they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals” (Amos 2:6). What God indicts is not a “religious” sin like idolatry, but the injustice and oppression within society: they “sell the righteous for silver” — for a bit of money, they sold justice, wronged the innocent; “sell the needy for a pair of sandals” — for a benefit as insignificant as a pair of sandals, they trampled the poor underfoot, exploiting them to the utmost. In a society with thriving religion and a prosperous economy, God’s eyes fixed on those poor and righteous being trampled by others; he declares: however you have treated the weakest, I have seen it all, and I will surely hold you accountable.

This message exposes an extremely dangerous spiritual illusion: thinking that as long as my religious activity is sufficient, as long as my personal morality is passable, God is satisfied, and as for social justice, as for how the helpless are treated, that’s “a separate matter.” But through Amos, God ties these two things tightly together: if you offer sacrifices and worship God as usual on one hand, while oppressing the poor, perverting justice, and turning a blind eye to the injustice around you on the other, then all your religion, in God’s eyes, is false and detestable. Because God is a just God, he specially watches over the helpless, the oppressed, those who cannot raise their voice; whoever tramples them is at enmity with God. True godliness can never be divorced from justice, from mercy toward the poor.

This God who “pleads the cause of the poor” has revealed himself to us more clearly in Christ. The Lord Jesus declared he came to “proclaim good news to the poor... to set at liberty those who are oppressed” (Luke 4:18); he also said how we treat “the least of these brothers of mine” — the hungry, the stranger, the naked, the imprisoned — is how we treat him (Matthew 25:40). So a person truly transformed by the gospel will never have their faith stop at personal godliness and religious activity alone; it will surely overflow into a regard for justice, mercy for the weak, and no longer turning a blind eye to the injustice around them. Today, God is also examining: in your life, how do you treat those weaker, more helpless, more voiceless than you? Have you ever, “for a bit of benefit,” perverted justice, trampled others? Ask God to let your godliness never be divorced from justice and mercy.

Meditation: Do I think that as long as my religious activity is sufficient, my personal morality passable, God is satisfied, and as for social justice, how the helpless are treated, that’s “a separate matter”? Yet God ties worship and justice tightly together — how do I treat those weaker, more helpless, more voiceless than myself? Have I ever, for a bit of benefit, perverted justice, trampled others?

Application: Today, in your circle of life, take notice of someone “weaker, more helpless, more easily overlooked or trampled than you”; refuse to mistreat them for your own benefit — instead deliberately treat them with justice, help them with mercy, letting your godliness overflow into care for the weak.

Prayer: Just and merciful Lord, when Israel’s religion flourished and its economy prospered, you fixed your eyes on their injustice of selling the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals. I confess I often think that as long as religion is sufficient, morality passable, that’s enough, while turning a blind eye to the injustice and the weak around me. Thank you, Lord Jesus, for coming to proclaim good news to the poor and oppressed, and saying that treating the least of these brothers well is treating you well. Let my godliness never be divorced from justice and mercy, treating the weak around me with justice and mercy. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 竭力追求认识他——专注于神
entries.title_en: Let Us Press On to Know the LORD — Focused on God
entries.content:
竭力追求认识他——专注于神

「我们务要认识耶和华,竭力追求认识他。他出现确如晨光;他必临到我们像甘雨,像滋润田地的春雨。」(何西阿书 6:3)

这一周,我们看见神对不忠之民不肯舍弃的爱、祂喜爱人认识祂胜于祭祀、又应许医治背道的病、浇灌祂的灵。这一切,都指向一件事:神渴望我们真正地认识祂。

今天安息日,请留意这句话里的动词:「务要认识」「竭力追求认识」。认识神,不是信主那一刻就自动完成、从此一劳永逸的;它是一生「竭力追求」的功课——像追求一位所爱的人一样,越追求,越深地认识。而这追求从不落空:「他出现确如晨光」——祂必向竭力寻求祂的人显现,如清晨的曙光一样确实;祂必如春雨临到你,滋润你干渴的心田。今天,不要满足于「关于神的一些道理」;竭力追求认识祂本身。你越追求,祂越向你显明;你越认识祂,你的心就越被祂滋润、越以祂为乐。

"Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD; his going out is sure as the dawn." (Hosea 6:3)
entries.content_en:
Let Us Press On to Know the LORD — Focused on God

"Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD; his going out is sure as the dawn; he will come to us as the showers, as the spring rains that water the earth." (Hosea 6:3)

This week, we saw God’s love that refuses to give up on the unfaithful, his desire to be known rather than merely be given sacrifices, his promise to heal apostasy, and his pouring out of the Spirit. All of it points to one thing: God longs for us to truly know him.

Today, on the Sabbath, notice the verbs in this sentence: "let us know," "let us press on to know." Knowing God is not something completed automatically the moment you believe, settled once and for all from then on; it is a lifelong lesson of "pressing on" — like pursuing someone you love, the more you pursue, the more deeply you know. And this pursuit never comes to nothing: "his going out is sure as the dawn" — he will surely appear to those who earnestly seek him, as certain as the morning light; he will surely come to you like the spring rain, watering your thirsty heart. Today, don’t be satisfied with "some doctrines about God"; press on to know him himself. The more you pursue, the more he reveals himself to you; the more you know him, the more your heart is watered by him, and the more you delight in him.

"Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD; his going out is sure as the dawn." (Hosea 6:3)

entries.title: 听不见神话语的饥荒
entries.title_en: A Famine of Hearing the Words of the LORD
entries.verse: 阿摩司书八章十一节
entries.content:
阿摩司向繁荣却不义的以色列,宣告了一连串的审判。而在这些审判中,有一样是最可怕、也最出人意料的。人所惧怕的饥荒,通常是没有粮食、没有水的饥荒;可神在这里宣告的,是一种更深、更致命的饥荒。

「主耶和华说:日子将到,我必命饥荒降在地上。人饥饿非因无饼,干渴非因无水,乃因不听耶和华的话。」(阿摩司书8:11)这是「听不见神话语」的饥荒。请思想这是何等严重的一种刑罚:神任凭他们,收回祂的话——他们再也听不见神向他们说话了。他们要东奔西跑,遍地寻求耶和华的话,却寻不着。当一个人、一个时代,长久地厌弃、不听神的话,神最终会照他们所要的,收回祂的话,任凭他们落在一种「听不见神」的可怕荒凉里。而这饥荒之所以最可怕,是因为身处其中的人,往往感觉不到自己在挨饿——他们照旧吃喝、照旧忙碌、照旧「过得不错」,却不知自己的灵,正在一种听不见神的饥荒中,慢慢地枯死。

这警告,对活在一个「神的话唾手可得、却少有人真听」的时代的我们,格外扎心。我们何等有福:圣经就在手边,随时可读;讲道、书籍、资源多到数不清。可我们是否珍惜、是否饥渴地「听」?一个长久把神的话挤在一边、听而不闻、有而不读的人,虽然圣经就在书架上,他里面却可能正处在一场「听不见神话语」的饥荒中——不是神不说话,而是他早已不听、也听不进了。当神的话失去它当有的分量,当我们对它麻木、厌倦、可有可无时,那属灵饥荒的阴影,就已经悄悄笼罩下来了。

主耶稣说:「人活着,不是单靠食物,乃是靠神口里所出的一切话」(太4:4)。神的话,是我们属灵生命的粮;没有它,人的灵必要饥饿、枯干、死亡。而这话,最终成了肉身——「太初有道……道成了肉身」(约1:1、14);我们若饥渴地来到圣经面前,所要饱足的,归根究底是基督自己。所以,趁着现今神的话还向你敞开、你还听得见,不要轻慢它、不要让它蒙尘。像饥饿的人扑向食物一样,饥渴地来听、来读、来遵行神的话;免得有一天,落在那最可怕、却最无知无觉的饥荒里。今天,你对神的话,是饥渴,还是麻木?

默想:我是否活在一个「神的话唾手可得、我却听而不闻」的光景里?我对神的话,是像饥饿的人扑向食物一样饥渴,还是麻木、厌倦、可有可无?我是否正处在一场「听不见神话语」的饥荒中,却因照旧吃喝忙碌而毫无察觉?

应用:今天不轻慢那唾手可得的神的话;像饥饿的人一样,饥渴地读一段圣经——不只求「读完」,而是渴慕从中真听见神向你说话;并省察你对神话语的态度,趁着还听得见,珍惜它、遵行它。

祷告:说话的主,你警告说最可怕的饥荒,是听不见你话语的饥荒。我承认,我活在你的话唾手可得的时代,却常听而不闻、麻木厌倦,不知自己的灵正在饥荒中枯死。谢谢你的话成了肉身,就是基督。求你叫我趁着还听得见,饥渴地来听、来读、来遵行你的话,免得落在那无知无觉的饥荒里。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Amos declared a series of judgments to a prosperous yet unjust Israel. And among these judgments, there is one that is the most terrifying, and also the most unexpected. The famine people usually fear is a famine without food, without water; but what God declares here is a deeper, more fatal kind of famine.

“Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land — not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD” (Amos 8:11). This is a famine of “not being able to hear God’s word.” Consider how severe a punishment this is: God allows them, withdrawing his word — they will never again hear God speak to them. They will run to and fro, seeking the word of the LORD everywhere, but will not find it. When a person, an age, long despises and refuses to listen to God’s word, God will ultimately, according to what they wanted, withdraw his word, letting them fall into a terrifying desolation of “not hearing God.” And this famine is the most terrifying precisely because those in the midst of it often don’t feel themselves starving — they eat and drink as usual, stay busy as usual, “get along fine” as usual, without realizing their spirit is slowly withering to death in a famine of not hearing God.

This warning strikes especially close to home for us, living in an age where “God’s word is within easy reach, yet few truly listen.” How blessed we are: the Bible is right at hand, readable anytime; sermons, books, resources are countless. But do we treasure it, do we “listen” to it hungrily? A person who has long pushed God’s word to the side, hearing without heeding, having it without reading it, though the Bible sits right there on the shelf, may within be right in the midst of a famine of “not hearing God’s word” — not because God isn’t speaking, but because he has long since stopped listening, and can no longer take it in. When God’s word loses the weight it should have, when we’ve grown numb, weary, indifferent to it, the shadow of that spiritual famine has already quietly settled in.

The Lord Jesus said: “man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God” (Matthew 4:4). God’s word is the food of our spiritual life; without it, a person’s spirit must hunger, wither, die. And this word ultimately became flesh — “in the beginning was the Word... and the Word became flesh” (John 1:1, 14); if we come hungrily before Scripture, what we’re meant to be satisfied by, traced to its root, is Christ himself. So, while God’s word is still open to you now, while you can still hear it, don’t take it lightly, don’t let it gather dust. Like a hungry person throwing themselves at food, hungrily come to hear, to read, to obey God’s word; lest one day you fall into that most terrifying, yet most unnoticed, famine. Today, toward God’s word, are you hungry, or numb?

Meditation: Am I living in a condition where “God’s word is within easy reach, yet I hear without heeding”? Toward God’s word, am I hungry like a starving person throwing themselves at food, or numb, weary, indifferent? Am I currently in the midst of a famine of “not hearing God’s word,” yet utterly unaware of it because I’m eating, drinking, and staying busy as usual?

Application: Today, don’t take lightly the word of God so readily at hand; like a hungry person, hungrily read a passage of Scripture — not just seeking to “finish reading,” but longing to truly hear God speak to you through it; and examine your attitude toward God’s word, treasuring it and obeying it while you can still hear it.

Prayer: Lord who speaks, you warn that the most terrifying famine is a famine of not hearing your word. I confess I live in an age where your word is within easy reach, yet I often hear without heeding, numb and weary, unaware that my spirit is withering to death in famine. Thank you that your word became flesh, that is, Christ. Let me, while I can still hear, hungrily come to hear, to read, to obey your word, lest I fall into that unnoticed famine. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 你怎样待人,人必怎样待你
entries.title_en: As You Have Done, It Shall Be Done to You
entries.verse: 俄巴底亚书一章十五节
entries.content:
俄巴底亚书,是旧约中最短的一卷,只有一章,专门宣告神对以东的审判。以东,是以扫的后裔,与以色列(雅各的后裔)本是兄弟之邦。然而,当巴比伦攻打耶路撒冷、犹大遭难的时候,以东非但没有伸出援手,反倒站在一旁幸灾乐祸;他们甚至趁火打劫,抢夺犹大的财物,又拦截、交出那些逃难的人。他们在弟兄最落难的时候,落井下石。神看见了这一切,并宣告了审判的原则。

「耶和华降罚的日子临近万国。你怎样行,他也必照样向你行;你的报应必归到你头上。」(俄巴底亚书1:15)神所宣告的原则,朴素而严肃:「你怎样行,他也必照样向你行。」以东怎样冷酷地对待落难的弟兄——幸灾乐祸、趁火打劫、落井下石——神也必照样报应在他们头上。这是神公义的定律:我们怎样对待别人,尤其是怎样对待那些落难的、软弱的、无力还手的人,神都记着,也必按此报应。

而以东的罪,格外值得我们警醒,因为它是一种极隐蔽、极「不流血」的罪——幸灾乐祸。以东没有亲手杀人放火,他们「只是」在一旁看着弟兄落难,心里暗暗高兴,顺手占点便宜。我们很容易觉得这算不得什么大罪;可神却极其严肃地追讨它。因为幸灾乐祸,暴露的是一颗冷酷、缺乏怜悯、甚至以别人的痛苦为乐的心。当我们看见那与我们不和的人跌倒、那我们嫉妒的人失败、那得罪过我们的人遭难,心里若升起一丝暗暗的快意——那正是「以东式」的罪。它或许无人看见,神却看得一清二楚。

福音把我们引向一条与以东截然相反的路。主耶稣不但没有在我们这些悖逆之人落难时幸灾乐祸,反倒在我们还与祂为敌、还落在罪的绝境中时,主动来搭救我们、为我们舍命(罗5:8、10)。祂又教导我们:「你仇敌跌倒,你不要欢喜」(箴24:17);要「与喜乐的人要同乐;与哀哭的人要同哭」(罗12:15)。一个被这样的爱改变了的人,再也不能对别人的痛苦幸灾乐祸,反倒学会了怜悯、同情、甚至向仇敌施恩。今天,你心里是否藏着一丝「以东式」的幸灾乐祸——为某个人的跌倒、失败、遭难而暗暗快意?求神除去你心里这冷酷的根,赐你一颗怜悯的心。

默想:我心里是否藏着一种「以东式」的幸灾乐祸——当那与我不和的、我嫉妒的、得罪过我的人跌倒、失败、遭难时,心里暗暗升起一丝快意?我是否觉得这「不算什么大罪」,却不知神极其严肃地追讨它?「你怎样待人,人必怎样待你」如何警醒我?

应用:今天省察你对某个「你不喜欢、或曾亏待你」之人的心;若里面有幸灾乐祸的根,就向神认罪,求祂除去;并刻意操练「与哀哭的人同哭」——对一个正落难的人(哪怕是你不喜欢的),生出真实的怜悯,而非暗暗的快意。

祷告:公义又怜悯的主,以东在弟兄落难时幸灾乐祸、趁火打劫,你就宣告「你怎样行,他也必照样向你行」。我承认,我心里也常藏着这隐蔽的、以东式的幸灾乐祸,为别人的跌倒暗暗快意,还以为不算什么。谢谢主耶稣在我落难、与你为敌时,不但不幸灾乐祸,反倒为我舍命。求你除去我心里冷酷的根,赐我一颗怜悯、与人同哭的心。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Obadiah is the shortest book in the Old Testament, only one chapter, devoted entirely to declaring God’s judgment on Edom. Edom, descended from Esau, was, with Israel (descended from Jacob), originally a brother nation. Yet when Babylon attacked Jerusalem and Judah suffered calamity, Edom, far from lending a helping hand, instead stood by gloating over their misfortune; they even looted amid the chaos, plundering Judah’s wealth, and intercepted and handed over those fleeing for their lives. At their brother’s darkest hour, they kicked them while they were down. God saw all this, and declared the principle of judgment.

“For the day of the LORD is near upon all the nations. As you have done, it shall be done to you; your deeds shall return on your own head” (Obadiah 15). The principle God declares is plain, and solemn: “as you have done, it shall be done to you.” However coldly Edom treated their brother in distress — gloating, looting amid chaos, kicking them while they were down — God would do the same to them in return. This is God’s law of justice: however we treat others, especially those in distress, weak, unable to fight back, God remembers, and will surely repay accordingly.

And Edom’s sin deserves our special alertness, because it is an extremely hidden, extremely “bloodless” sin — gloating over another’s misfortune. Edom did not personally kill or burn; they “merely” stood by watching their brother’s calamity, secretly delighted, taking advantage where they could. We easily think this hardly counts as a serious sin; yet God pursues it with extreme solemnity. Because gloating over misfortune exposes a heart that is cold, lacking mercy, even delighting in others’ pain. When we see someone we’re at odds with stumble, someone we envy fail, someone who’s wronged us suffer calamity, and a flicker of secret delight rises in our hearts — that is exactly an “Edom-style” sin. No one may see it, but God sees it clearly.

The gospel leads us onto a road utterly opposite to Edom’s. The Lord Jesus, far from gloating over us rebels in our distress, instead, while we were still his enemies, still in the desperate straits of sin, actively came to rescue us, giving his life for us (Romans 5:8, 10). He also taught us: “do not rejoice when your enemy falls” (Proverbs 24:17); to “rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep” (Romans 12:15). A person changed by such love can no longer gloat over others’ pain — instead they learn mercy, compassion, even showing grace to enemies. Today, is there a flicker of “Edom-style” gloating hidden in your heart — secret delight over someone’s fall, failure, or calamity? Ask God to remove this cold root within you, and give you a heart of mercy.

Meditation: Is there an “Edom-style” gloating hidden in my heart — when someone I’m at odds with, envy, or who has wronged me stumbles, fails, or suffers calamity, does a flicker of secret delight rise within me? Do I think this “hardly counts as a serious sin,” not knowing God pursues it with extreme solemnity? How does “as you have done, it shall be done to you” awaken me?

Application: Today, examine your heart toward someone “you dislike, or who has once wronged you”; if there’s a root of gloating within, confess it to God, asking him to remove it; and deliberately practice “weeping with those who weep” — toward someone currently in distress (even someone you dislike), give rise to real compassion, rather than secret delight.

Prayer: Just and merciful Lord, Edom gloated over their brother’s calamity, looting amid chaos, and you declared “as you have done, it shall be done to you.” I confess there is also hidden within me this concealed, Edom-style gloating, secretly delighting in others’ falls, thinking it hardly matters. Thank you, Lord Jesus, that when I was in distress, at enmity with you, you did not gloat, but instead gave your life for me. Remove the cold root within my heart, and give me a heart of mercy, that weeps with others. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
