entries.title: 你们就是这些事的见证
entries.title_en: You Are Witnesses of These Things
entries.verse: 路加福音廿四章五节下至六节上、四十八至四十九节
entries.content:
妇女们清早带着香料来到坟墓,要膏抹一具尸体,天使却对她们说:「为什么在死人中找活人呢?他不在这里,已经复活了!」(路24:5-6)这句话像一记警钟。她们来时以为故事已经结束、只剩哀悼;殊不知,最大的转折刚刚发生——死亡被胜过了,坟墓是空的。

复活不是一则供人私下感动的美丽故事。耶稣对门徒说:「你们就是这些事的见证」(路24:48)。既然主真的复活了,这消息就必须被传出去。祂随即应许:「我要将我父所应许的降在你们身上……直到你们领受从上头来的能力」(路24:49)。见证的能力,不是靠门徒的口才或胆量,而是靠圣灵——但领受能力的目的,始终是为了「去作见证」。路加在他的第二卷书里,把这应许说得更具体:「圣灵降临在你们身上,你们就必得着能力,并要在耶路撒冷、犹太全地,和撒马利亚,直到地极,作我的见证」(徒1:8)——从空坟墓到地极,是同一条线。

这向我们发出扎心的一问:我们是否也常常「在死人中找活人」——把一位又真又活、掌管一切的主,活成了一段每周例行、与生活无关的宗教记忆?复活的主是活的,祂今天仍在动工。你若真信祂活着,就无法把这件事只藏在心里。求主用祂复活的大能充满你,再差你出去,作那位活主的见证。

默想:在我的实际生活中,耶稣更像一位「活着、掌权、正在动工」的主,还是一段与今天无关的宗教记忆?

应用:今天具体地向一个人分享一件「复活的主近来在你生命中做的事」,哪怕只是一句简短的见证。

祷告:复活的主,赦免我常把你活成一段遥远的记忆,忘了你今天仍然活着、仍在作工。求你用你复活的大能、用你所应许的圣灵充满我,叫我成为你又真又活的见证,从我所在的地方直到地极,把这胜过死亡的好消息带给身边的人。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The women came early with spices to anoint a body, but the angel said to them: "Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen!" (Luke 24:5-6). These words rang like an alarm bell. They came expecting the story was already over, with nothing left but mourning; little did they know, the greatest turning point had just happened — death had been overcome, the tomb was empty.

The resurrection is not a beautiful story meant merely for private inspiration. Jesus said to the disciples: "You are witnesses of these things" (Luke 24:48). Since the Lord has truly risen, this news must be carried out. He immediately promised: "I am sending the promise of my Father upon you... until you are clothed with power from on high" (Luke 24:49). The power to witness rests not on the disciples’ eloquence or courage, but on the Holy Spirit — yet the purpose of receiving that power was always "to go and bear witness." Luke, in his second volume, states this promise even more concretely: "you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth" (Acts 1:8) — from the empty tomb to the ends of the earth is one unbroken line.

This poses a piercing question to us: do we too often "seek the living among the dead" — turning a Lord who is truly alive and reigning over all into a weekly religious routine disconnected from life? The risen Lord is alive, and he is still at work today. If you truly believe he is alive, you cannot keep this locked away in your heart alone. Ask the Lord to fill you with the power of his resurrection, then send you out, to be a witness of that living Lord.

Meditation: In my actual life, is Jesus more like a Lord who is "alive, reigning, at work," or a religious memory disconnected from today?

Application: Today, share concretely with one person "something the risen Lord has recently done in your life," even if it’s just a brief testimony.

Prayer: Risen Lord, forgive me for often treating you as a distant memory, forgetting that you are still alive and still at work today. Fill me with the power of your resurrection and with the Spirit you promised, and make me a witness of you, truly alive, carrying this good news that has overcome death to those around me, from where I am to the ends of the earth. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 道成了肉身:神的生命进入人里面
entries.title_en: The Word Became Flesh: God's Life Enters Into Man
entries.verse: 约翰福音一章一至四节、十二节，三章十六节
entries.content:
约翰福音的开头把我们带回万有之先:「太初有道,道与神同在,道就是神……生命在他里头,这生命就是人的光」(约1:1-4)。这位创造万有的「道」,竟然「成了肉身,住在我们中间」(约1:14)。倪柝声常强调:基督徒信仰的核心,不只是一套要遵守的教训,更是一个「生命」——神的生命,藉着道成肉身的基督,进入了人的里面。

约翰接着说:「凡接待他的,就是信他名的人,他就赐他们权柄,作神的儿女」(约1:12)。作神的儿女,不是靠血气、不是靠人的努力修行,而是靠「接待」、「接受」这位赐生命的主。我们信主,不单是罪得赦免、地位改变,更是里面得着了一个新生命——那从神而来、能胜过罪与死的属天生命。

这就是三章十六节所讲的:神爱世人,把独生子赐给我们,叫一切信祂的「得永生」。永生不只是将来在天上的年日,更是现在就能拥有的那一位「生命之主」的同在。保罗后来把这真理说得斩钉截铁:「基督是我们的生命,他显现的时候,你们也要与他一同显现在荣耀里」(西3:4)——不是「基督给我们生命」,而是「基督是我们的生命」,这正是倪柝声一生反复述说的核心。

今天,你不必靠咬牙苦撑来讨神喜悦;你要学的,是不断回到那位住在你里面的主,支取祂的生命,让祂的生命从你里面活出来。

默想:我是把信仰当作一套「要努力遵守的规条」,还是当作「里面一个要支取、要活出的新生命」?这两者会带来怎样不同的生活?

应用:今天遇到一件靠自己「过不去」的事(一个软弱、一次坏脾气)时,不再单靠意志硬撑,而是安静地转向住在你里面的主,求祂的生命顶替你的无能。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你道成肉身,把神的生命带进我里面,又赐我权柄作神的儿女。你是我的生命,不只是给我生命的那一位。求你叫我不再只靠自己的努力来信你,而是每天回到你面前,支取你的生命。愿你的生命在我里面长大,从我这必朽的身体里活出来。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The opening of John’s Gospel takes us back before all things: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... In him was life, and the life was the light of men" (John 1:1-4). This "Word," who created all things, actually "became flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14). Watchman Nee often emphasized: the core of the Christian faith is not merely a set of teachings to keep, but a "life" — God’s life, entering into man through the incarnate Christ.

John goes on to say: "to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God" (John 1:12). Becoming children of God is not by blood, not by human effort or self-cultivation, but by "receiving," by "welcoming" this life-giving Lord. Our faith in the Lord is not merely sins forgiven and status changed, but an inner reception of a new life — that heavenly life, from God, able to overcome sin and death.

This is exactly what 3:16 speaks of: God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him would "have eternal life." Eternal life is not merely future days in heaven, but the present possession of the presence of that "Lord of life." Paul later stated this truth with utter certainty: "Christ is our life, and when he appears, you also will appear with him in glory" (Colossians 3:4) — not "Christ gives us life," but "Christ is our life," and this is exactly the core Watchman Nee spoke of again and again throughout his life.

Today, you don’t need to grit your teeth to please God; what you need to learn is to keep returning to the Lord who dwells within you, drawing on his life, letting his life live itself out from within you.

Meditation: Do I treat faith as a set of "rules to strive to keep," or as "a new life within me to draw on and live out"? What different kind of life would each of these produce?

Application: Today, when you meet something you "can’t get past" on your own (a weakness, a burst of temper), don’t grit your teeth and force it alone — instead quietly turn to the Lord who dwells within you, and ask his life to replace your inability.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for becoming flesh, bringing God’s life into me, and giving me the right to become a child of God. You are my life, not merely the one who gives me life. Let me stop trying to believe in you only through my own effort, but return to you every day, drawing on your life. Let your life grow within me, and live itself out through this perishable body of mine. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 生命的粮:唯有祂能真正喂饱你
entries.title_en: The Bread of Life: Only He Can Truly Satisfy You
entries.verse: 约翰福音六章卅五节
entries.content:
耶稣刚用五饼二鱼喂饱了五千人,众人第二天又来找祂——但耶稣看穿了他们的心:他们找祂,是「因吃饼得饱」(约6:26),要的是肚腹的满足,而非那赐粮的主。于是祂把他们的眼光引向更深处:「我就是生命的粮。到我这里来的,必定不饿;信我的,永远不渴」(约6:35)。

耶稣在此触及人心最深的饥渴。我们里面有一个胃口,是任何食物、成就、感情、娱乐都填不满的——因为它本是为神而造的。以赛亚早就发出同样的诘问:「你们为何花钱买那不足为食物的?用劳碌得来的买那不使人饱足的呢?」(赛55:2)我们一生却常常拿着「饼」当作终点,以为多赚一点、多拥有一点、多成就一点,就能饱足;结果吃了还饿,喝了还渴。耶稣说,问题不在于你吃得不够多,而在于你找错了粮。

「到我这里来的,必定不饿」——祂不是说信祂就没有任何需要,而是说唯有祂能满足那最深的饥渴。这正是福音的邀请:神造你,不是要你在受造之物里东拼西凑地找满足,而是要你在祂里面得着那永不再饿、永不再渴的丰盛。今天,与其继续追逐一块又一块填不饱的饼,不如来到生命的粮面前,让祂喂养你的灵魂。

默想:我最近一直在追逐哪一块「饼」,指望它让我满足?它真的喂饱我了吗,还是吃了还饿?

应用:今天刻意用十分钟,不为求什么、单单来到主面前默想祂、以祂为满足,操练「到生命的粮这里来」。

祷告:主啊,你是生命的粮。赦免我常常拿着填不饱的饼当作满足,用劳碌买那不使人饱足的,吃了还饿、喝了还渴。求你叫我看见,唯有你能喂饱我灵魂最深的饥渴。今天我来到你面前,不为别的,单单要你自己作我永远的饱足。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Jesus had just fed five thousand with five loaves and two fish, and the crowd came looking for him again the next day — but Jesus saw through their hearts: they sought him "because you ate the loaves and had your fill" (John 6:26), wanting the satisfaction of their stomachs, not the Lord who gave the bread. So he turned their eyes to something deeper: "I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst" (John 6:35).

Here Jesus touches the deepest hunger of the human heart. There is an appetite within us that no food, achievement, relationship, or entertainment can fill — because it was made for God himself. Isaiah long ago raised the same question: "Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy?" (Isaiah 55:2) Yet we spend our lives treating "bread" as the destination, thinking that earning a little more, owning a little more, achieving a little more will satisfy us; yet we eat and are still hungry, drink and are still thirsty. Jesus says the problem isn’t that you haven’t eaten enough — it’s that you’ve been looking for the wrong bread.

"Whoever comes to me shall not hunger" — he is not saying that believing in him removes every need, but that only he can satisfy that deepest hunger. This is exactly the invitation of the gospel: God did not create you to scrape together satisfaction from created things, but to find in him the fullness that never hungers, never thirsts again. Today, rather than continuing to chase after one unsatisfying loaf after another, come before the bread of life, and let him feed your soul.

Meditation: Which "loaf" have I been chasing lately, hoping it would satisfy me? Has it truly fed me, or have I eaten it and remained hungry?

Application: Today, set aside ten minutes deliberately not to ask for anything, but simply to come before the Lord, meditate on him, and be satisfied in him — practicing "coming to the bread of life."

Prayer: Lord, you are the bread of life. Forgive me for so often treating unsatisfying bread as satisfaction, spending my labor on what does not satisfy, eating and remaining hungry, drinking and remaining thirsty. Let me see that only you can feed the deepest hunger of my soul. Today I come before you, for nothing else, only wanting you yourself to be my everlasting satisfaction. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 世界的光,叫你得真自由
entries.title_en: The Light of the World, Who Sets You Truly Free
entries.verse: 约翰福音八章十二节，约翰福音八章卅二节
entries.content:
耶稣宣告:「我是世界的光。跟从我的,就不在黑暗里走,必要得着生命的光」(约8:12)。在同一段,祂又说:「你们必晓得真理,真理必叫你们得以自由」(约8:32)。光与自由,是约翰福音第八至十一章反复出现的主题——祂使瞎眼的看见、使被罪捆绑的得释放,甚至叫已死的拉撒路从坟墓里出来。

当时听众的反应很有意思:他们说「我们是亚伯拉罕的后裔,从来没有作过谁的奴仆」,不肯承认自己需要被释放。这正是人的光景——我们常以为自己是自由的,其实早被许多看不见的东西捆住:被别人的评价捆住、被过去的失败捆住、被非满足不可的欲望捆住。耶稣说,唯有真理、唯有祂自己,能把人从这些黑暗里领出来。

值得注意的是,真自由不是「没有任何约束、爱做什么就做什么」。一条鱼「自由地」离开水,只会死;它真正的自由,是留在那使它得生命的水里。同样,人真正的自由,是回到那位造我们、爱我们的主面前,活在祂的光中。约翰在异象的末了,看见这光终极的归宿:那城「不用日月光照,因有神的荣耀光照,又有羔羊为城的灯」(启21:23)。今天跟从这世界的光,正是走向那座光源永不熄灭的城。

默想:我自以为自由,实际上却被什么悄悄捆住——他人的看法?过去的阴影?某个放不下的欲望?

应用:把一样长期捆绑你的东西带到主面前,今天用祂的真理(一节相关的经文)来对付那黑暗里的谎言。

祷告:主啊,你是世界的光,也是叫我得自由的真理。求你光照我里面自以为自由、其实被捆绑的地方。用你的真理释放我,叫我不再在黑暗里摸索乱走,而是跟从你,走在通向那光源永不熄灭之城的路上,得着那唯有你能赐的真自由。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Jesus declared: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life" (John 8:12). In the same passage he also said: "you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free" (John 8:32). Light and freedom are themes that recur throughout John 8–11 — he gives sight to the blind, releases those bound by sin, and even calls the already-dead Lazarus out of the tomb.

The listeners’ reaction at the time is worth noting: they said "we are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone," unwilling to admit they needed to be set free. This is exactly the human condition — we often think ourselves free, when we’re already bound by many invisible things: bound by others’ opinions, bound by past failures, bound by desires that demand satisfaction. Jesus says only the truth, only he himself, can lead a person out of this darkness.

It’s worth noting that true freedom is not "no restraint at all, do whatever you please." A fish that "freely" leaves the water only dies; its true freedom is to remain in the water that gives it life. Likewise, true human freedom is returning to the Lord who made us and loves us, living in his light. John, at the very end of his vision, saw the ultimate destination of this light: that city "has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb" (Revelation 21:23). To follow the light of the world today is exactly to walk toward that city whose light source never goes out.

Meditation: I think myself free, but what am I actually quietly bound by — others’ opinions? shadows of the past? some desire I can’t let go of?

Application: Bring one thing that has long bound you before the Lord, and today use his truth (one relevant verse) to confront the lie in that darkness.

Prayer: Lord, you are the light of the world, and also the truth that sets me free. Shine your light on the places within me where I think myself free, but am actually bound. Free me with your truth, so that I no longer grope around in darkness, but follow you, walking the road toward that city whose light source never goes out, gaining the true freedom that only you can give. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 安息与更新
entries.title_en: Rest and Renewal
entries.content:
安息与更新

「你们得救在乎归回安息;你们得力在乎平静安稳。」(以赛亚书 30:15)

倪柝声提醒我们:真正的安息不是停止做工,而是停止倚靠自己。我们劳碌,常是因为里面那个「非我不可、非做不可」的自己从未歇下。归回安息,就是把重担卸给那位已经为我们成就一切的主。

今天,让身体歇下,更让里面那颗紧绷、想要掌控一切的心歇下。安静在主面前,不必挣扎、不必表现,单单让祂的爱重新更新你。

"In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength." (Isaiah 30:15) True rest is ceasing to rely on yourself.
entries.content_en:
Rest and Renewal

"In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength." (Isaiah 30:15)

Watchman Nee reminds us: true rest is not ceasing to work, but ceasing to rely on ourselves. We labor, often because that inner self who insists "it must be me, I must do it" never lays itself down. Returning to rest means handing our burdens over to the Lord who has already accomplished everything for us.

Today, let your body rest, and even more, let that tense, controlling heart within you rest. Be still before the Lord — no need to strive, no need to perform — simply let his love renew you afresh.

"In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength." (Isaiah 30:15) True rest is ceasing to rely on yourself.

entries.title: 我就是道路、真理、生命
entries.title_en: I Am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life
entries.verse: 约翰福音十四章六节，十三章卅四至卅五节
entries.content:
耶稣要离世前,门徒忧愁。祂说:「你们心里不要忧愁……我去原是为你们预备地方去。」多马问:「主啊,我们不知道你往哪里去,怎么知道那条路呢?」耶稣答:「我就是道路、真理、生命;若不藉着我,没有人能到父那里去」(约14:6)。

请注意,耶稣没有说祂指出一条路、教导一套真理、提供一种生命——祂说祂「就是」。基督信仰的核心不是一套原则或一份人生指南,而是一位位格。得着祂,就得着了通往父的路本身。这句话在今天听来「排他」,却也是天大的好消息:通往神的路不必你去摸索、去挣得,神已经亲自成了那条路,向你走来。

而这位「从最高来到最低」的神子,就在同一夜俯身为门徒洗脚,并留下新命令:「我赐给你们一条新命令,乃是叫你们彼此相爱;我怎样爱你们,你们也要怎样相爱」(约13:34)。认识这条又真又活的道路,不是停在头脑的认信,而是走上一条彼此相爱、俯身服事的路——因为那正是祂自己所走的路。

默想:我是把耶稣当作众多人生选项中的一个「帮助」,还是当作通往神、通往生命唯一的那一位?

应用:今天在一个具体的选择上,不问「怎样对我最有利」,而问「跟随这位道路、真理、生命的主,会怎样行」。

祷告:主耶稣,你就是道路、真理、生命。谢谢你亲自成为我到父那里的路,是我无法自己挣得的。求你叫我不只在头脑里认识你,更走上你所走的路——彼此相爱、俯身服事。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
As Jesus was about to leave the world, the disciples grew sorrowful. He said: "Let not your hearts be troubled... I go to prepare a place for you." Thomas asked: "Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?" Jesus answered: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me" (John 14:6).

Notice, Jesus did not say he points out a way, teaches a set of truths, or provides a kind of life — he said he "is." The core of the Christian faith is not a set of principles or a life guide, but a person. To have him is to have the very road to the Father. This sentence sounds "exclusive" to modern ears, yet it is also tremendously good news: the road to God does not need to be groped out or earned by you — God has personally become that road, walking toward you.

And this Son of God, who "came from the highest to the lowest," on that very same night, stooped down to wash the disciples’ feet, and left a new command: "A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another" (John 13:34). To know this true and living way is not to stop at intellectual assent, but to walk a road of loving one another, of stooping to serve — because that is exactly the road he himself walked.

Meditation: Do I treat Jesus as one "help" among many life options, or as the one and only way to God, to life?

Application: Today, in one concrete decision, don’t ask "what benefits me most," but ask "what would following this Lord who is the way, the truth, and the life look like here?"

Prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the way, and the truth, and the life. Thank you for personally becoming my road to the Father, a road I could never have earned myself. Let me not only know you intellectually, but walk the road you walked — loving one another, stooping to serve. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 你们要常在我里面
entries.title_en: Abide in Me
entries.verse: 约翰福音十六章卅三节
entries.content:
耶稣用葡萄树的比喻,讲出属灵生命的秘诀:「你们要常在我里面,我也常在你们里面。枝子若不常在葡萄树上,自己就不能结果子;你们若不常在我里面,也是这样」(约15:4)。倪柝声常提醒我们:基督徒的难处,往往在于想「为主」结果子,却忘了唯一的路是「在主里面」。

枝子结果子,从不是靠使劲、靠挣扎,而是靠与树连结、让树的生命自然流通。同样,爱心、忍耐、圣洁,不是我们咬牙挤出来的,而是当我们住在基督里,祂的生命从我们里面自然生发出来的。「离了我,你们就不能做什么」——不是不能做「大事」,而是什么真正属灵的果子都结不出来。

这份「在里面」的联合,主在临别的祷告里说得更深:「使他们都合而为一,正如你父在我里面,我在你里面,使他们也在我们里面,叫世人可以信你差了我来」(约17:21)。这不是说我们与父、子同享同一位格的合一,而是主照着祂与父那不可分的合一为样式,求父使门徒也被接入与父、子的团契、彼此相爱合一,好叫世人因此认出差祂来的正是父。「常在我里面」原来指向这样深的呼召——不是独自与主连结而已,更是被接入这场以叫世人相信为目的的合一。

所以主临别时应许:「在世上你们有苦难;但你们可以放心,我已经胜了世界」(约16:33)。平安不在于环境无风无浪,而在于那位已经得胜的主住在我们里面。今天最要紧的,不是更努力,而是更亲近——回到主里面,安息在祂里面,让祂活出祂自己。

默想:我最近是在「为主」拼命,还是在「主里面」安息?我的果子,是硬挤出来的,还是从与祂的连结里流出来的?

应用:今天刻意安排几段短短的「回到主里面」的时刻,哪怕只是一两分钟,把心思重新连于祂,而非只顾往前冲。

祷告:主啊,赦免我常想「为你」做工,却忘了「在你里面」。求你叫我像枝子连于葡萄树一样,时刻住在你里面,进入你与父那合而为一的团契,让你的生命在我里面自然结出果子。在苦难中,叫我因你已得胜而放心。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Using the parable of the vine, Jesus spoke the secret of the spiritual life: "Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in me" (John 15:4). Watchman Nee often reminds us: a Christian’s difficulty is often wanting to bear fruit "for the Lord," while forgetting that the only way is to be "in the Lord."

A branch never bears fruit by straining or struggling, but by being connected to the tree, letting the tree’s life naturally flow through it. Likewise, love, patience, and holiness are not things we grit our teeth and squeeze out, but things that naturally spring up from within us as we abide in Christ, as his life flows out. "Apart from me you can do nothing" — not that we cannot do "great things," but that we cannot bear any truly spiritual fruit at all.

This union of "abiding in" is stated even more deeply in the Lord’s farewell prayer: "that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me" (John 17:21). This does not mean we share the same personal oneness the Father and Son share, but that the Lord, patterned after his own unbreakable unity with the Father, asks the Father to bring the disciples too into fellowship with the Father and Son, united in love with one another, so that the world would recognize by this that it was the Father who sent him. "Abiding in me" points to a calling this deep — not merely being connected to the Lord alone, but being brought into this union whose very purpose is that the world would believe.

So the Lord, at his parting, promises: "In the world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world" (John 16:33). Peace does not lie in circumstances free of storms, but in the fact that the Lord who has already overcome dwells within us. What matters most today is not trying harder, but drawing nearer — returning into the Lord, resting in him, letting him live himself out.

Meditation: Have I lately been striving desperately "for the Lord," or resting "in the Lord"? Is my fruit forced out by effort, or flowing out from my connection with him?

Application: Deliberately arrange a few short "returning into the Lord" moments today, even just a minute or two, reconnecting your mind to him rather than only rushing forward.

Prayer: Lord, forgive me for often thinking of working "for you," while forgetting to be "in you." Let me, like a branch connected to the vine, abide in you at all times, entering into that fellowship of oneness you share with the Father, letting your life naturally bear fruit within me. In tribulation, let me take heart because you have already overcome. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 这些事记下来,是要叫你们信
entries.title_en: These Things Are Written So That You May Believe
entries.verse: 约翰福音二十章卅一节
entries.content:
约翰在记述了耶稣的受难与复活后,道出他写这卷福音书的目的:「但记这些事,要叫你们信耶稣是基督,是神的儿子,并且叫你们信了他,就可以因他的名得生命」(约20:31)。整卷书所拣选记载的神迹,不是为满足人的好奇,而是要指向一个信仰的决断:耶稣是谁。

值得注意的是多马的经历。他起初不信,直到亲眼看见、亲手摸了主的伤痕,才呼喊「我的主!我的神!」耶稣却说:「你因看见了我才信;那没有看见就信的有福了」(约20:29)。我们这些没有亲眼见过的人,凭什么信?正是凭着这卷被圣灵默示、可靠地记载下来的见证。信心不是盲目的一跃,而是建立在神所启示、可信的话语之上。

保罗后来对提摩太说得更全面:「圣经都是神所默示的,于教训、督责、使人归正、教导人学义都是有益的」(提后3:16)。约翰福音不是孤例——它和全本圣经一样,是神呼出的话,值得我们把信心的全部重量都放上去。

这提醒我们:圣经不是一本任人取用的心灵鸡汤,而是神为要叫人「信而得生命」所存留的见证。我们读经的目的,始终不只是获取知识,而是被带到一个抉择前——信这位基督、神的儿子,并因祂的名得生命。

默想:我读圣经,是把它当作参考资料,还是当作那要引我信主、得生命的神的话?我的信,是建立在感觉上,还是建立在神可靠的话语上?

应用:今天带着「这是要叫我信、叫我得生命」的心读一段经文,读完后具体回应:这段话要我信什么、行什么?

祷告:主啊,谢谢你藉着可信、被你默示的话语,把你儿子的真相留给了我。求你坚固我的信心,不建立在飘忽的感觉上,而扎根在你的话语上。叫我因信你的名,天天支取那真正的生命。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
After recounting Jesus’s suffering and resurrection, John states the purpose for which he wrote this Gospel: "but these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name" (John 20:31). Every miracle this whole book selects to record was not to satisfy human curiosity, but to point toward a decision of faith: who is Jesus.

Thomas’s experience is worth noting. He did not believe at first, not until he saw with his own eyes and touched the Lord’s wounds with his own hands, that he cried out "My Lord and my God!" Jesus said to him: "Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed" (John 20:29). We who have not seen with our own eyes — on what basis do we believe? Precisely on this reliable, Spirit-inspired testimony recorded here. Faith is not a blind leap, but is built on God’s revealed, trustworthy word.

Paul later put it more fully to Timothy: "All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness" (2 Timothy 3:16). John’s Gospel is not an isolated case — it is, like the whole of Scripture, God’s breathed-out word, worthy of the full weight of our faith.

This reminds us: Scripture is not a spiritual self-help book for us to pick and choose from at will, but the testimony God has preserved so that people would "believe and have life." The purpose of our Bible reading is never merely to gain knowledge, but to be brought before a decision — to believe this Christ, the Son of God, and to have life through his name.

Meditation: Do I treat the Bible as a reference book, or as God’s word meant to lead me to faith, to life? Is my faith built on feeling, or on God’s reliable word?

Application: Today, read a passage with the mindset "this is meant to lead me to believe, to have life," and after reading, concretely respond: what does this passage ask me to believe, to do?

Prayer: Lord, thank you for leaving me the truth about your Son through your reliable, inspired word. Strengthen my faith, not built on shifting feelings, but rooted in your word. Let me, by believing in your name, daily draw on that true life. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 一心一意的教会
entries.title_en: A Church of One Heart and Mind
entries.verse: 使徒行传四章十二、卅二节
entries.content:
五旬节圣灵降临后,教会诞生了。路加这样描写初期教会:「那许多信的人都是一心一意的,没有一人说他的东西有一样是自己的,都是大家公用」(徒4:32)。与此同时,彼得在公会前放胆宣告:「除他以外,别无拯救;因为在天下人间,没有赐下别的名,我们可以靠着得救」(徒4:12)。

这是一群被复活的主彻底改变的人。他们对耶稣的确信如此真实——「别无拯救」——以致这确信自然流溢成一种全新的生活方式:「都恒心遵守使徒的教训,彼此交接,擘饼,祈祷」(徒2:42),财物彼此分享、需要彼此担当。他们不是被规条逼着这样做,而是被同一位主的爱融化,再也无法只顾自己。

保罗后来用身体作比方,道出这「一心一意」的深层逻辑:「若一个肢体受苦,所有的肢体就一同受苦;若一个肢体得荣耀,所有的肢体就一同快乐」(林前12:26)。初代教会的彼此相顾,不是一时的热情,而是活出了「我们同属一个身体」这一福音的事实。

对照今天的我们,常常信仰归信仰、钱包归钱包、生活照旧。但初期教会提醒我们:真正相信「唯有基督能救」的人,不可能仍旧紧抓自己的东西、活在自己的小圈子里。福音一旦真进到心里,就会动到我们的时间、金钱和关系。求主让我们的信,不只停在口里,也活在彼此相爱、彼此分享的团契里。

默想:我的信仰,有没有真正动到我的钱包、时间和生活方式?还是它被安全地锁在「宗教」的格子里,与其余的我无关?

应用:这周主动为教会或身边一位弟兄姊妹的实际需要,摆上一样「本来属于自己」的东西——时间、金钱或款待。

祷告:主啊,你是天下人间唯一的拯救。求你叫我对你的信,不只停在嘴上,而是像初期教会那样,融化我的自我,叫我甘心与弟兄姊妹一心一意、彼此相爱、彼此分享,因我们本是一个身体。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
After the Holy Spirit descended at Pentecost, the church was born. Luke describes the early church this way: "Now the full number of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things that belonged to him was his own, but they had everything in common" (Acts 4:32). At the same time, Peter boldly proclaimed before the council: "there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved" (Acts 4:12).

This was a group of people utterly transformed by the risen Lord. Their conviction about Jesus was so real — "no other salvation" — that this conviction naturally overflowed into an entirely new way of life: "they devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers" (Acts 2:42), sharing possessions with one another, bearing one another’s needs. They weren’t forced into this by rules — they were melted by the love of that one Lord, no longer able to think only of themselves.

Paul later used the metaphor of the body to state the deep logic behind this "one heart and mind": "if one member suffers, all suffer together; if one member is honored, all rejoice together" (1 Corinthians 12:26). The mutual care of the early church was not a passing burst of enthusiasm, but the living out of the gospel fact that "we belong to one body."

In contrast, we today often keep faith as faith, wallet as wallet, life going on as usual. But the early church reminds us: those who truly believe "Christ alone saves" cannot possibly keep clutching their own possessions, living within their own small circle. Once the gospel truly enters the heart, it moves our time, our money, our relationships. May the Lord let our faith not stop at our lips, but live itself out in a fellowship of mutual love and mutual sharing.

Meditation: Has my faith actually moved my wallet, my time, and my way of life? Or is it safely locked away in a "religious" compartment, unrelated to the rest of me?

Application: This week, proactively give something "that originally belonged to you" — time, money, or hospitality — toward a concrete need of the church or a brother or sister around you.

Prayer: Lord, you are the only salvation under heaven. Let my faith in you not stop at my lips, but, like the early church, melt my self, making me willing to be of one heart and mind with my brothers and sisters, loving and sharing with one another, for we truly are one body. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 顺从神,不顺从人
entries.title_en: We Must Obey God Rather Than Men
entries.verse: 使徒行传五章廿九节
entries.content:
使徒们因传扬耶稣复活,被公会拿住、下在监里,又被严严地禁止再奉这名教导人。彼得和众使徒的回答斩钉截铁:「顺从神,不顺从人,是应当的」(徒5:29)。这不是叛逆权柄的口号,而是当人的命令与神的命令正面冲突时,信徒清醒而坚定的抉择。

请注意他们所付的代价:被鞭打之后,他们「心里欢喜,因被算是配为这名受辱」(徒5:41)。他们不是不知道后果,而是心里有一个更高的权柄和更深的喜乐,使他们不再被人的威吓所辖制。当一个人真正敬畏神过于惧怕人,人的恐吓就失去了挟制他的力量。

这原则很快就被推到了极处。同一卷书稍后记载,司提反被石头打死时,呼喊:「求主耶稣接收我的灵魂!……主啊,不要将这罪归于他们!」(徒7:59-60)这几乎是主耶稣在十字架上所说之话的回声。彼得等人「欢喜受辱」,司提反则以性命印证了「顺从神,不顺从人」——这条路的尽头,不是自义的悲壮,而是效法基督、以恩慈待逼迫者的心。

今天我们未必面对牢狱,却天天面对更隐蔽的压力:随波逐流、避免尴尬、不愿得罪人。这些时候,同样的原则仍然适用——神的话若在一件事上说了「是」,我们就不该因怕人而说「不」。真正的忠诚,是在无人喝彩、甚至要付代价时,仍选择顺从神。

默想:在我的生活中,「怕得罪人」最常在哪些地方让我妥协、违背我明知是神心意的事?

应用:找出一件你一直因怕人而回避的顺服(一句该说的真话、一个该守的界线),今天选择顺从神。

祷告:主啊,你配得我至高的忠诚。求你除去我对人的惧怕,叫我敬畏你过于惧怕人。当人的期待与你的话冲突时,给我勇气顺从你,哪怕要付上代价,也以能为你的名受辱为喜乐,像司提反那样,以恩慈回应逼迫我的人。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The apostles were seized by the council for proclaiming Jesus’s resurrection, thrown into prison, and strictly forbidden to teach in this name again. Peter and the apostles’ answer was unwavering: "We must obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29). This was not a slogan of rebellion against authority, but the clear-eyed, firm decision of believers when human commands directly collide with God’s command.

Notice the price they paid: after being beaten, they left the council "rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the name" (Acts 5:41). It’s not that they didn’t know the consequences — they had within them a higher authority and a deeper joy, which freed them from being controlled by human threats. When a person truly fears God more than he fears man, man’s intimidation loses its power to control him.

This principle was quickly pushed to its furthest extreme. Later in the same book, as Stephen was being stoned to death, he cried out: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!... Lord, do not hold this sin against them!" (Acts 7:59-60) This is almost an echo of what the Lord Jesus himself said on the cross. Peter and the others "rejoiced in dishonor"; Stephen sealed "obey God rather than men" with his very life — and the end of this road is not the tragic grandeur of self-righteousness, but the imitation of Christ, responding to persecutors with grace.

Today we may not face prison, but we face subtler pressures every day: going along with the crowd, avoiding awkwardness, being unwilling to offend. In these moments, the same principle still applies — if God’s word has said "yes" to something, we should not say "no" out of fear of man. True loyalty is choosing to obey God even when no one applauds, even at a cost.

Meditation: In my life, where does "fear of offending people" most often make me compromise, going against what I clearly know is God’s will?

Application: Identify one act of obedience you’ve been avoiding out of fear of man (a true word that needs saying, a boundary that needs holding), and today choose to obey God.

Prayer: Lord, you deserve my highest loyalty. Remove my fear of man, and let me fear you more than I fear man. When human expectations collide with your word, give me courage to obey you, even at a cost, counting it joy to be dishonored for your name, like Stephen, responding to those who persecute me with grace. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 患难中四散,福音却传开
entries.title_en: Scattered by Persecution, Yet the Gospel Spread
entries.verse: 使徒行传八章一、四、七、八节
entries.content:
司提反殉道后,「耶路撒冷的教会大遭逼迫」,门徒分散到各处。表面看,这是一场灾难。然而路加接着说:「那些分散的人往各处去传道」(徒8:4)。腓利下到撒马利亚城传扬基督,神迹随着,「在那城里,就大有欢喜」(徒8:8)。神竟用逼迫的风,把福音的种子吹到更远的地方。

这让我们看见神奇妙的主权:祂能叫万事——包括痛苦和逼迫——互相效力,成就祂福音广传的旨意。门徒并没有等到处境改善才传道,他们是在被打散、在颠沛流离中,一路走一路传。神国的扩展,常常不是经由顺境的大道,而是经由苦难所开的窄门。

保罗后来在自己的捆锁里,也见证了同一个原则:「我所遭遇的事更是叫福音兴旺,以致我受的捆锁在御营全军和其余的人中,已经显明是为基督的缘故」(腓1:12-13)。从耶路撒冷的四散,到保罗在罗马的监牢,神一次又一次地证明:祂手中没有一样苦难是白费的。

这对正在患难中的我们是极大的安慰,也是挑战。你此刻所受的挫折、被迫离开的处境、不得已的改变,在神手中都可能成为福音临到新地方、新人群的通道。求主给我们信心,不把苦难只当作损失,而是留心:主在这被打散的处境里,要藉着我传扬什么?

默想:我是否只把患难当作要赶快脱离的麻烦?神会不会正藉着我目前的难处,把我摆在一个能为祂作见证的新位置上?

应用:在你目前的一个难处中,求主给你一双「福音的眼睛」,看见祂可能藉此要你接触、祝福的一个人。

祷告:主啊,你能使万事互相效力,连逼迫与患难都成为福音广传的通道,正如你叫保罗的捆锁显明是为基督的缘故。求你叫我在难处中不只顾着脱身,而是看见你的手,忠心地在你所摆我去的地方传扬你,叫那里也大有欢喜。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
After Stephen’s martyrdom, "a great persecution arose against the church in Jerusalem," and the disciples were scattered to various places. On the surface, this looked like a disaster. Yet Luke goes on to say: "those who were scattered went about preaching the word" (Acts 8:4). Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed Christ, and miracles followed, and "there was much joy in that city" (Acts 8:8). God actually used the wind of persecution to blow the seed of the gospel further afield.

This lets us see God’s wondrous sovereignty: he can make all things — including pain and persecution — work together to accomplish his purpose of spreading the gospel. The disciples did not wait for circumstances to improve before preaching; scattered, uprooted, they preached as they went. The expansion of God’s kingdom often does not come through the broad road of favorable circumstances, but through the narrow gate opened by suffering.

Paul later, in his own chains, bore witness to this same principle: "what has happened to me has really served to advance the gospel, so that it has become known throughout the whole imperial guard and to all the rest that my imprisonment is for Christ" (Philippians 1:12-13). From the scattering in Jerusalem to Paul’s imprisonment in Rome, God proved again and again: not a single hardship in his hand is ever wasted.

This is a great comfort, and a great challenge, to us in our own hardships. The setback you’re facing right now, the situation you were forced to leave, the change you didn’t choose — in God’s hand these may all become channels through which the gospel reaches new places, new people. May the Lord give us faith not to see hardship only as loss, but to pay attention: what might the Lord want to proclaim through me in this scattered place?

Meditation: Do I only treat hardship as trouble to escape as quickly as possible? Might God be using my current difficulty to place me in a new position to bear witness for him?

Application: In one of your current difficulties, ask the Lord to give you "gospel eyes," to see one person he might want you to reach and bless through it.

Prayer: Lord, you can make all things work together, even persecution and hardship becoming channels for the gospel’s spread, just as you made Paul’s imprisonment known to be for Christ’s sake. Let me, in difficulty, not only seek to escape, but see your hand, faithfully proclaiming you in the place you have set me, so that there too, there would be much joy. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 记念神的创造
entries.title_en: Remembering God's Creation
entries.content:
记念神的创造

「诸天述说神的荣耀;穹苍传扬他的手段。」(诗篇 19:1)

安息日不仅是停下工作,更是抬起头来,重新看见那位创造万有的神。祂造了这一切,不是要我们只顾使用,而是要我们透过受造之物,惊叹并敬拜那位赐下这一切的主。

今天,走到户外,看一看天空、树木、阳光。让每一样受造之物,都成为把你的心引向创造主、以祂为乐的邀请。

"The heavens declare the glory of God." (Psalm 19:1) Let creation lift your eyes to the Creator, and turn wonder into worship.
entries.content_en:
Remembering God's Creation

"The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork." (Psalm 19:1)

The Sabbath is not only a ceasing from work, but a lifting up of your eyes, seeing afresh the God who created all things. He made all of this not merely for us to use, but so that, through creation, we would marvel at and worship the Lord who gave it all.

Today, go outside, and look at the sky, the trees, the sunlight. Let every created thing become an invitation drawing your heart toward the Creator, delighting in him.

"The heavens declare the glory of God." (Psalm 19:1) Let creation lift your eyes to the Creator, and turn wonder into worship.

entries.title: 靠这人,罪得赦免、得称为义
entries.title_en: Through This Man Forgiveness of Sins Is Proclaimed, and Justification Is Given
entries.scripture: 徒十三至十五章卅五节
entries.verse: 使徒行传十三章卅八、卅九节
entries.content:
保罗第一次宣教旅程,在彼西底的安提阿会堂里,把福音的核心讲得清清楚楚:「所以弟兄们,你们当晓得:赦罪的道是由这人传给你们的。你们靠摩西的律法,在一切不得称义的事上信靠这人,就都得称义了」(徒13:38-39)。

这两节把两条路摆在人面前。一条是「靠律法称义」——靠自己努力守全律法、做够好,来换取神的接纳;但保罗说,这条路在「一切不得称义的事上」都行不通,因为没有人能守全。另一条是「信靠这人」——就是信靠耶稣基督,凭祂所成就的,白白得称为义。称义不是奖赏,而是恩典;不是靠行为赚来的工价,而是靠信心领受的礼物。

保罗日后在罗马书里,把这在安提阿会堂初次宣讲的真理,发展成整卷书信的骨干:「我们看定了:人称义是因着信,不在乎遵行律法」(罗3:28)。从加利利到罗马,从会堂到书信,这是同一位使徒、同一个不变的福音核心。

这是全本圣经的分水岭,也是每个人必须面对的抉择。我们心里都有一种根深蒂固的倾向,想靠自己的好行为、宗教表现来站立在神面前。但福音宣告:你永远无法靠律法称义,唯有信靠基督。今天,你若仍在靠自己的努力赚取神的接纳,愿这节经文释放你——赦罪的道,已经藉着这人白白临到你。

默想:在我心底,我是否仍在靠「做得够好」来赚取神的接纳?哪些地方显出我还没真正安息在「因信称义」里?

应用:今天每当你因失败而觉得「神不会悦纳我」时,就默想这句话:我得称义,不是靠我的表现,乃是靠信靠这人。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你藉着基督,把赦罪与称义白白赐给信靠祂的人。赦免我总想靠自己的努力站在你面前。求你叫我彻底安息在因信称义的恩典里,不再靠律法挣扎,而是靠信靠你得自由。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
On his first missionary journey, in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch, Paul stated the core of the gospel with utter clarity: "Let it be known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and by him everyone who believes is freed from everything from which you could not be freed by the law of Moses" (Acts 13:38-39).

These two verses set two roads before people. One is "justification by the law" — trying to earn God’s acceptance by one’s own effort to fully keep the law, to be good enough; but Paul says this road fails in "everything" — because no one can keep the law fully. The other is "believing in this man" — that is, believing in Jesus Christ, receiving justification freely on the basis of what he accomplished. Justification is not a reward, but grace; not wages earned by works, but a gift received by faith.

Paul later, in Romans, developed this truth — first proclaimed here in the Antioch synagogue — into the backbone of the entire letter: "For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law" (Romans 3:28). From Galilee to Rome, from synagogue to epistle, it is the same apostle, the same unchanging core of the gospel.

This is the watershed of the whole Bible, and a decision every person must face. We all have a deeply rooted tendency within us to want to stand before God on our own good works, our own religious performance. But the gospel declares: you can never be justified by the law, only by believing in Christ. Today, if you are still trying to earn God’s acceptance by your own effort, may this verse set you free — the message of forgiveness has already come to you freely, through this man.

Meditation: Deep down, am I still trying to earn God’s acceptance by "being good enough"? In what ways does this show I haven’t truly rested in "justification by faith"?

Application: Today, whenever you feel "God won’t accept me" because of some failure, meditate on this: I am justified not by my performance, but by believing in this man.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for freely giving forgiveness and justification, through Christ, to all who believe in him. Forgive me for always trying to stand before you by my own effort. Let me rest completely in the grace of justification by faith, no longer struggling under the law, but finding freedom through believing in you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 当信主耶稣,你必得救
entries.title_en: Believe in the Lord Jesus, and You Will Be Saved
entries.scripture: 徒十五章卅六节至十八章廿二节
entries.verse: 使徒行传十六章卅一节
entries.content:
保罗和西拉在腓立比被下在监里,半夜却唱诗赞美神。忽然地大震动,监门全开,锁链松脱。禁卒以为囚犯已逃,拔刀要自杀,保罗拦住他。这位在崩溃边缘的人颤抖着问:「二位先生,我当怎样行才可以得救?」他们说:「当信主耶稣,你和你一家都必得救」(徒16:31)。

请注意这答案何等简单,又何等深刻。禁卒没有被要求先改好自己的人生、先赎清罪、先证明自己配得——只被要求「信」。救恩不是给那些够格的人的奖赏,而是给那些走投无路、肯伸手接受的人的礼物。这正是福音的震撼:在你最糟、最绝望的一刻,恩典的门是敞开的。保罗后来把这份「只需信」的简单,写成了一句公式:「你若口里认耶稣为主,心里信神叫他从死里复活,就必得救」(罗10:9)——不必先攒够功德,只需口里承认、心里相信。

当夜,这位禁卒就给他们洗伤、全家受洗,「因为信了神,都很喜乐」(徒16:34)。几小时前还想结束自己生命的人,如今满心喜乐。这就是福音的能力:它不要求你先变好才能来,它使你因信而来,再从里面把你更新。今天,无论你觉得自己多不配,这句话仍向你发出:当信主耶稣,你必得救。

默想:我是否仍暗暗以为,要先把自己整理好,神才会接纳我?「当信主耶稣」这简单的邀请,对我意味着什么?

应用:今天为一个正在人生低谷、走投无路的人祷告,并求主给你机会,把这简单而有能力的好消息带给他。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你不是等我配得才拯救我,而是在我走投无路时,只要我口里承认、心里相信,就白白拯救了我。求你除去我「先变好才敢来」的错觉,叫我单纯信靠你,也把这份喜乐的好消息带给身边绝望的人。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul and Silas were thrown into prison at Philippi, yet at midnight they sang hymns of praise to God. Suddenly a great earthquake shook the place, the prison doors flew open, and everyone’s chains came loose. The jailer, supposing the prisoners had escaped, drew his sword to kill himself, but Paul stopped him. Trembling, this man on the verge of collapse asked: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" They said: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household" (Acts 16:31).

Notice how simple, and how profound, this answer is. The jailer was not asked to first clean up his life, first pay off his sins, first prove himself worthy — only asked to "believe." Salvation is not a reward for the qualified, but a gift for those at the end of their rope who simply reach out and receive. This is exactly the shock of the gospel: at your worst, most desperate moment, the door of grace stands open. Paul later wrote this simplicity of "only believe" into a formula: "if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved" (Romans 10:9) — no need to first accumulate enough merit, only to confess with the mouth and believe with the heart.

That very night, the jailer washed their wounds, and he and his whole household were baptized, "having believed in God, [he] rejoiced along with his entire household" (Acts 16:34). A man who, hours before, wanted to end his own life, was now filled with joy. This is the power of the gospel: it does not require you to become good first before you can come — it lets you come by faith, and then renews you from within. Today, no matter how unworthy you feel, this word still calls out to you: believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved.

Meditation: Do I still secretly think I need to get myself together before God will accept me? What does the simple invitation "believe in the Lord Jesus" mean for me?

Application: Today, pray for someone in the depths of life, at the end of their rope, and ask the Lord for an opportunity to bring them this simple, powerful good news.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for not waiting until I was worthy to save me, but saving me freely when I was at the end of my rope, the moment I confessed with my mouth and believed in my heart. Remove my illusion of needing to "get better before I dare come," and let me simply believe in you, and also carry this joyful good news to those around me who are in despair. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 施比受更为有福
entries.title_en: It Is More Blessed to Give Than to Receive
entries.scripture: 徒十八章廿三节至廿一章十七节
entries.verse: 使徒行传二十章卅五节
entries.content:
保罗第三次宣教旅程,在与以弗所长老含泪道别时,引用了一句主耶稣的话——这句话四福音没有记载,却被保罗郑重传下:「施比受更为有福」(徒20:35)。保罗不是站着说漂亮话,他刚提醒众人,自己「凡事给你们作榜样」,亲手做工供给自己和同人的需用。他是活出来了,才这样说。

这句话彻底挑战我们本能的算盘。我们直觉认为「得」才有福——多拿一点、多留一点、多积一点才安全。但主说,真正的福,在于「施」。所罗门早就用另一种方式说过同样的悖论:「有施散的,却更增添;有吝惜过度的,反致穷乏。好施舍的,必得丰裕;滋润人的,必得滋润」(箴11:24-25)。这不是一套可以算计操控的公式,而是神在祂所造的世界里,埋下的一条属灵定律:紧抓带来枯竭,施予带来丰盛。

因为施予让我们像神——那位不住地赐予、把独生子都舍了的神;也因为施予释放我们脱离对财物的紧抓,尝到一种拥有再多也换不来的喜乐。

问题是,我们常把「施」留到「有余」以后——等我更宽裕了、更有安全感了再说。但那一天几乎永远不会到。主的邀请是现在就开始:在还觉得不够时就伸手给予,你会发现:那从不是净损失,而是紧抓时从未尝过的自由与喜乐——这才是主所说「更为有福」的真意,不是来日加倍偿还的利息,而是施予本身此刻就带来的丰盛。

默想:我真的相信「施比受更为有福」吗?还是我的生活方式其实在说「受比施更有福」?我把「施予」拖到了什么条件之后?

应用:今天不等「有余」,就主动施予一次——一笔奉献、一段时间、一份款待——刻意给到略微超出你舒适的地步。

祷告:主啊,你是那位把独生子都舍了、不住施予的神。赦免我总想着「得」,把「施」拖到将来。求你叫我此刻就学习施予,像你一样慷慨,在给予中尝到那超乎所舍的福乐。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
On his third missionary journey, bidding a tearful farewell to the Ephesian elders, Paul quoted a saying of the Lord Jesus — one not recorded in the four Gospels, yet solemnly passed down by Paul: "It is more blessed to give than to receive" (Acts 20:35). Paul was not standing there offering pretty words; he had just reminded them that he himself "gave you an example in every way," working with his own hands to supply his own needs and those of his companions. He said this only because he had lived it.

This sentence utterly challenges our instinctive calculations. We instinctively feel that "receiving" is blessed — grabbing a little more, keeping a little more, saving up a little more feels safer. But the Lord says the true blessing lies in "giving." Solomon long ago expressed the same paradox another way: "One gives freely, yet grows all the richer; another withholds what he should give, and only suffers want. Whoever brings blessing will be enriched, and one who waters will himself be watered" (Proverbs 11:24-25). This isn’t a formula you can calculate and manipulate, but a spiritual law God has embedded in the world he made: clinging tightly brings withering, giving brings abundance.

Giving makes us like God — the God who gives without ceasing, who even gave up his only Son; giving also frees us from clinging to our possessions, letting us taste a joy that no amount of wealth can buy.

The problem is, we often postpone "giving" until we have "surplus" — waiting until we’re more comfortable, more secure, before we say it. But that day almost never comes. The Lord’s invitation is to start now: reach out and give while you still feel it’s not enough, and you’ll discover it was never a net loss, but a freedom and joy you never tasted while clinging — this is the true meaning of the Lord’s words "more blessed," not interest to be repaid double someday, but the abundance that giving itself brings, right now.

Meditation: Do I truly believe "it is more blessed to give than to receive"? Or does my actual lifestyle say "it’s more blessed to receive than to give"? What condition have I been dragging "giving" behind?

Application: Today, without waiting for "surplus," proactively give once — a gift, some time, an act of hospitality — deliberately giving to a point slightly beyond your comfort.

Prayer: Lord, you are the God who gave up your only Son, who gives without ceasing. Forgive me for always thinking about "receiving," postponing "giving" to the future. Let me learn to give right now, generous as you are, tasting in giving a blessing greater than what was given up. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title_en: A Clear Conscience Toward God and Man
entries.scripture: 徒廿一章十八节至廿四章
entries.verse: 使徒行传廿四章十六节
entries.content:
保罗被捉拿、受审,面对诬告与威胁,他在巡抚腓力斯面前从容陈明自己的为人:「我因此自己勉励,对神对人常存无亏的良心」(徒24:16)。「勉励」表明这不是自然而然、毫不费力的,而是一生刻意的操练与追求——保守自己在神面前、也在人面前,良心清洁无亏。

一个「无亏的良心」是极大的财富。它让保罗在诬陷面前坦然,在患难中站立得稳,因为他里面没有需要遮掩的黑暗、没有出卖过自己的把柄。反过来,一个被亏负、被玷污的良心,会像内里的蛀虫,使人在压力下退缩、在试探前妥协、在独处时不安。保罗后来提醒提摩太,这不只是保罗个人的操练,更是信仰本身能否站立的根基:「常存信心和无亏的良心。有人丢弃良心,就在真道上如同船破坏了一般」(提前1:19)——良心的亏损,足以拖垮一个人的整个信仰。

保守无亏的良心,意味着两件事:对神,不容让隐而未现的罪;对人,不亏欠、不欺瞒。这需要及时的认罪、诚实的关系、和在小事上的忠心。今天的世界告诉我们「别人看不见就没关系」,但敬畏神的人知道:神看得见,而一个清洁的良心,是任何名利都换不来的自由。

默想:此刻我的良心,在神面前、在人面前,有没有一处「亏欠」是我一直不肯处理的?它是否正在暗中削弱我的坦然与刚强,甚至动摇我信仰的根基?

应用:今天处理一件亏欠的事——向神认一个隐藏的罪,或向人道一个当道的歉、还一笔当还的债。

祷告:主啊,求你帮助我像保罗一样,刻意保守对你、对人无亏的良心,免得像丢弃良心的人那样,在真道上如同船破坏了一般。光照我里面隐藏的、亏欠的地方,给我勇气及时认罪、及时和好。叫我拥有那清洁良心所带来的坦然与自由。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul, seized and put on trial, facing false accusations and threats, calmly declared his own conduct before the governor Felix: "So I always take pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man" (Acts 24:16). "Take pains" shows this was not something natural or effortless, but a lifelong, deliberate discipline and pursuit — keeping his conscience clean and clear both before God and before man.

A "clear conscience" is a tremendous asset. It let Paul stand calm before false accusation, stand firm in hardship, because there was no darkness within him needing to be hidden, no leverage he had ever handed over against himself. Conversely, a wounded, defiled conscience is like an inner moth, causing a person to shrink back under pressure, compromise before temptation, feel uneasy in solitude. Paul later reminded Timothy that this was not merely Paul’s personal discipline, but the very foundation on which faith itself can stand: "holding faith and a good conscience. By rejecting this, some have made shipwreck of their faith" (1 Timothy 1:19) — a damaged conscience is enough to drag down a person’s entire faith.

Keeping a clear conscience means two things: toward God, not tolerating hidden, unconfessed sin; toward man, not owing, not deceiving. This requires timely confession, honest relationships, and faithfulness in small things. Today’s world tells us "it doesn’t matter if no one sees," but those who fear God know: God sees, and a clean conscience is a freedom that no fame or fortune can buy.

Meditation: Right now, is there a place of "debt" in my conscience, before God, before man, that I have refused to deal with? Is it quietly weakening my calm and strength, even shaking the foundation of my faith?

Application: Today, deal with one thing you owe — confess a hidden sin to God, or offer an overdue apology to someone, or repay a debt you owe.

Prayer: Lord, help me, like Paul, to deliberately keep a clear conscience toward you and toward man, lest I, like those who reject their conscience, make shipwreck of my faith. Shine light on the hidden, indebted places within me, give me courage to confess and reconcile promptly. Let me possess the calm and freedom that a clean conscience brings. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 拦阻不住的福音
entries.title_en: The Gospel That Cannot Be Stopped
entries.verse: 使徒行传廿八章三十、卅一节
entries.content:
使徒行传以一幅出人意料的画面收尾:保罗——一个戴着锁链的囚犯——在罗马「放胆传讲神国的道,将主耶稣基督的事教导人,并没有人禁止」(徒28:31)。原文的最后一个词是「毫无拦阻地」。一个被囚的人,福音却毫无拦阻;这正是路加要留给我们的信息。

从耶路撒冷的一小群门徒,到福音传至当时世界的中心罗马;从逼迫、下监、船难,到此刻锁链中的宣讲——没有一样能拦住神国的推进。人可以捆住保罗的身体,却捆不住神的话。保罗自己后来在另一次监禁中,把这真理浓缩成一句掷地有声的宣告:「我为这福音受苦难,甚至被捆绑,像犯人一样。然而神的道却不被捆绑」(提后2:9)。锁链锁得住使徒,锁不住福音。

这给每一个感到「被困住」的信徒极大的鼓励。也许你此刻被环境捆绑、被处境限制,觉得自己无能为力。但神的国不受你处境的辖制。保罗在锁链中仍能放胆传讲、结出果子;神也能在你看似受限的位置上,藉着你成就祂拦阻不住的工作。

默想:我是否常以「等我处境好转、等我更自由了」为借口,推迟为主而活?保罗在锁链中的宣讲,如何挑战这借口?

应用:就在你目前「受限」的处境里(工作、家庭、健康),找一件今天就能为主做的小事,忠心去做,不等环境改变。

祷告:掌管万有的主,你的国和你的道,是人拦阻不住的。赦免我常以处境为借口而止步。求你叫我像锁链中的保罗一样,深信神的道不被捆绑,在我被摆放的地方,放胆为你而活。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Acts ends with an unexpected picture: Paul — a prisoner in chains — in Rome "proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance" (Acts 28:31). The last word in the original text is "unhindered." A man in prison, yet the gospel utterly unhindered — this is exactly the message Luke wants to leave with us.

From a small band of disciples in Jerusalem, to the gospel reaching Rome, the center of the world at that time; from persecution, imprisonment, shipwreck, to this preaching in chains — nothing could stop the advance of God’s kingdom. Men could bind Paul’s body, but they could not bind God’s word. Paul himself later, in another imprisonment, condensed this truth into a resounding declaration: "For which I am suffering, bound with chains as a criminal. But the word of God is not bound!" (2 Timothy 2:9) Chains could lock up the apostle, but not the gospel.

This is a tremendous encouragement to every believer who feels "trapped." Perhaps you are right now bound by circumstances, limited by your situation, feeling utterly powerless. But God’s kingdom is not controlled by your circumstances. Paul, in chains, could still boldly proclaim and bear fruit; God can also, in your seemingly limited position, accomplish through you his work that cannot be stopped.

Meditation: Do I often use "when my circumstances improve, when I’m more free" as an excuse to postpone living for the Lord? How does Paul’s preaching in chains challenge that excuse?

Application: Right in your current "limited" circumstances (work, family, health), find one small thing you can do for the Lord today, and do it faithfully, without waiting for circumstances to change.

Prayer: Sovereign Lord over all things, your kingdom and your word cannot be stopped by man. Forgive me for often using circumstances as an excuse to stop. Let me, like Paul in chains, believe deeply that God’s word is not bound, and boldly live for you right where you have placed me. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 世人都犯了罪,却白白称义
entries.title_en: All Have Sinned, Yet Are Justified Freely
entries.verse: 罗马书三章廿三、廿四节
entries.content:
保罗在罗马书用了整整两章多,细细论证一件人最不愿承认的事:无论是有律法的犹太人,还是没有律法的外邦人,「没有义人,连一个也没有」。然后他下了总结:「因为世人都犯了罪,亏缺了神的荣耀;如今却蒙神的恩典,因基督耶稣的救赎,就白白地称义」(罗3:23-24)。

这两节里藏着福音全部的张力。前半句把每个人都拉到同一条起跑线上——无一例外,都犯了罪、都亏缺。这话戳破了我们最深的自义:我不比别人差、我还算个好人。但正是这「坏消息」,让「好消息」显得如此惊人:「却蒙神的恩典……白白地称义。」我们本该受审判,得着的却是白白的赦免。

「白白」二字是关键。称义不是打折出售,也不是先付订金;它是全然的礼物,是基督已经付清了全部代价。保罗后来在以弗所书把这真理写成了最简洁的公式:「你们得救是本乎恩,也因着信;这并不是出于自己,乃是神所赐的;也不是出于行为,免得有人自夸」(弗2:8-9)。这既击碎骄傲——你无一点可夸,也挪去自卑——你的被接纳不靠你的表现。

当一个人真明白自己「都犯了罪」、却「白白称义」,他既谦卑又坦然,既不再自义,也不再自弃。

默想:「世人都犯了罪」——我是否真把自己算在其中,还是暗暗觉得自己是例外?「白白称义」的礼物,我是否真的领受了,还是仍想自己付一点?

应用:今天当你想靠表现证明自己时,停下来对自己宣告:我已因基督白白称义,我的价值不靠今天的表现来加减。

祷告:主啊,我承认我也在「都犯了罪」之列,毫无可夸。谢谢你不按我所当受的报应我,反因基督的救赎,白白称我为义——不是出于我的行为,免得我自夸。求你叫我天天活在这恩典里——既谦卑,又坦然,不再自义,也不再自弃。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
In Romans, Paul spends over two whole chapters carefully arguing something no one wants to admit: whether Jew under the law or Gentile without it, "there is no one righteous, not even one." Then he draws his conclusion: "for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus" (Romans 3:23-24).

These two verses hold the entire tension of the gospel. The first half draws everyone to the same starting line — without exception, all have sinned, all fall short. This punctures our deepest self-righteousness: I’m not worse than others, I’m a decent person. But it is exactly this "bad news" that makes the "good news" so astonishing: "yet are justified by his grace... as a gift." We deserved judgment, yet received free pardon.

The word "gift" is key. Justification is not sold at a discount, nor a down payment first required; it is an entirely free gift, because Christ has already paid the full price. Paul later, in Ephesians, wrote this truth into the most concise formula: "For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9). This both shatters pride — you have nothing to boast of — and removes self-loathing — your acceptance does not depend on your performance.

When a person truly understands that they have "all sinned," yet are "justified freely," they become both humble and at peace, no longer self-righteous, and no longer self-condemning.

Meditation: "All have sinned" — do I truly count myself among them, or do I secretly feel I’m the exception? The gift of "justified freely" — have I truly received it, or am I still trying to pay some of it myself?

Application: Today, when you find yourself trying to prove your worth through performance, stop and declare to yourself: I am already justified freely through Christ; my worth is not added to or subtracted from by today’s performance.

Prayer: Lord, I confess that I too am among "all have sinned," with nothing to boast of. Thank you for not repaying me as I deserve, but instead, through Christ’s redemption, freely declaring me righteous — not by my works, so that I cannot boast. Let me live daily in this grace — both humble and at peace, no longer self-righteous, no longer self-condemning. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 在主里得自由
entries.title_en: Free in the Lord
entries.content:
在主里得自由

「所以天父的儿子若叫你们自由,你们就真自由了。」(约翰福音 8:36)

倪柝声提醒我们:真正的自由,不是从此可以随心所欲,而是脱离了那非靠自己不可、非表现不可的重担。在基督里,你的被接纳早已成定局,不必再挣扎证明。

今天,把那颗紧绷、想靠自己达标的心放下来。你是神所爱、已被称义的儿女——安息在这自由里,单单享受作祂儿女的坦然。

"If the Son sets you free, you are free indeed." (John 8:36) Freedom is not doing as you please, but resting in a love you no longer have to earn.
entries.content_en:
Free in the Lord

"So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." (John 8:36)

Watchman Nee reminds us: true freedom is not being able to do whatever you please from now on, but being freed from the burden of having to rely on yourself, having to perform. In Christ, your acceptance is already settled — you no longer need to strive to prove it.

Today, lay down that tense heart that keeps trying to measure up on its own. You are God’s beloved, already-justified child — rest in this freedom, simply enjoying the calm of being his child.

"If the Son sets you free, you are free indeed." (John 8:36) Freedom is not doing as you please, but resting in a love you no longer have to earn.

entries.title: 神既不爱惜自己的儿子
entries.title_en: He Who Did Not Spare His Own Son
entries.verse: 罗马书八章廿六、卅二节
entries.content:
罗马书第八章是全本圣经的高峰之一。保罗从「如今那些在基督耶稣里的,就不定罪了」起步,一路攀升到无可比拟的确据。途中他提醒我们,在软弱中并不孤单:「我们本不晓得当怎样祷告,只是圣灵亲自用说不出来的叹息替我们祷告」(罗8:26)。连我们结巴、说不出口的祷告,圣灵都接过去,替我们向父陈明。

而全章的根基,是那句压不住的宣告:「神既不爱惜自己的儿子,为我们众人舍了,岂不也把万物和他一同白白地赐给我们吗?」(罗8:32)保罗的逻辑是「从大到小」:神已经付出了那最贵、最难舍的——祂的独生子;那么一切较小的恩典——供应、看顾、最终的得赎——祂岂会吝惜?约翰后来用同一个逻辑说明爱的起源:「不是我们爱神,乃是神爱我们,差他的儿子为我们的罪作了挽回祭」(约壹4:10)。十字架是神爱我们的铁证,一次性地解决了「神到底顾不顾念我」的疑问。

这对我们焦虑的心是极大的安稳。当我们怀疑神是否真的为我们好、是否会撇下我们,只需回望十字架:那位连儿子都舍了的神,绝不会在小事上亏待你。祂对你的爱,不是靠你今天的感觉来衡量,而是靠祂已经付出的那不可思议的代价来担保。

默想:我常在哪些事上怀疑神是否真的顾念我?「连儿子都舍了」这一铁证,如何回答我心中的疑虑?

应用:今天把一件你正为之焦虑的事带到神面前,并以罗马书八章卅二节向自己宣告祂的爱,把它交托给祂。

祷告:父啊,你连自己的儿子都为我舍了,还有什么好处是你会向我吝惜的呢?求你用十字架的铁证安定我焦虑的心,叫我深信不是我先爱你、乃是你先爱我,并在软弱中,信靠那位替我叹息代求的圣灵。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Romans 8 is one of the peaks of the entire Bible. Paul begins with "there is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus," and climbs step by step to an incomparable assurance. Along the way he reminds us that we are not alone in our weakness: "we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words" (Romans 8:26). Even our stammering, wordless prayers, the Spirit takes up and presents to the Father on our behalf.

And the foundation of the whole chapter is that irrepressible declaration: "He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?" (Romans 8:32) Paul’s logic runs "from the greater to the lesser": God has already given up the most costly, the hardest to give up — his only Son; how then would he withhold anything lesser — provision, care, the final redemption? John later used this same logic to explain the origin of love: "not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins" (1 John 4:10). The cross is the ironclad proof of God’s love for us, settling once and for all the question "does God really care about me."

This is a tremendous stabilizer for our anxious hearts. When we doubt whether God truly means well for us, whether he will abandon us, we need only look back at the cross: the God who gave up even his Son will never shortchange you in the small things. His love for you is not measured by how you feel today, but guaranteed by that inconceivable price he has already paid.

Meditation: In what matters do I often doubt whether God truly cares about me? How does this ironclad proof — "he did not even spare his Son" — answer the doubts in my heart?

Application: Today, bring one thing you’re anxious about before God, declare his love to yourself using Romans 8:32, and entrust it to him.

Prayer: Father, you gave up even your own Son for me — what good thing would you ever withhold from me? Let the ironclad proof of the cross settle my anxious heart, let me believe deeply that it is not I who loved you first, but you who loved me first, and in weakness, let me trust the Spirit who groans and intercedes for me. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 为骨肉之亲心里忧伤
entries.title_en: Sorrow for My Own Flesh and Blood
entries.verse: 罗马书九章三节、十章九节
entries.content:
保罗刚在第八章唱完得胜的凯歌,笔锋一转,却是沉重的忧伤:「我是大有忧愁,心里时常伤痛……为我弟兄,我骨肉之亲,就是自己被咒诅,与基督分离,我也愿意」(罗9:2-3)。这是何等惊人的话——为了同胞能得救,保罗甚至愿意自己被咒诅。这不是一时冲动,而是一颗被神的爱烧透了的心。他在第十章又说:「弟兄们,我心里所愿的,向神所求的,是要以色列人得救」(罗10:1)——忧伤没有把他压垮成绝望,而是化成了不住的代求。

对照我们,常常一边享受着「因信称义」的平安,一边对身边未信的家人、同胞无动于衷。保罗清楚地知道得救之路:「你若口里认耶稣为主,心里信神叫他从死里复活,就必得救」(罗10:9)。正因他知道这门是敞开的,也知道许多人还在门外,他的心才如此焦急、如此忧伤。

这向我们发出一个扎心的问题:我们为失丧者流过泪吗?我们是否也曾为自己所爱之人的灵魂,心里伤痛、切切代求?福音若真进入了心,不会只让我们自己安然得救,还会让我们为那些还没得救的人坐立难安。求主把保罗那样的心肠,也放在我们里面。

默想:我上一次为一个未信之人的灵魂,真正忧伤、恳切代求,是什么时候?我的心是否早已对身边人的失丧麻木了?

应用:今天为一位你所爱、却还未信主的家人或朋友,专心、恳切地祷告,并求主给你向他传福音的负担与机会。

祷告:主啊,赦免我常只顾自己的平安,却对身边人的灵魂漠不关心。求你把保罗那颗为骨肉之亲忧伤、切切祈求的心赐给我,叫我为失丧的人流泪代求,并甘心把「认耶稣为主必得救」的好消息带给他们。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul, having just finished singing the triumphant song of chapter 8, turns his pen to a heavy sorrow: "I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart... For I could wish that I myself were accursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh" (Romans 9:2-3). What astonishing words — for the sake of his own people’s salvation, Paul would even be willing to be accursed himself. This was not a momentary impulse, but a heart utterly set ablaze by God’s love. In chapter 10 he says again: "Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved" (Romans 10:1) — sorrow did not crush him into despair, but turned into unceasing intercession.

In contrast, we often enjoy the peace of "justification by faith" on one hand, while remaining indifferent to the unbelieving family and countrymen around us on the other. Paul knew clearly the way of salvation: "if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved" (Romans 10:9). Precisely because he knew this door was open, and knew many were still outside it, his heart was this anxious, this sorrowful.

This poses a piercing question to us: have we ever wept for the lost? Have we ever felt grief in our hearts, interceding earnestly, for the souls of those we love? If the gospel has truly entered our hearts, it will not merely let us rest secure in our own salvation, but will also make us unable to sit still for those who are not yet saved. May the Lord place in us that same heart Paul had.

Meditation: When was the last time I truly grieved and earnestly interceded for the soul of an unbeliever? Has my heart already grown numb to the lostness of those around me?

Application: Today, pray focused, earnest prayer for one family member or friend you love who does not yet believe, and ask the Lord for a burden and an opportunity to share the gospel with them.

Prayer: Lord, forgive me for often only caring about my own peace, while remaining indifferent to the souls around me. Give me that heart Paul had, grieving and earnestly interceding for his own flesh and blood, let me weep and intercede for the lost, and willingly bring them the good news that "confessing Jesus as Lord brings salvation." In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 将身体献上,当作活祭
entries.title_en: Present Your Bodies as a Living Sacrifice
entries.verse: 罗马书十二章一至二节，十五章一至二节
entries.content:
罗马书前十一章,保罗讲尽了神的怜悯——白白的称义、不能隔绝的爱、奇妙的救恩。到了第十二章,他才转向「该怎样活」:「所以弟兄们,我以神的慈悲劝你们,将身体献上,当作活祭……你们如此事奉乃是理所当然的」(罗12:1)。请注意那个「所以」——基督徒的伦理,永远是从福音的恩典流出来的回应,而不是赚取神喜悦的手段。

次序至关重要。宗教说:你要献上、要付出、要圣洁,神才会爱你、接纳你。福音却倒过来说:神已经因基督白白地爱你、接纳你了——「以神的慈悲」——所以你才甘心把整个自己献上。前者是恐惧驱动的苦役,后者是感恩涌流的敬拜。同样是「奉献」,动机却天差地别。保罗后来给提多的教导,把这次序说得同样清楚:「神救众人的恩典已经显明出来,教训我们除去不敬虔的心和世俗的情欲,在今世自守、公义、敬虔度日」(多2:11-12)——是恩典亲自教导、亲自催逼我们敬虔,不是我们靠敬虔去换恩典。

接着保罗说:「不要效法这个世界,只要心意更新而变化」(罗12:2)。真正的改变,不是靠外在硬性的规条,而是从被恩典融化的心里、从更新的心思里,长出与神心意相合的生活。今天,你若感到事奉是重担、是交差,或许该先回到第一至十一章——重新被神的慈悲触摸,让感恩重新点燃你甘心的奉献。

默想:我的奉献与事奉,是被「怕神不爱我」驱动,还是被「神已白白爱我」的感恩涌流出来?这两者在我心中占多大比重?

应用:今天把一件你觉得像「交差」的事奉,先停下来数算神的慈悲,再带着感恩重新去做,让它成为敬拜而非苦役。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你先以慈悲白白地接纳了我,又用你的恩典亲自教导我敬虔度日。求你叫我的奉献不再出于恐惧的苦役,而是出于感恩的敬拜。更新我的心思,叫我不效法这世界,而是从被你的爱融化的里面,甘心把整个自己献给你。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
In the first eleven chapters of Romans, Paul lays out the full extent of God’s mercy — free justification, love that cannot be separated, wondrous salvation. Only in chapter 12 does he turn to "how then shall we live": "I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice... which is your spiritual worship" (Romans 12:1). Notice that "therefore" — Christian ethics always flow as a response to the grace of the gospel, never as a means to earn God’s favor.

The order matters immensely. Religion says: you must offer, must pay, must be holy, before God will love you, accept you. The gospel says the reverse: God has already, freely, through Christ, loved you, accepted you — "by the mercies of God" — and so you willingly offer your entire self. The former is fear-driven servitude; the latter is worship overflowing from gratitude. The same word "offering," yet worlds apart in motive. Paul’s later instruction to Titus states this same order just as clearly: "the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age" (Titus 2:11-12) — it is grace itself that teaches us, that compels us toward godliness, not us earning grace through godliness.

Paul then says: "Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind" (Romans 12:2). True change does not come through external, rigid rules, but grows out of a heart melted by grace, out of a renewed mind, into a life that aligns with God’s will. Today, if you feel serving is a burden, a duty to check off, perhaps you should return first to chapters 1–11 — be touched afresh by God’s mercy, and let gratitude reignite your willing offering.

Meditation: Is my giving and service driven by "fear that God doesn’t love me," or overflowing from gratitude that "God already loves me freely"? How much weight does each carry in my heart?

Application: Today, before doing an act of service that feels like a "duty to check off," first pause and count God’s mercies, then do it with gratitude, letting it become worship rather than servitude.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for first accepting me freely through mercy, and then personally teaching me through your grace to live a godly life. Let my offering no longer come from fear-driven servitude, but from grateful worship. Renew my mind, that I would not be conformed to this world, but from a heart melted by your love, willingly offer my whole self to you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
entries.verse_text: 所以，弟兄们，我以 神的慈悲劝你们，将身体献上，当作活祭，是圣洁的，是 神所喜悦的；你们如此事奉乃是理所当然的。不要效法这个世界，只要心意更新而变化，叫你们察验何为 神的善良、纯全、可喜悦的旨意。我们坚固的人应该担代不坚固人的软弱，不求自己的喜悦。我们各人务要叫邻舍喜悦，使他得益处，建立 德行 。

entries.title: 神拣选了世上软弱的
entries.title_en: God Chose What Is Weak in the World
entries.verse: 哥林多前书一章廿五、廿七至廿九节
entries.content:
哥林多教会崇尚口才、智慧与地位,保罗却把他们的价值观整个翻转过来:「因神的愚拙总比人智慧,神的软弱总比人强壮」(林前1:25)。他提醒他们看看自己蒙召的光景:按人看,他们中间有智慧的、有能力的、有尊贵的,并不多。「神却拣选了世上愚拙的,叫有智慧的羞愧;又拣选了世上软弱的,叫那强壮的羞愧」(林前1:27)。

神为什么这样做?保罗说得明白:「使一切有血气的,在神面前一个也不能自夸」(林前1:29)。神救恩的设计,从根本上就是要除掉人一切自夸的余地。祂拣选软弱的、卑微的、被世界轻看的,好叫得救全然出于祂的恩典,荣耀全然归给祂自己,没有人能说「这是我靠自己挣来的」。

保罗紧接着说出这一切的落脚点:「你们得在基督耶稣里是本乎神,神又使他成为我们的智慧、公义、圣洁、救赎。如经上所记:夸口的,当指着主夸口」(林前1:30-31)。我们的智慧、义、圣洁,没有一样是自己修来的,全都「在基督耶稣里」白白得着——所以能夸的,只剩下这一位主。

这既谦卑我们,也安慰我们。谦卑我们——因为我们没有一样可夸,连信心都是祂所赐;安慰我们——因为神向来喜欢使用那些自觉软弱、无可夸口的人。你不必先变得够强、够有能力、够有资格,神才能用你;恰恰相反,当你承认自己的软弱、单单倚靠祂,你正是祂乐意使用的器皿。

默想:我是否仍靠自己的能力、成就、恩赐在神面前暗暗自夸?神「拣选软弱的」这一原则,如何改变我看待自己的软弱?

应用:今天把一样你以为「不够格、太软弱」而不敢为主摆上的地方,交在神手中,信靠祂的能力在你的软弱上显得完全。

祷告:主啊,你拣选软弱的、愚拙的,好叫无人能在你面前自夸,又使基督成了我们的智慧、公义、圣洁、救赎。求你除去我一切的自恃与自夸,叫我甘心承认自己的软弱,单单倚靠你的恩典与能力。愿一切荣耀都归给你,而非归给我。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The Corinthian church prized eloquence, wisdom, and status, but Paul turned their entire value system upside down: "For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men" (1 Corinthians 1:25). He reminded them to look at their own calling: by human standards, not many among them were wise, powerful, or of noble birth. "But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong" (1 Corinthians 1:27).

Why did God do this? Paul states it plainly: "so that no human being might boast in the presence of God" (1 Corinthians 1:29). The very design of God’s salvation is meant, at its root, to remove every ground for human boasting. He chose the weak, the lowly, those the world despises, so that salvation would be entirely by his grace, and glory entirely his own, with no one able to say "I earned this myself."

Paul immediately follows with the landing point of all this: "because of him you are in Christ Jesus, who became to us wisdom from God, righteousness and sanctification and redemption, so that, as it is written, ‘Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord’" (1 Corinthians 1:30-31). Not one of our wisdom, righteousness, or holiness is self-cultivated — all of it is received freely "in Christ Jesus" — so the only one left to boast in is this one Lord.

This both humbles us and comforts us. It humbles us — because we have nothing to boast of, even faith itself is his gift; it comforts us — because God has always loved to use those who acknowledge their own weakness, who have nothing to boast of. You don’t need to first become strong enough, capable enough, qualified enough before God can use you; quite the opposite — when you acknowledge your weakness, relying solely on him, you are exactly the vessel he delights to use.

Meditation: Am I still secretly boasting before God in my own ability, achievements, gifts? How does the principle "God chose the weak" change how I view my own weakness?

Application: Today, hand over to God one area you’ve thought yourself "too unqualified, too weak" to offer for him, trusting that his power is made perfect in your weakness.

Prayer: Lord, you chose the weak, the foolish, so that no one could boast before you, and you made Christ our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption. Remove all my self-reliance and self-boasting, let me willingly acknowledge my weakness, relying solely on your grace and power. May all glory belong to you, not to me. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 你们是重价买来的
entries.title_en: You Were Bought with a Price
entries.verse: 哥林多前书六章十二、二十节
entries.content:
哥林多城道德败坏,教会里也有人以「凡事我都可行」为借口放纵身体。保罗回应:「凡事我都可行,但不都有益处……但无论哪一件,我总不受它的辖制。」接着他抛出一个改变一切的事实:「你们不是自己的人,因为你们是重价买来的。所以要在你们的身子上荣耀神」(林前6:19-20)。

「你们不是自己的人」——这句话彻底颠覆了现代人「我的身体我作主」的口号。保罗说,你之所以不能任意放纵,不是因为一堆冷冰冰的规条,而是因为你已经被「重价买来」了。那重价,是神儿子的宝血。彼得后来把这重价说得更具体:「你们得赎……不是凭着能坏的金银等物,乃是凭着基督的宝血,如同无瑕疵、无玷污的羔羊之血」(彼前1:18-19)。你的身体不再属你自己,而属那位用生命赎买你的主。

这让「圣洁」有了全新的意义。它不再是压抑、是扫兴,而是一种归属的自然流露:既然我整个人——包括身体——都是主用命换来的,我就要用它来荣耀祂,而不是糟蹋它、贱卖它。当你真明白自己被爱到什么地步、被赎买的代价有多大,你就再不愿把这被重价买来的身子,随便交给罪。

默想:我是否在某些方面,仍活得像「我的身体、我的生活我作主」?「你们是重价买来的」如何改变我对待自己身体、时间、习惯的态度?

应用:找出一个你一直放纵、或用来败坏自己的领域(眼目、饮食、私下的习惯),今天在其中作一个「荣耀神」的具体选择。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你用重价——你儿子那无瑕疵、无玷污的宝血——把我赎买回来。我不再是自己的人。求你叫我看重这归属,除去我「身体我作主」的放纵,叫我甘心在我的身子上荣耀你,因我整个人都属于你。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The city of Corinth was morally corrupt, and even within the church some used "all things are lawful for me" as an excuse to indulge the body. Paul responded: "‘All things are lawful for me,’ but not all things are helpful... I will not be dominated by anything." Then he threw out a fact that changes everything: "You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

"You are not your own" — this sentence utterly overturns the modern slogan "my body, my choice." Paul says you cannot indulge yourself as you please, not because of a pile of cold, lifeless rules, but because you have already been "bought with a price." That price is the blood of God’s own Son. Peter later stated this price even more concretely: "you were ransomed... not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot" (1 Peter 1:18-19). Your body no longer belongs to you, but to the Lord who redeemed you with his own life.

This gives "holiness" an entirely new meaning. It is no longer suppression, no longer a killjoy, but the natural overflow of belonging: since my whole self — including my body — was bought with the Lord’s life, I should use it to glorify him, not waste it, not sell it cheap. When you truly understand how deeply you are loved, how great the price of your redemption, you will no longer be willing to hand this body, bought at such a price, over to sin so carelessly.

Meditation: In some areas, am I still living as though "my body, my life, my choice"? How does "you were bought with a price" change how I treat my body, my time, my habits?

Application: Identify an area you’ve been indulging, or using to corrupt yourself (what you look at, what you eat, a private habit), and today make a concrete "glorify God" choice in that area.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for redeeming me with a price — your Son’s unblemished, spotless, precious blood. I am no longer my own. Let me treasure this belonging, remove my indulgent "my body, my choice" attitude, and willingly glorify you in my body, for my whole self belongs to you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 无论做什么,都要荣耀神
entries.title_en: Whatever You Do, Do It All for the Glory of God
entries.verse: 哥林多前书十章廿三、廿四、卅一节
entries.content:
论到信徒的自由,保罗给了一条贯穿一切的总原则:「凡事都可行,但不都有益处……无论何人,不要求自己的益处,乃要求别人的益处。」最后归结为一句总纲:「所以,你们或吃或喝,无论做什么,都要为荣耀神而行」(林前10:23-24、31)。

这句话把神的荣耀,从「宗教活动」的小格子里释放出来,铺满了生活的每一个角落。不只是祷告、聚会、读经可以荣耀神,连最平凡的「吃喝」——最日常、最不属灵的事——都能成为荣耀神的场所。保罗后来把这原则说得更全面:「无论做什么,或说话或行事,都要奉主耶稣的名,藉着他感谢父神」(西3:17)。换句话说,基督徒没有「与神无关」的时刻;整个人生,都是敬拜的舞台。

「荣耀神」是什么意思?就是让神显为大、显为美、显为满足——透过我们如何生活,叫人看见这位神值得倚靠、值得以祂为乐。当我以感恩的心吃一顿饭、以诚实做一件工、以爱顾念别人的益处,我就在向世界宣告:我的神是又真又好的。今天最平凡的事,都可以成为你把荣耀归给祂的机会。

默想:我是否把生活切成了「属灵的」和「世俗的」两半,以为只有前者与神有关?若连吃喝都能荣耀神,我今天的日常会有什么不同?

应用:选一件今天最平凡的事(一餐饭、一段通勤、一项家务),刻意带着「为荣耀神而行」的心去做。

祷告:主啊,你配得我生活每一处的荣耀,不只是聚会和祷告的时刻。求你叫我不再把生活分成属灵与世俗,而是或吃或喝、无论做什么,都奉你的名而行、为荣耀你而行,叫我整个人生都成为向你献上的敬拜。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
On the subject of believers’ freedom, Paul gives an overarching principle that runs through everything: "‘All things are lawful,’ but not all things are helpful... Let no one seek his own good, but the good of his neighbor." He then sums it all up in one governing statement: "So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God" (1 Corinthians 10:23-24, 31).

This sentence frees the glory of God from the small compartment labeled "religious activity," spreading it across every corner of life. Not only prayer, worship gatherings, and Bible reading can glorify God — even the most mundane "eating and drinking," the most everyday, least "spiritual" things, can become a place where God is glorified. Paul later stated this principle even more comprehensively: "whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him" (Colossians 3:17). In other words, there is no moment in a Christian’s life that is "unrelated to God"; the whole of life is a stage for worship.

What does "glorify God" mean? It means letting God appear great, appear beautiful, appear satisfying — letting people see, through the way we live, that this God is worth relying on, worth delighting in. When I eat a meal with a grateful heart, do a piece of work honestly, care about another’s good in love, I am declaring to the world: my God is true and good. Today, even the most ordinary things can become an opportunity for you to give him glory.

Meditation: Have I cut my life into two halves, "spiritual" and "secular," thinking only the former relates to God? If even eating and drinking can glorify God, how would today’s ordinary routine be different?

Application: Pick the most ordinary thing you’ll do today (a meal, a commute, a household chore), and deliberately do it with the intention of "doing it for the glory of God."

Prayer: Lord, you deserve glory in every part of my life, not only in moments of worship gatherings and prayer. Let me no longer divide life into spiritual and secular, but whether eating or drinking, whatever I do, let me do it in your name, for your glory, so that my whole life becomes an offering of worship to you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 属灵的加油站
entries.title_en: The Spiritual Refueling Station
entries.content:
属灵的加油站

「你们要住在我里面,我也住在你们里面。」(约翰福音 15:4)

倪柝声提醒我们:属灵的力量不是从加倍的忙碌里挤出来的,而是从住在主里面、与祂连结中流出来的。枝子若离了树,再努力也结不出果子。

今天,不要急着为主奔跑,先安静地回到主里面。让祂的生命重新流通到你里面枯干的地方,重新得力,再上路。

"Abide in me, and I in you." (John 15:4) Strength is not squeezed out of busyness, but drawn from staying connected to Him.
entries.content_en:
The Spiritual Refueling Station

"Abide in me, and I in you." (John 15:4)

Watchman Nee reminds us: spiritual strength is not squeezed out of redoubled busyness, but flows from abiding in the Lord, from staying connected to him. A branch cut off from the tree, no matter how hard it tries, cannot bear fruit.

Today, don't rush to run for the Lord — first quietly return into him. Let his life flow again into the dried-up places within you, be strengthened, and then set out.

"Abide in me, and I in you." (John 15:4) Strength is not squeezed out of busyness, but drawn from staying connected to Him.

entries.title: 爱是恒久忍耐
entries.title_en: Love Is Patient
entries.verse: 哥林多前书十三章四至八节上
entries.content:
哥林多教会追求属灵恩赐,却彼此纷争、骄傲、缺乏爱。保罗在讲论恩赐之间,插入了这段被称为「爱的真谛」的话:「爱是恒久忍耐,又有恩慈;爱是不嫉妒,爱是不自夸,不张狂,不做害羞的事,不求自己的益处……凡事包容,凡事相信,凡事盼望,凡事忍耐。爱是永不止息」(林前13:4-8)。

我们常把这段话读成婚礼上的浪漫诗,但保罗写的其实是一面照妖镜。试着把每一句里的「爱」换成你的名字——「某某恒久忍耐,某某不求自己的益处」——你就会发现自己远远够不上。这段话不是先让我们感动,而是先让我们谦卑:唯有一位真正做到了这一切。

把「爱」换成「基督」,句句都成立。祂对我们恒久忍耐、不求自己的益处、凡事包容、永不止息。保罗后来在以弗所书说得更直白:「你们该效法神,好像蒙慈爱的儿女一样。也要凭爱心行事,正如基督爱我们,为我们舍了自己,当作馨香的供物和祭物,献与神」(弗5:1-2)。我们之所以能一点点学会这样去爱,不是靠咬牙效法一份高不可攀的标准,而是先被这样的爱充满、被这样的爱融化。先领受基督如此的爱,才生得出对人如此的爱。

默想:把这段经文里的「爱」换成我的名字,哪一句最扎心、最不像我?再换成「基督」,祂如此爱我,如何触动我?

应用:今天挑这段经文里的一个特质(如「不求自己的益处」或「恒久忍耐」),在一段具体关系里刻意实践出来。

祷告:主啊,这样的爱我实在做不到,唯有你做到了——你如此恒久忍耐、不求自己益处地爱了我,为我舍了自己,当作馨香的祭物。求你用你的爱先充满我、融化我,叫我因被你这样爱过,能一点一点这样去爱身边的人。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The Corinthian church pursued spiritual gifts, yet was full of strife, pride, and lacking in love. In the middle of his discussion of gifts, Paul inserts this passage known as "the love chapter": "Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way... Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never ends" (1 Corinthians 13:4-8).

We often read this passage as a romantic poem for weddings, but what Paul actually wrote is a mirror that exposes us. Try replacing "love" in each line with your own name — "so-and-so is patient, so-and-so does not insist on his own way" — and you’ll find yourself falling far short. This passage is not meant first to move us, but first to humble us: only one person has ever truly fulfilled all of this.

Replace "love" with "Christ," and every line holds true. He is patient with us, does not seek his own good, bears all things, never ends. Paul later put it even more plainly in Ephesians: "Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children. And walk in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God" (Ephesians 5:1-2). The reason we can gradually learn to love this way is not by gritting our teeth to imitate an unreachable standard, but by first being filled, first being melted, by love like this. Only by first receiving Christ’s love like this can we bring forth love like this for others.

Meditation: Replace "love" in this passage with my name — which line pierces me most, sounds least like me? Now replace it with "Christ" — how does his love for me like this move me?

Application: Today, pick one quality from this passage (like "does not seek its own good" or "is patient"), and deliberately practice it in one concrete relationship.

Prayer: Lord, I truly cannot love this way — only you have. You have loved me this patiently, not seeking your own good, giving yourself up for me as a fragrant offering. Fill me first with your love, melt me first, so that having been loved by you like this, I can, little by little, love those around me in the same way. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
