entries.title: 你们的劳苦不是徒然的
entries.title_en: Your Labor Is Not in Vain
entries.verse: 哥林多前书十五章五十八节
entries.content:
哥林多前书第十五章,保罗用整章郑重论证基督的复活,以及信徒将来身体复活的确据。他把这教义与我们的日常生活紧紧扣在一起,以一句实际的劝勉作结:「所以,我亲爱的弟兄们,你们务要坚固,不可摇动,常常竭力多做主工;因为知道,你们的劳苦在主里面不是徒然的」(林前15:58)。

请留意这句话的逻辑:「因为知道」。正因为基督已经复活、死亡已被吞灭、我们将来必要复活,所以今生一切为主而做的,都不会化为乌有。若没有复活,保罗说,信仰就是枉然,劳苦也就真是徒然;但既然复活是确实的,我们今天的每一分忠心、每一点摆上,都被存记在永恒里,绝不落空。

这对疲乏的人是极大的激励。我们服事,常感到看不见果效、无人看见、似乎白费力气。但复活的确据保证:在主里面的劳苦,没有一样是徒然的。希伯来书这样安慰那些觉得自己被忽略的人:「神并非不公义,竟忘记你们所做的工和你们为他名所显的爱心」(来6:10)。神都数算、都记念、都要在那日显明。所以「不可摇动,常常竭力多做主工」——不是靠自己硬撑,而是因着确知劳苦不徒然,而重新得力、站稳脚步。

默想:我是否因「看不见果效、无人看见」而在服事上灰心、想放弃?复活的确据——「劳苦不是徒然的」——如何重燃我的盼望?

应用:今天在一件你一直默默摆上、却看不见回报的事上,凭着「在主里劳苦不徒然」的确据,选择坚固、不摇动地继续。

祷告:主啊,因为你已经复活,我知道在你里面的劳苦没有一样是徒然的,你并非不公义,不会忘记我所做的工与所显的爱心。求你在我灰心、看不见果效的时候,用这确据坚固我,叫我不摇动,常常竭力多做主工,把一切摆上都交在你手中。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
In 1 Corinthians 15, Paul spends the entire chapter solemnly arguing for the resurrection of Christ, and the certainty of believers’ future bodily resurrection. He ties this doctrine tightly to our everyday lives, closing with a practical exhortation: "Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that in the Lord your labor is not in vain" (1 Corinthians 15:58).

Notice the logic of this sentence: "knowing that." Precisely because Christ has already risen, death has been swallowed up, and we too will certainly rise — everything done for the Lord in this life will never come to nothing. If there were no resurrection, Paul says, faith would be futile, and labor truly in vain; but since the resurrection is certain, every bit of our faithfulness today, every offering, is stored up in eternity, never wasted.

This is a tremendous encouragement to the weary. In serving, we often feel we see no results, that no one notices, that our effort seems wasted. But the certainty of the resurrection guarantees: labor in the Lord is never in vain. Hebrews comforts those who feel overlooked this way: "For God is not unjust so as to overlook your work and the love that you have shown for his name" (Hebrews 6:10). God counts it, remembers it, and will bring it to light on that day. So "be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord" — not by gritting your teeth to hold on alone, but by finding fresh strength and firm footing precisely because you know your labor is not in vain.

Meditation: Am I discouraged, wanting to give up in service, because "I see no results, no one notices"? How does the certainty of the resurrection — "labor is not in vain" — rekindle my hope?

Application: Today, in something you’ve been quietly offering with no visible return, hold on to the certainty that "labor in the Lord is not in vain," and choose to remain steadfast, immovable.

Prayer: Lord, because you have risen, I know that no labor in you is ever in vain — you are not unjust, and will not forget the work I have done and the love I have shown for your name. When I grow discouraged, seeing no results, strengthen me with this certainty, let me be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in your work, entrusting everything I offer into your hands. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 主的灵在哪里,那里就得自由
entries.title_en: Where the Spirit of the Lord Is, There Is Freedom
entries.verse: 哥林多后书三章十七节
entries.content:
保罗对比旧约与新约的职事,指出旧约的荣光会渐渐褪去,新约在圣灵里的荣光却越发增长。他说:「主就是那灵;主的灵在哪里,那里就得以自由」(林后3:17)。基督徒的生命,不是靠外面刻在石版上的律法勉强达标,而是靠里面那位圣灵活出来的自由。

倪柝声常强调:属灵生命的关键,在于「里面的灵」而非「外面的律」。律法能告诉你该做什么,却给不了你去做的能力,反倒常让人挫败、被定罪。保罗在罗马书里把这自由说得更精确:「赐生命圣灵的律,在基督耶稣里释放了我,使我脱离罪和死的律了」(罗8:2)——不是没有律,而是换了一个律:从「叫人知罪却无力的律法」,换成「赐生命、叫人得释放的圣灵的律」。这才是真自由:不是没有约束,而是里面有了活的生命去回应神。

保罗接着说,我们「就变成主的形状,荣上加荣,如同从主的灵变成的」(林后3:18)。这变化不是靠我们咬牙自我改造,而是当我们敞着脸、专注地注视主,圣灵一点一点地把我们模成祂的样式。所以成圣的秘诀,不是更用力,而是更亲近——转向主、注视主,让那住在里面的灵改变你。

默想:我追求改变,是更多靠「外面加规条、更用力」,还是靠「转向主、让里面的圣灵作工」?这两条路有何不同的结果?

应用:今天遇到自己「怎么也改不了」的软弱时,不再单靠意志硬压,而是安静转向主,求那住在你里面的圣灵释放你、改变你。

祷告:主啊,你就是那灵,你的灵在哪里,那里就得自由,你已用赐生命圣灵的律,释放我脱离罪和死的律。求你叫我不再靠外面的律苦苦挣扎,而是靠里面的圣灵活出生命。当我敞脸注视你时,求你用你的灵把我一点一点模成你的形状,荣上加荣。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul contrasts the ministry of the old covenant with the new, pointing out that the glory of the old covenant was fading away, while the glory of the new covenant in the Spirit only grows greater. He says: "Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom" (2 Corinthians 3:17). The Christian life is not lived by straining to meet a standard carved on stone tablets from outside, but by the freedom lived out from the Spirit within.

Watchman Nee often emphasized: the key to spiritual life lies in "the inner Spirit," not "the outer law." The law can tell you what to do, but cannot give you the power to do it — it more often leaves people frustrated, condemned. Paul, in Romans, states this freedom even more precisely: "the law of the Spirit of life has set me free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death" (Romans 8:2) — not that there is no law, but that one law has been exchanged for another: from "the law that reveals sin yet gives no power" to "the law of the Spirit of life, which sets free." This is true freedom: not the absence of restraint, but a living life within, able to respond to God.

Paul goes on to say that we "are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another, for this comes from the Lord who is the Spirit" (2 Corinthians 3:18). This transformation does not come by our gritting our teeth to remake ourselves, but as, with unveiled face, we gaze intently on the Lord, the Spirit shapes us little by little into his likeness. So the secret of sanctification is not trying harder, but drawing nearer — turning to the Lord, gazing on him, letting the Spirit who dwells within transform you.

Meditation: Do I pursue change more by "adding external rules, trying harder," or by "turning to the Lord, letting the inner Spirit work"? What different results do these two roads produce?

Application: Today, when you meet a weakness you "just can’t seem to change," don’t grit your teeth and force it alone — instead quietly turn to the Lord, and ask the Spirit who dwells within you to free you, to change you.

Prayer: Lord, you are the Spirit, and where your Spirit is, there is freedom; you have already, by the law of the Spirit of life, set me free from the law of sin and death. Let me stop struggling bitterly under the outer law, and instead live out life by the inner Spirit. As I gaze on you with unveiled face, transform me little by little, by your Spirit, into your likeness, from glory to glory. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 至暂至轻的苦楚
entries.title_en: A Light Momentary Affliction
entries.verse: 哥林多后书四章十六至十八节
entries.content:
保罗一生饱经患难——被打、下监、船难、饥渴。然而他却说:「所以,我们不丧胆。外体虽然毁坏,内心却一天新似一天。我们这至暂至轻的苦楚,要为我们成就极重无比、永远的荣耀」(林后4:16-17)。注意他怎样称呼自己所受的:「至暂至轻」。这不是因为他的苦小,而是因为他有一副永恒的天平。

秘诀在下一节:「原来我们不是顾念所见的,乃是顾念所不见的;因为所见的是暂时的,所不见的是永远的」(林后4:18)。保罗把今生的苦难,放在永恒的荣耀旁边一比——再重的患难,与那「极重无比、永远的荣耀」相比,就显得至暂至轻了。他在罗马书里也用同一副天平称量过:「我想,现在的苦楚若比起将来要显于我们的荣耀就不足介意了」(罗8:18)。这不是一时的安慰话,而是保罗一生反复使用、经过验证的属灵算法。

他不是否认痛苦,而是拒绝让痛苦成为衡量一切的最终标准。这不是逃避现实的自我安慰,而是被永恒真理校准过的眼光。当我们只盯着眼前所见的难处,苦难就显得压倒一切、遥遥无期;但当我们抬起眼来,顾念那所不见的、永远的荣耀,同样的患难就被放回它真实的比例里。今天,你的重担有多沉,取决于你把它放在哪一副天平上称。

默想:我衡量目前的难处,用的是「眼前所见」的天平,还是「永远所不见」的天平?若真信那荣耀「极重无比」,我今天的愁烦会有什么改变?

应用:今天为一个正压着你的难处,刻意花几分钟「顾念所不见的」——默想那永远的荣耀,让它重新校正你看待此刻的眼光。

祷告:主啊,求你给我一副永恒的天平。当患难压着我、看似遥遥无期时,叫我抬起眼来,顾念那所不见的、永远的荣耀。使我不丧胆,内心一天新似一天,深知这至暂至轻的苦楚,正为我成就极重无比的荣耀。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul’s whole life was full of hardship — beaten, imprisoned, shipwrecked, hungry and thirsty. Yet he said: "So we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day. For this light momentary affliction is preparing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison" (2 Corinthians 4:16-17). Notice how he names what he suffers: "light, momentary." Not because his sufferings were small, but because he weighed them on an eternal scale.

The secret is in the next verse: "as we look not to the things that are seen but to the things that are unseen. For the things that are seen are transient, but the things that are unseen are eternal" (2 Corinthians 4:18). Paul set this life’s hardship beside eternal glory and compared them — the heaviest hardship, next to that "eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison," appears light, momentary. He weighed things on that same scale in Romans as well: "I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us" (Romans 8:18). This wasn’t a momentary comforting phrase, but a spiritual calculus Paul used and tested throughout his whole life.

He doesn’t deny the pain — he refuses to let pain become the final measure of everything. This isn’t self-comforting denial of reality, but a vision calibrated by eternal truth. When we stare only at the difficulty right in front of us, suffering seems overwhelming, endless; but when we lift our eyes, looking to that unseen, eternal glory, the same hardship is placed back into its true proportion. Today, how heavy your burden feels depends on which scale you weigh it with.

Meditation: Am I measuring my current difficulty with the scale of "what is seen right now," or the scale of "the eternal unseen"? If I truly believed that glory is "beyond all comparison," how would my worry today change?

Application: Today, for something weighing on you, deliberately spend a few minutes "looking to the unseen" — meditate on that eternal glory, and let it recalibrate your view of this moment.

Prayer: Lord, give me an eternal scale. When hardship presses on me and seems endless, let me lift my eyes, looking to that unseen, eternal glory. Let me not lose heart, let my inner self be renewed day by day, knowing deeply that this light, momentary affliction is preparing for me an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 甘心乐意的施予
entries.title_en: Cheerful, Willing Giving
entries.verse: 哥林多后书九章六至七节
entries.content:
保罗鼓励哥林多教会为耶路撒冷的贫穷圣徒捐助,他讲出一条属灵的定律:「少种的少收,多种的多收……各人要随本心所酌定的,不要作难,不要勉强,因为捐得乐意的人是神所喜爱的」(林后9:6-7)。神所看重的,不只是我们给了多少,更是我们「怎样给」——是勉强挤出来,还是甘心乐意地献上。

「捐得乐意」的原文,是「欢喜、雀跃」的意思。神要的,不是一个咬牙割舍、心疼不已的奉献者,而是一个因给予而喜乐的人。主耶稣自己也说过同样的定律:「你们要给人,就必有给你们的,并且用十足的升斗,连摇带按,上尖下流地倒在你们怀里;因为你们用什么量器量给人,也必用什么量器量给你们」(路6:38)。这不是一句可以算计操控神的公式,而是提醒我们:紧抓与施予,各自结出不同的生命光景。

我们常常反过来——紧抓不放,因为怕给出去就少了、就不安全了。但保罗提醒:施予像撒种,不是失去,而是投入将来的收成;而那收成,神必按祂丰盛的恩典加给。今天的挑战是:不勉强、不作难,而是带着信心和喜乐,松开手,把神所赐的分给有需要的人。

默想:我奉献时,更多是「勉强、作难」,还是「甘心、乐意」?这背后反映出我对神供应的信心有多少?

应用:这周随本心酌定一份奉献或帮助,带着喜乐而非勉强去做,操练「捐得乐意」的心。

祷告:主啊,你是那位少种少收、多种多收,绝不亏待人的供应者。赦免我奉献时的勉强与不舍。求你坚固我对你供应的信心,叫我能甘心乐意、欢欢喜喜地施予,成为你所喜爱的捐献者。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul, encouraging the Corinthian church to give toward the poor saints in Jerusalem, states a spiritual law: "whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9:6-7). What God values is not just how much we give, but "how" we give — squeezed out reluctantly, or offered willingly and cheerfully.

"Cheerful" in the original means "joyful, delighted." What God wants is not a giver who grits their teeth and gives up something painfully, but someone who is joyful in giving. The Lord Jesus himself stated the same principle: "give, and it will be given to you, good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, will be put into your lap. For with the measure you use it will be measured back to you" (Luke 6:38). This isn’t a formula for calculating and manipulating God, but a reminder: clinging and giving each produce a different kind of life.

We often do the opposite — clinging tightly, afraid that giving away means having less, feeling less secure. But Paul reminds us: giving is like sowing seed, not loss, but investment in a future harvest; and that harvest, God will surely add according to his abundant grace. Today’s challenge is: don’t give reluctantly, under compulsion, but with faith and joy, open your hand, and share what God has given with those in need.

Meditation: When I give, is it more often "reluctant, under compulsion," or "willing, joyful"? What does this reflect about how much I trust God’s provision?

Application: This week, decide in your heart on one act of giving or help, and do it with joy rather than reluctance, practicing "giving cheerfully."

Prayer: Lord, you are the provider who never shortchanges anyone — sparing sowing, sparing harvest; bountiful sowing, bountiful harvest. Forgive me for my reluctance and clinging when I give. Strengthen my faith in your provision, let me give cheerfully and joyfully, becoming the kind of giver you love. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 我的恩典够你用
entries.title_en: My Grace Is Sufficient for You
entries.verse: 哥林多后书十二章九节
entries.content:
保罗有一根「身上的刺」,三次求主挪去,主却没有答应,只回答他:「我的恩典够你用的,因为我的能力是在人的软弱上显得完全。」保罗于是说:「我更喜欢夸自己的软弱,好叫基督的能力覆庇我……因我什么时候软弱,什么时候就刚强了」(林后12:9-10)。

这颠覆了我们对「蒙福」的想象。我们总以为,神帮助我们,就是挪去软弱、除掉难处、让我们变强。但主在这里说「不」——祂没有挪去那根刺,而是把祂的恩典赐够。原来神有时不除去我们的软弱,是要藉着软弱,让我们不再倚靠自己,转而经历祂那覆庇一切的能力。软弱本身,成了恩典进来的门。希伯来书说,历代因信而站立的人也曾「软弱变为刚强,争战显出勇敢」(来11:34)——那一次次,是神把软弱挪去、化为得胜。但保罗在这里经历的,是另一种同样真实的恩典:软弱并未被挪去,神的能力却仍在其中显得完全。有时神挪去软弱、赐下刚强;有时神留下软弱、却把祂自己赐下——两者都出于同一位又真又活的神。

这对每一个「有一根刺」的人是深深的安慰。你那始终没被挪去的难处、那反复挣扎的软弱、那你多次祈求却依旧存在的重担——也许神不是不听,而是要在其中给你更宝贵的东西:祂自己的能力与同在。今天,不必再为自己的软弱羞愧或假装刚强;把它带到主面前,让祂的恩典在那里显得完全。

默想:我心里那根「求主挪去却仍在」的刺是什么?我能否相信,神要藉着它,而不是绕过它,把祂的恩典赐给我?

应用:今天不再假装刚强,坦然把一个你一直遮掩的软弱交给主,并求祂的能力在其中覆庇你。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你说「我的恩典够你用」。当你没有挪去我的软弱时,求你叫我看见,你要在那软弱上显出你的能力,叫我软弱变为刚强。叫我不再靠自己逞强,而是甘心夸我的软弱,好让你的能力覆庇我,使我在软弱中因你刚强。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul had a "thorn in the flesh," and pleaded three times with the Lord to remove it, but the Lord did not grant it, only answering him: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Paul then said: "I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me... for when I am weak, then I am strong" (2 Corinthians 12:9-10).

This overturns our picture of being "blessed." We always assume that God helping us means removing weakness, taking away hardship, making us strong. But the Lord says "no" here — he did not remove the thorn, but gave grace sufficient for it. It turns out that sometimes God does not remove our weakness in order to let us, through that weakness, stop relying on ourselves, and instead experience his power that covers everything. Weakness itself becomes the door through which grace enters. Hebrews says that those who through the ages stood firm by faith also "were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war" (Hebrews 11:34) — those times, God removed the weakness, turning it into victory. But what Paul experiences here is another, equally real grace: the weakness was not removed, yet God’s power was still made perfect in it. Sometimes God removes the weakness and gives strength; sometimes God leaves the weakness, but gives us himself — both come from the same true and living God.

This is a deep comfort to everyone who has "a thorn." That difficulty that has never been removed, that recurring struggle, that burden you’ve prayed about many times and it’s still there — perhaps God is not refusing to listen, but wanting to give you something more precious through it: his own power and presence. Today, you don’t need to be ashamed of your weakness or pretend to be strong; bring it before the Lord, and let his grace be made perfect there.

Meditation: What is the "thorn" in my heart that I’ve asked the Lord to remove, yet is still there? Can I believe that God wants to give me his grace through it, rather than around it?

Application: Today, stop pretending to be strong, and openly hand over to the Lord a weakness you’ve been hiding, asking his power to cover you in it.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for saying "my grace is sufficient for you." When you have not removed my weakness, let me see that you want to display your power in that very weakness, turning my weakness into strength. Let me stop forcing my own strength, but willingly boast in my weakness, so that your power may rest on me, and I may be strong in you through my weakness. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 数算恩典
entries.title_en: Counting Your Blessings
entries.content:
数算恩典

「凡事谢恩;因为这是神在基督耶稣里向你们所定的旨意。」(帖撒罗尼迦前书 5:18)

感恩不是等一切顺利才有的心情,而是一种被恩典训练出来的眼光——在大事小事里,都认出那位赐恩者的手。数算恩典的尽头,是更深地以神自己为乐。

今天,安静下来,具体地为主这一周的恩惠一一感谢,然后抬起头,单单为着「赐下这一切的祂」而喜乐。

"Give thanks in all circumstances." (1 Thess 5:18) Count the gifts, then rejoice in the Giver.
entries.content_en:
Counting Your Blessings

"give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you." (1 Thessalonians 5:18)

Gratitude is not a mood that only comes once everything goes smoothly, but a way of seeing trained by grace — recognizing the hand of the Giver in matters great and small alike. The end point of counting your blessings is to delight even more deeply in God himself.

Today, be still, and give thanks specifically, one by one, for the Lord’s kindnesses this week, then lift up your eyes, and rejoice simply in "the one who gave all of this."

"Give thanks in all circumstances." (1 Thess 5:18) Count the gifts, then rejoice in the Giver.

entries.title: 圣灵的果子,是长出来的
entries.title_en: The Fruit of the Spirit Grows
entries.verse: 加拉太书五章廿二至廿三节，六章八至十节
entries.content:
加拉太书对比两种活法:随从「情欲」而活,或随从「圣灵」而行。保罗列出圣灵的果子:「仁爱、喜乐、和平、忍耐、恩慈、良善、信实、温柔、节制」(加5:22-23)。请留意,他用的是「果子」,不是「产品」。果子不是靠机器制造出来的,而是从有生命的树上,自然长出来的。

倪柝声常提醒我们:许多基督徒的挫败,在于想「制造」果子——咬牙让自己更有爱心、更有忍耐、更温柔,结果精疲力竭,徒有其表。但果子不是这样来的。它是当我们「顺着圣灵而行」、让圣灵的生命在里面运行时,自然结出来的。你不能靠使劲叫一棵树结果,你只能让它健康地连于根、吸取养分。保罗后来对腓立比教会所说的,正是这份信心的写照:「我深信那在你们心里动了善工的,必成全这工,直到耶稣基督的日子」(腓1:6)——动工、成全的,始终是神自己。

所以保罗接着说:「我们行善,不可丧志;若不灰心,到了时候就要收成……有了机会就当向众人行善」(加6:9-10)。一面,果子是圣灵长出来的,不靠我们苦苦制造;另一面,我们要恒切地顺着圣灵、行在善中,不灰心地让生命持续被浇灌。今天的功课,不是更用力挤出果子,而是更亲近那位赐生命的圣灵。

默想:我是在「制造」属灵的果子(靠意志硬撑),还是在「结出」果子(顺着圣灵、让生命流通)?我的疲惫,是否正来自前者?

应用:今天在你最缺乏的那样果子上(如忍耐或温柔),不靠自己硬挤,而是先安静求圣灵充满,再顺着祂去回应。

祷告:圣灵啊,果子是你在我里面结出来的,不是我制造的。赦免我常靠自己苦苦挣扎、徒然疲惫。求你充满我、在我里面运行,叫仁爱、喜乐、忍耐这些果子,从你的生命里自然长出来,深信你这动了善工的,必成全这工。也叫我行善不灰心,到了时候必要收成。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Galatians contrasts two ways of living: living according to "the flesh," or walking according to "the Spirit." Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit: "love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control" (Galatians 5:22-23). Notice, he uses the word "fruit," not "product." Fruit is not manufactured by machine, but grows naturally from a living tree.

Watchman Nee often reminds us: many Christians’ frustration lies in trying to "manufacture" fruit — gritting their teeth to make themselves more loving, more patient, more gentle, ending up exhausted, with only the appearance of it. But fruit doesn’t come this way. It grows naturally when we "walk by the Spirit," letting the Spirit’s life operate within us. You cannot force a tree to bear fruit by straining — you can only let it stay healthily connected to its root, drawing up nutrients. What Paul later said to the Philippian church is exactly a portrait of this kind of confidence: "he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:6) — it is always God himself who begins and completes the work.

So Paul goes on to say: "let us not grow weary of doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up... let us do good to everyone" (Galatians 6:9-10). On one hand, fruit is grown by the Spirit, not manufactured through our own struggling; on the other hand, we are to persist in walking by the Spirit, doing good, not growing discouraged, letting our life continue to be watered. Today’s lesson is not to squeeze out fruit harder, but to draw nearer to the Spirit who gives life.

Meditation: Am I "manufacturing" spiritual fruit (gritting my teeth through willpower), or "bearing" fruit (walking by the Spirit, letting life flow through)? Does my exhaustion come from the former?

Application: Today, in the fruit you lack most (like patience or gentleness), don’t force it out on your own — first quietly ask the Spirit to fill you, then respond by walking with him.

Prayer: Spirit, the fruit is grown by you within me, not manufactured by me. Forgive me for often struggling bitterly on my own, exhausted for nothing. Fill me, work within me, let love, joy, patience, and these other fruits grow naturally out of your life, believing deeply that you, who began this good work, will bring it to completion. And let me not grow weary in doing good, for in due season I will surely reap. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 你们得救是本乎恩,也因着信
entries.title_en: By Grace You Have Been Saved Through Faith
entries.verse: 以弗所书二章八至九节
entries.content:
以弗所书把福音的根基说得再清楚不过:「你们得救是本乎恩,也因着信;这并不是出于自己,乃是神所赐的;也不是出于行为,免得有人自夸」(弗2:8-9)。短短两节,把人一切自救、自夸的路都堵死了,只留下一条:白白的恩典,藉着信心领受。

「本乎恩」——救恩从头到尾是神的礼物,不是你挣来的工价。「也因着信」——你不是靠做够好去赚,而是靠伸手去接。「免得有人自夸」——神特意如此设计,好叫没有人能站在祂面前说「这是我的功劳」。保罗在罗马书里把这恩典的后果说得温暖:「我们既因信称义,就藉着我们的主耶稣基督得与神相和」(罗5:1)——这既击碎骄傲,也拆毁自卑:你无一点可夸,但你的被接纳也无关乎你够不够好,而是已经与神和好。

这与世上一切宗教和道德体系都不同。它们都说「做到,才能被接纳」;唯有福音说「你已被接纳,所以甘心去做」。前者叫人不是骄傲就是绝望——做得好就自义,做不好就自弃;后者叫人既谦卑又坦然。今天,若你仍在靠表现赚取神的爱,愿这两节释放你:得救本乎恩,不是出于你,是神所赐的。

默想:我心里是否仍暗暗靠「行为」在神面前记功、或因失败而记过?「本乎恩、因着信、不是出于自己」如何拆毁我的自义与自卑?

应用:今天当你想靠好表现证明自己、或因失败而觉得神远离你时,就默想这两节,重新安息在白白的恩典里。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你,我的得救本乎恩、因着信,全然是你白白的礼物,没有一点是我的功劳,又藉着基督使我与你相和。求你除去我靠行为自夸、或因失败自弃的心,叫我天天安息在你的恩典里,既不骄傲,也不绝望。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Ephesians states the foundation of the gospel as clearly as possible: "For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9). In just two verses, every road of self-salvation, self-boasting is blocked off, leaving only one: free grace, received through faith.

"By grace" — salvation, from beginning to end, is God’s gift, not wages you have earned. "Through faith" — you don’t earn it by being good enough, but receive it by reaching out your hand. "So that no one may boast" — God deliberately designed it this way, so that no one could stand before him and say "this is my own achievement." Paul, in Romans, states the warm consequence of this grace: "since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 5:1) — this both shatters pride and tears down self-loathing: you have nothing to boast of, but your acceptance also has nothing to do with whether you’re good enough — you have already been reconciled to God.

This is different from every religious and moral system in the world. They all say "do it, and then you’ll be accepted"; only the gospel says "you are already accepted, so you willingly do it." The former leads people to either pride or despair — do well and you become self-righteous, do poorly and you give up on yourself; the latter leads people to be both humble and at peace. Today, if you are still trying to earn God’s love through performance, may these two verses set you free: salvation is by grace, not from yourself, it is the gift of God.

Meditation: Deep in my heart, am I still secretly keeping score of my "works" before God, or keeping score of my failures? How does "by grace, through faith, not of yourselves" tear down both my self-righteousness and my self-loathing?

Application: Today, when you try to prove yourself through good performance, or feel God is distant because of failure, meditate on these two verses, and rest afresh in free grace.

Prayer: Lord, thank you — my salvation is by grace, through faith, entirely your free gift, with nothing of my own achievement in it, and through Christ you have reconciled me to you. Remove my tendency to boast in my works, or to give up on myself over failure, let me rest daily in your grace, neither proud nor despairing. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 一无挂虑,凡事交托
entries.title_en: Be Anxious for Nothing
entries.verse: 腓立比书四章六至七节
entries.content:
保罗在监狱中写下腓立比书,却满纸喜乐。他给焦虑之人一剂良方:「应当一无挂虑,只要凡事藉着祷告、祈求,和感谢,将你们所要的告诉神。神所赐、出人意外的平安,必在基督耶稣里保守你们的心怀意念」(腓4:6-7)。

请注意保罗没有说「别担心」就完了——那样的安慰苍白无力。他指出一条实际的出路:把挂虑「藉着祷告告诉神」。焦虑,本质上是把重担扛在自己肩上、反复在心里打转;祷告,则是把重担卸给那位掌管一切、又爱我们的天父。而且要「带着感谢」——感谢让我们的眼光从「我所缺的」转向「神所是、神所已赐的」。

结果是「出人意外的平安」。这平安不是因为问题解决了、前路明朗了,而是因为那位坐在宝座上的神亲自保守我们的心。保罗接着在同一封信里,交代了这平安落地生根的样子:「我无论在什么景况都可以知足,这是我已经学会了……我靠着那加给我力量的,凡事都能做」(腓4:11-13)。平安不是一时的情绪高峰,而是学来的、靠主而活的知足。

今天,与其让挂虑在心里空转,不如一样一样地带到神面前,用祷告和感谢,换取那超然的平安。

默想:我处理焦虑的方式,通常是自己反复打转,还是「藉着祷告告诉神」?我的祷告里,有没有「感谢」的成分?

应用:今天把心中挂虑的事一件一件具体地写下来,逐一交托给神,并为每一件找出一个可以感谢祂的理由。

祷告:主啊,我常把挂虑扛在自己肩上,反复愁烦。求你教我一无挂虑,凡事藉着祷告、祈求和感谢,把所要的告诉你。求你把那出人意外的平安赐给我,在基督耶稣里保守我的心怀意念,叫我学会靠你知足,凡事都能做。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul wrote Philippians from prison, yet the whole letter overflows with joy. He gives a remedy to the anxious: "do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus" (Philippians 4:6-7).

Notice, Paul doesn’t just say "don’t worry" and leave it there — such comfort would be hollow. He points to a practical way out: bring your anxieties "to God through prayer." Anxiety, at its core, is carrying a burden on your own shoulders, turning it over and over in your mind; prayer is handing that burden over to the Father who governs all things and loves us. And it must come "with thanksgiving" — gratitude turns our gaze from "what I lack" to "who God is, what God has already given."

The result is "peace that surpasses all understanding." This peace does not come because the problem is solved, because the path ahead is clear, but because the God seated on the throne personally guards our hearts. Paul, later in the same letter, describes what this peace looks like taking root: "I have learned, in whatever situation I am, to be content... I can do all things through him who strengthens me" (Philippians 4:11-13). Peace is not a momentary emotional high, but a learned contentment, lived out by relying on the Lord.

Today, rather than letting anxiety spin endlessly in your heart, bring it, one thing at a time, before God, exchanging it through prayer and thanksgiving for that transcendent peace.

Meditation: How do I usually handle anxiety — turning it over and over on my own, or "telling God through prayer"? Does my prayer include an element of "thanksgiving"?

Application: Today, write down, one by one, the concrete things weighing on your heart, entrust each one to God, and for each one find a reason to thank him.

Prayer: Lord, I often carry my anxieties on my own shoulders, worrying over and over. Teach me to be anxious for nothing, to make my requests known to you in everything through prayer, petition, and thanksgiving. Give me that peace which surpasses understanding, guarding my heart and mind in Christ Jesus, let me learn to be content in you, able to do all things through you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
entries.verse_text: 应当一无挂虑，只要凡事藉着祷告、祈求，和感谢，将你们所要的告诉 神。神所赐、出人意外的平安必在基督耶稣里保守你们的心怀意念。

entries.title: 存怜悯、恩慈、彼此饶恕
entries.title_en: Put On Compassionate Hearts, Kindness, and Forgive One Another
entries.verse: 歌罗西书三章十二至十三节
entries.content:
保罗描绘一个「在基督里」之人当有的样式:「所以,你们既是神的选民,圣洁蒙爱的人,就要存怜悯、恩慈、谦虚、温柔、忍耐的心。倘若这人与那人有嫌隙,总要彼此包容,彼此饶恕;主怎样饶恕了你们,你们也要怎样饶恕人」(西3:12-13)。「存」这个字,原文有「穿上」的意思——像每天早晨穿衣服一样,这些品格是我们要刻意「穿戴」的,不是碰运气、看心情。

怜悯、恩慈、谦虚、忍耐,不会在我们睡一觉后自动长出来;它们需要我们每天有意识地披戴上身,尤其在与人有摩擦、被冒犯、想要计较的时候。彼得后来提醒我们,这样的爱有它实际的果效:「最要紧的是彼此切实相爱,因为爱能遮掩许多的罪」(彼前4:8)。穿上怜悯与忍耐,不只是修养,更是在保护一段关系不被摩擦的碎片划破。

而饶恕的标准与动力,都是同一个:「主怎样饶恕了你们,你们也要怎样饶恕人。」我们能饶恕,不是因为对方配,也不是因为伤害不算什么,而是因为我们自己先被主赦免了那无法偿还的债。一个真正天天记得自己蒙了何等赦免的人,穿戴怜悯与饶恕,就不再是勉强的重担,而是感恩的回应。

默想:今早我「穿上」了什么?是怜悯、温柔、忍耐,还是不自觉地披上了计较、易怒、苛刻?此刻我与谁有「嫌隙」,是主要我去饶恕的?

应用:今天在一段有摩擦的关系里,刻意「穿上」一样品格(恩慈或忍耐),并向那位得罪你的人,踏出一步饶恕。

祷告:主啊,你既拣选我、爱我,又赦免了我无法偿还的债。求你叫我每天有意识地穿上怜悯、恩慈、谦虚、温柔、忍耐,尤其在被冒犯、想计较的时候,因为爱能遮掩许多的罪。因你怎样饶恕了我,叫我也怎样去饶恕人。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul describes what a person "in Christ" ought to look like: "Put on then, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience, bearing with one another and, if one has a complaint against another, forgiving each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive" (Colossians 3:12-13). The word "put on" in the original carries the sense of "clothing yourself" — like putting on clothes every morning, these character traits are things we must deliberately "wear," not leave to chance or mood.

Compassion, kindness, humility, and patience will not automatically grow in us after a night’s sleep; they require us to consciously clothe ourselves in them every day, especially when there’s friction with others, when we’re offended, when we want to keep score. Peter later reminds us that this kind of love has a real, practical effect: "above all, keep loving one another earnestly, since love covers a multitude of sins" (1 Peter 4:8). Putting on compassion and patience is not merely self-cultivation, but protects a relationship from being cut by the shards of friction.

And the standard and motivation for forgiveness are one and the same: "as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive." We are able to forgive, not because the other person deserves it, or because the hurt doesn’t matter, but because we ourselves were first forgiven by the Lord a debt we could never repay. A person who truly remembers every day how great a forgiveness they have received, in putting on compassion and forgiveness, no longer finds it a reluctant burden, but a grateful response.

Meditation: What did I "put on" this morning? Compassion, gentleness, patience — or, without realizing it, resentment, irritability, harshness? Who do I have a "complaint" against right now that the Lord wants me to forgive?

Application: Today, in a relationship with friction, deliberately "put on" one quality (kindness or patience), and take a step of forgiveness toward the person who has wronged you.

Prayer: Lord, you have chosen me and loved me, and forgiven me a debt I could never repay. Let me consciously put on compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience every day, especially when offended, when tempted to keep score, for love covers a multitude of sins. As you have forgiven me, let me also forgive others. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 要常常喜乐,不住祷告,凡事谢恩
entries.title_en: Rejoice Always, Pray Without Ceasing, Give Thanks in All Circumstances
entries.verse: 帖撒罗尼迦前书四章三节，五章十六至十八节
entries.content:
帖撒罗尼迦前书的末了,保罗接连给出几个简短却分量极重的命令:「要常常喜乐,不住地祷告,凡事谢恩;因为这是神在基督耶稣里向你们所定的旨意」(帖前5:16-18)。许多人苦苦寻求「神对我人生的旨意」,保罗却在这里直接告诉我们:这三样,就是神明明白白的旨意。

请注意这三个命令的绝对性:「常常」喜乐、「不住」祷告、「凡事」谢恩。它们不留例外、不设条件。这不是叫我们否认痛苦、假装快乐,而是提醒我们:喜乐、祷告、感恩的根据,不在于环境顺遂,而在于那位不改变的神。尼希米对着流泪认罪的百姓,也说过同样的话:「你们不要忧愁,因靠耶和华而得的喜乐是你们的力量」(尼8:10)——这喜乐不是靠环境挤出来的情绪,而是倚靠神本身所生出的力量。

而在这段之前,保罗也提到神旨意的另一面:「神的旨意就是要你们成为圣洁,远避淫行」(帖前4:3)。可见神的旨意,并非总是隐藏难测的「该去哪、该做什么」,更多是清楚明白的「该成为怎样的人」——圣洁、喜乐、常祷告、常感恩。与其焦虑于未知的引导,不如今天就顺服这些已知的旨意。

默想:我是否常把「寻求神的旨意」想成难测的谜,却忽略了祂已明说的旨意——喜乐、祷告、谢恩、圣洁?这三个「常常、不住、凡事」,我最缺哪一样?

应用:今天刻意操练这三样中你最缺的一样:在难处中找出可喜乐的、可感谢的,或在忙碌中不住地转向神祷告。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你把你的旨意清楚地摆在我面前——常常喜乐、不住祷告、凡事谢恩。赦免我常忽略这些已知的,却焦虑于未知的。求你叫我无论处境如何,都以你为喜乐、倚靠和感恩的根据,靠你而得的喜乐成为我的力量,活出你所定的旨意。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Toward the end of 1 Thessalonians, Paul gives, one after another, a few brief yet weighty commands: "Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you" (1 Thessalonians 5:16-18). Many people search anxiously for "God’s will for my life," but Paul tells us directly here: these three things are God’s clearly stated will.

Notice the absoluteness of these three commands: "always" rejoice, "without ceasing" pray, give thanks in "all" circumstances. They leave no exception, set no condition. This isn’t telling us to deny pain, to pretend to be happy, but reminds us: the basis of joy, prayer, and gratitude is not smooth circumstances, but the unchanging God. Nehemiah said the same thing to the people weeping in confession: "Do not be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength" (Nehemiah 8:10) — this joy is not an emotion squeezed out by circumstances, but strength that springs from relying on God himself.

And just before this passage, Paul also mentions another side of God’s will: "this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality" (1 Thessalonians 4:3). It’s clear God’s will is not always a hidden, hard-to-discern "where should I go, what should I do," but more often the clearly stated "what kind of person should I become" — holy, joyful, always praying, always thankful. Rather than being anxious about unknown guidance, why not obey today the will that is already known?

Meditation: Do I often think of "seeking God’s will" as an unsolvable riddle, while overlooking the will he has already clearly stated — joy, prayer, thanksgiving, holiness? Of these three "always, without ceasing, in all circumstances," which do I lack the most?

Application: Today, deliberately practice whichever of these three you lack most: find something to rejoice in or give thanks for amid difficulty, or turn to God in prayer without ceasing amid busyness.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for laying your will clearly before me — rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances. Forgive me for often overlooking what is already known, while being anxious about what is unknown. Let me, no matter my circumstances, take you as the basis for joy, dependence, and gratitude, let the joy I have in you become my strength, and let me live out the will you have set. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 行善不可丧志
entries.title_en: Do Not Grow Weary in Doing Good
entries.verse: 帖撒罗尼迦后书三章十三节
entries.content:
帖撒罗尼迦后书里,有些信徒因误解主的再来而懒散度日,保罗一面纠正,一面勉励忠心的人:「弟兄们,你们行善不可丧志」(帖后3:13)。这句短短的劝勉,道出了每个认真跟随主之人迟早会面对的一种疲惫——不是不知道该行善,而是行了许久、看不见回报,渐渐「丧志」、想放手。

行善之所以让人容易丧志,是因为它常常无人看见、无人感谢,甚至被误解、被利用。撒种的看不见立时的收成,服事的换不来对等的回报,坚持做对的事反而吃亏。在这样的时候,「丧志」是极自然的试探:何必呢?值得吗?再撑下去有意义吗?

但保罗的命令简单而坚定:不可丧志。因为我们行善,终极不是做给人看、等人回报,而是做在那位看得见、必不亏待人的主面前。希伯来书应许:「神并非不公义,竟忘记你们所做的工和你们为他名所显的爱心」(来6:10)。祂记念每一件在暗中所行的善,也应许「若不灰心,到了时候就要收成」(加6:9)。

今天若你正因行善疲乏、灰心,愿主坚固你:不要在离收成不远的地方松手,继续忠心地行善下去。

默想:我是否在某件「对的事、善的事」上,因看不见回报、无人看见而渐渐丧志、想放弃?是什么让我疲乏?

应用:今天在那件让你灰心的善事上,重新选择忠心做下去一步,并把它交给那位「必不亏待、到时收成」的主。

祷告:主啊,行善的路上我时常疲乏、想放手,尤其在无人看见、无回报的时候。求你坚固我的心,叫我行善不丧志。提醒我,我是做在你面前,你都看见、都记念,那生命的冠冕正为爱你的人存留。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
In 2 Thessalonians, some believers had grown idle due to a misunderstanding about the Lord’s return; Paul both corrects them and encourages the faithful: "brothers, do not grow weary in doing good" (2 Thessalonians 3:13). This short exhortation names a weariness every serious follower of the Lord will sooner or later face — not that they don’t know they should do good, but that having done it for a long time without seeing any return, they gradually "grow weary," wanting to let go.

Doing good easily leads to weariness precisely because it often goes unseen, unappreciated, even misunderstood, even exploited. The sower doesn’t see an immediate harvest, the servant doesn’t get a matching return, persisting in doing what’s right instead brings loss. In such moments, "growing weary" is an entirely natural temptation: what’s the point? Is it worth it? Is there any meaning in holding on?

But Paul’s command is simple and firm: do not grow weary. Because when we do good, ultimately it is not done for people to see, waiting for people to repay, but done before the Lord who sees, who will never shortchange anyone. Hebrews promises: "God is not unjust so as to overlook your work and the love that you have shown for his name" (Hebrews 6:10). He remembers every good deed done in secret, and also promises: "let us not grow weary of doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up" (Galatians 6:9).

If today you are weary, discouraged from doing good, may the Lord strengthen you: don’t let go when the harvest may not be far off — continue faithfully doing good.

Meditation: Am I gradually growing weary, wanting to give up, on some "right, good thing," because I see no return, no one notices? What is wearing me out?

Application: Today, take one more step of faithfulness in that good deed that discourages you, and entrust it to the Lord who "will never shortchange you, and whose harvest will come in due season."

Prayer: Lord, on the road of doing good I often grow weary, wanting to let go, especially when no one sees, when there’s no return. Strengthen my heart, let me not grow weary in doing good. Remind me that I do this before you, that you see it all, remember it all, and that crown of life is stored up for those who love you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
entries.verse_text: 弟兄们，你们行善不可丧志。

verse_parts.text: 弟兄们，你们行善不可丧志。

entries.title: 专注于神
entries.title_en: Focused on God
entries.content:
专注于神

「我将耶和华常摆在我面前,因他在我右边,我便不致摇动。」(诗篇 16:8)

倪柝声提醒我们:心思散乱、向外奔驰,是属灵生命最常见的漏洞。安息日,是把里面的眼睛重新对准主的时刻——不为别的,单单注视祂。

今天,放下手机与待办清单,让纷乱的心安静下来。把神常摆在你面前,单单亲近祂,让祂的同在重新校正你里面的焦点。

"I have set the Lord always before me." (Psalm 16:8) Quiet the scattered heart and fix your inward gaze on Him.
entries.content_en:
Focused on God

"I have set the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be shaken." (Psalm 16:8)

Watchman Nee reminds us: a scattered mind, running outward, is the most common leak in the spiritual life. The Sabbath is the moment to refocus our inward eyes on the Lord — for nothing else, simply gazing on him.

Today, set down your phone and your to-do list, and let your restless heart grow quiet. Set God always before you, simply drawing near to him, letting his presence recalibrate the focus within you.

"I have set the Lord always before me." (Psalm 16:8) Quiet the scattered heart and fix your inward gaze on Him.

entries.title: 基督到世上,为要拯救罪人
entries.title_en: Christ Jesus Came Into the World to Save Sinners
entries.verse: 提摩太前书一章十五节
entries.content:
保罗给年轻的提摩太写领袖手册,论到福音,他却先把自己摆进去:「基督耶稣降世,为要拯救罪人。这话是可信的,是十分可佩服的。在罪人中我是个罪魁」(提前1:15)。一位写了半部新约、开拓无数教会的使徒,竟称自己为「罪魁」——不是自谦的客套,而是他越靠近基督,越看清自己蒙的恩何等之大。

这里藏着一个属灵的吊诡:越成熟的基督徒,越深觉自己是罪人,也越惊叹于恩典。骄傲让人觉得自己还不错、比别人强;恩典却让人一面看清自己的败坏之深,一面看见神的爱之广。约翰说得直接:「我们若说自己无罪,便是自欺,真理不在我们心里了。我们若认自己的罪,神是信实的,是公义的,必要赦免我们的罪,洗净我们一切的不义」(约壹1:8-9)。保罗不是活在自卑的定罪里,而是活在「我这样的罪魁竟蒙拯救」的惊叹与感恩里,而这份坦然认罪,恰恰是他能持续支取赦免的管道。

这也拆毁了一个常见的错觉——以为信主久了,就该「不太算罪人」了。恰恰相反,真正的长进,是越来越诚实地承认自己需要恩典,也越来越被这恩典折服。今天,你不必假装自己已经很好;你可以像保罗一样坦然承认「我是个罪魁」,同时更大声地宣告「这话可信:基督降世,为要拯救罪人——包括我」。

默想:随着信主日子渐长,我是更看清自己需要恩典,还是渐渐觉得自己「还不错」?保罗自称「罪魁」,如何挑战我的自我评估?

应用:今天诚实地向神承认一处你一直不愿面对的软弱或罪,同时以「基督降世为要拯救罪人」宣告你所蒙的恩。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你——基督耶稣降世,为要拯救罪人,连我这样的罪魁也在其中。求你叫我不假装自己完美,也不困在自卑的定罪里,而是越认识你,越诚实认自己的罪,越看清自己的需要,也越惊叹你信实公义的赦免。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Writing a leadership manual for young Timothy, when Paul comes to the gospel, he puts himself into it first: "The saying is trustworthy and deserving of full acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost" (1 Timothy 1:15). An apostle who wrote half the New Testament and planted countless churches actually called himself "the foremost" of sinners — not modest politeness, but the closer he drew to Christ, the more clearly he saw how great a grace he had received.

Here lies a spiritual paradox: the more mature a Christian, the more deeply they feel themselves a sinner, and the more they marvel at grace. Pride makes people feel they’re doing fine, better than others; grace, on the other hand, makes people see both the depth of their own corruption and the breadth of God’s love. John states it plainly: "If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:8-9). Paul did not live under self-condemning shame, but in the wonder and gratitude of "even a foremost sinner like me being saved" — and this candid confession of sin is exactly the channel through which he could continue drawing on forgiveness.

This also tears down a common illusion — that after believing for a long time, one should "no longer be much of a sinner." Quite the opposite: true growth is becoming more and more honest about needing grace, and more and more overwhelmed by that grace. Today, you don’t need to pretend you’re already good; you can, like Paul, candidly confess "I am the foremost of sinners," while declaring even more loudly: "this saying is trustworthy: Christ came into the world to save sinners — including me."

Meditation: As the days since I believed grow longer, do I see more clearly my need for grace, or do I gradually feel I’m "doing fine"? How does Paul calling himself "the foremost" challenge my self-assessment?

Application: Today, honestly confess to God one weakness or sin you’ve been unwilling to face, while also declaring, over the grace you’ve received, "Christ came into the world to save sinners."

Prayer: Lord, thank you — Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, even a foremost sinner like me is included. Let me not pretend to be perfect, nor be trapped in self-condemning shame, but the more I know you, the more honestly I confess my sin, the more clearly I see my need, and the more I marvel at your faithful and righteous forgiveness. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 那美好的仗我已经打过了
entries.title_en: I Have Fought the Good Fight
entries.verse: 提摩太后书四章七至八节
entries.content:
提摩太后书是保罗的「遗言」,写于殉道前的监狱中。回望一生,他没有懊悔,也没有惧怕,只有一份忠心到底的坦然:「那美好的仗我已经打过了,当跑的路我已经跑尽了,所信的道我已经守住了。从此以后,有公义的冠冕为我存留」(提后4:7-8)。

保罗用了三个比喻总结自己的事奉。「打过了美好的仗」——信仰是一场需要争战、需要抵挡的属灵战役,他打到了最后。「跑尽了当跑的路」——不是跑得最快、最风光,而是跑到了终点、没有中途退场。「守住了所信的道」——在异端与逼迫中,他没有妥协、没有丢弃真理。忠心,不在于起步多热烈,而在于坚持到底。希伯来书告诉我们,这样的长跑从不是孤军奋战:「我们既有这许多的见证人,如同云彩围着我们,就当放下各样的重担……存心忍耐,奔那摆在我们前头的路程,仰望为我们信心创始成终的耶稣」(来12:1-2)。保罗跑尽了他的路程,眼睛所定睛的,始终是那位为他也为我们创始成终的主。

这向我们发出一个严肃又激励的问题:若今天是我人生的末了,我能不能说出这三句话?许多人起跑时满有热心,却在中途因疲乏、受伤、或世界的引诱而放慢、偏离、退场。保罗提醒我们:基督徒的一生是一场需要「守住」「跑尽」「打完」的长跑。而那位公义的主,已为一切忠心到底的人预备了冠冕。

默想:若今天是我人生的终点,我能说「仗打过了、路跑尽了、道守住了」吗?在这三方面,哪一样是我现在最需要重新得力、坚持到底的?

应用:今天为你的信仰长跑定一个「不退场」的具体决心——一个你近来想放松、想妥协、想退出的地方,选择守住。

祷告:主啊,求你叫我不只起步有热心,更能忠心到底——打完那美好的仗,跑尽当跑的路,守住所信的道。当我疲乏、受伤、想退场时,坚固我的心,叫我仰望你这位为我信心创始成终的主,一步一步跑到终点。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
2 Timothy is Paul’s "last words," written in prison before his martyrdom. Looking back on his life, he shows no regret, no fear, only the calm assurance of faithfulness to the end: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness" (2 Timothy 4:7-8).

Paul uses three metaphors to summarize his ministry. "Fought the good fight" — faith is a spiritual battle requiring struggle and resistance, and he fought it to the end. "Finished the race" — not running fastest or most gloriously, but reaching the finish line, not walking off midway. "Kept the faith" — amid heresy and persecution, he did not compromise, did not abandon the truth. Faithfulness is not measured by how enthusiastic the start was, but by whether one persevered to the end. Hebrews tells us that this kind of long race is never run alone: "since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight... let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith" (Hebrews 12:1-2). Paul finished his race with his eyes fixed always on that same Lord who was, for him and for us, the founder and perfecter of faith.

This poses a solemn yet inspiring question to us: if today were the end of my life, could I say these three things? Many people start out full of zeal, but slow down, drift, or drop out midway, worn out, wounded, or lured away by the world. Paul reminds us: the Christian life is a long race requiring us to "keep," "finish," and "fight" to the end. And that righteous Lord has already prepared a crown for all who are faithful to the end.

Meditation: If today were the end of my life, could I say "I have fought the fight, finished the race, kept the faith"? In these three areas, which do I most need renewed strength and perseverance in right now?

Application: Today, set one concrete resolve of "not dropping out" for your race of faith — one place you’ve recently wanted to ease up, compromise, or quit — choose to hold your ground.

Prayer: Lord, let me not only start with zeal, but be faithful to the end — fighting that good fight, finishing the race I’m to run, keeping the faith. When I’m weary, wounded, wanting to quit, strengthen my heart, let me look to you, the founder and perfecter of my faith, and run step by step to the finish line. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 在污秽人,什么都是污秽的
entries.title_en: To the Defiled, Nothing Is Pure
entries.verse: 提多书一章十五节
entries.content:
保罗差提多在道德败坏的克里特岛牧养教会,那里的人被形容为「说谎话、恶兽、贪食懒做」。面对这样一群看似「烂泥扶不上墙」的人,保罗指出问题的根源在人心:「在洁净的人,凡物都洁净;在污秽不信的人,什么都不洁净,连心地和天良也都污秽了」(多1:15)。问题不在外面的规条,而在里面的心。

这一针见血。人的败坏,不是靠换个环境、加些规矩就能解决的,因为污染的源头在心里——「连心地和天良也都污秽了」。同一件事物,在洁净的心里能被善用,在污秽的心里却被扭曲。所以真正的改变,必须从心开始;而唯有福音的恩典,能够洁净、更新一颗污秽的心。神早藉以西结应许过这样的手术:「我也要赐给你们一个新心,将新灵放在你们里面,又从你们的肉体中除掉石心,赐给你们肉心」(结36:26)。这原是向以色列所说的应许,但新约让我们看见,这更新之工藉着基督临到一切因信蒙恩的人(参林后三3);提多书里那些说谎、贪食懒做的克里特人,也正在恩典中经历这新心的更新。

但保罗写提多书,恰恰是要证明:恩典能改变最没指望的人。他说神的恩典「教训我们除去不敬虔的心和世俗的情欲,在今世自守、公义、敬虔度日」(多2:12)。没有一种人是恩典所改变不了的——再「烂」的泥,在神手中也能被重塑。这既叫我们对自己不灰心,也叫我们不轻易放弃任何一个人。

默想:我是否曾把某些人(或某个自己)看作「没救了、改不了」?「恩典能洁净人心」这真理,如何改变我看待他们、看待自己的眼光?

应用:为一个你几乎已经「放弃指望」的人(或自己的一个顽固软弱)祷告,求神用祂改变人心的恩典动工,并对他/自己重燃盼望。

祷告:主啊,你知道我的问题根在人心,不是换个环境就能解决的。求你照你古时的应许,除掉我的石心,赐给我肉心,用你的恩典洁净我里面污秽的心。也求你叫我不轻看任何人,深信没有一块泥是你的恩典重塑不了的——包括我自己。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Paul sent Titus to shepherd a church on the morally corrupt island of Crete, where the people were described as "liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons." Facing such a group who seemed like "mud too far gone to be shaped," Paul points to the root of the problem in the human heart: "To the pure, all things are pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their minds and their consciences are defiled" (Titus 1:15). The problem is not in outward rules, but in the heart within.

This cuts straight to the point. Human corruption cannot be solved by changing environments or adding more rules, because the source of pollution is in the heart — "both their minds and their consciences are defiled." The very same thing, in a pure heart, can be used well; in a defiled heart, it is twisted. So true change must begin from the heart; and only the grace of the gospel can cleanse and renew a defiled heart. God long ago, through Ezekiel, promised this very surgery: "I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh" (Ezekiel 36:26). This promise was originally spoken to Israel, but the New Testament lets us see that this work of renewal comes, through Christ, to all who receive grace by faith (see 2 Corinthians 3:3) — those lying, gluttonous, lazy Cretans in Titus were also, in grace, experiencing the renewal of this new heart.

But Paul wrote Titus precisely to prove: grace can change even the most hopeless people. He says God’s grace "trains us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age" (Titus 2:12). There is no kind of person grace cannot change — no mud so far gone that it cannot be reshaped in God’s hands. This both keeps us from despairing over ourselves, and keeps us from easily giving up on anyone.

Meditation: Have I ever regarded certain people (or myself) as "beyond hope, unable to change"? How does the truth that "grace can cleanse the heart" change how I see them, how I see myself?

Application: Pray for someone you’ve nearly "given up hope on" (or one of your own stubborn weaknesses), asking God to work through his heart-changing grace, and rekindle hope for them or for yourself.

Prayer: Lord, you know my problem is rooted in the heart, not something a change of environment can fix. According to your ancient promise, remove my heart of stone, give me a heart of flesh, and cleanse the defiled heart within me with your grace. Let me not look down on anyone, believing deeply that there is no mud your grace cannot reshape — including myself. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 在信仰上彼此相通
entries.title_en: Fellowship in the Faith
entries.verse: 腓利门书一章六节
entries.content:
腓利门书是一封私人短信。保罗为一个逃跑的奴隶阿尼西母求情,盼望他的主人腓利门能重新接纳这位如今已信主的弟兄。信中,保罗为腓利门祷告:「愿你与人所同有的信心显出功效,使人知道你们各样善事都是为基督做的」(门6)。门徒生命的标志之一,就是「彼此相通」的信心——信仰从不是各人自扫门前雪的私事。

倪柝声常强调:基督徒的生命是「身体」的生命,不是单独一粒麦子的生命。保罗在罗马书里也这样描绘教会:「我们这许多人,在基督里成为一身,互相联络作肢体,也是如此」(罗12:5)。我们同信一位主、同有一个生命,彼此之间就有一种真实的「相通」——你的信心影响我,我的爱心造就你;一个肢体的软弱牵动全身,一个肢体的刚强也扶持众人。腓利门如何对待阿尼西母,不是他一个人的家务事,而关乎整个信心团契的见证。

这挑战了现代人「我和神的关系是我私人的事」的想法。真实的属灵生命,必然活在与弟兄姊妹的相通里——彼此接纳、彼此饶恕、彼此担当、彼此造就。今天,你的信心若真是活的,就会「显出功效」,流通到身边的肢体中,成为别人的祝福。

默想:我是否把信仰当作「我与神之间的私事」,活得与弟兄姊妹相当疏离?我的信心,近来有没有「显出功效」、成为别人的祝福?

应用:今天主动向一位弟兄姊妹「相通」一步——分享你的信心、接纳一个曾亏欠你的人,或在实际需要上担当他的重担。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你把我放进你身体的相通里,与众肢体互相联络,而非孤单独行。求你叫我与人所同有的信心显出功效,不把信仰锁在私人的角落,而是流通到弟兄姊妹中间——彼此接纳、担当、造就,一同为你而活。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Philemon is a short, personal letter. Paul pleads on behalf of a runaway slave, Onesimus, hoping that his master Philemon might receive back this brother, now a believer. In the letter, Paul prays for Philemon: "that the sharing of your faith may become effective for the full knowledge of every good thing that is in us for the sake of Christ" (Philemon 6). One mark of a disciple’s life is exactly this faith that is "shared with" others — faith is never a private matter of each person sweeping the snow off their own doorstep.

Watchman Nee often emphasized: the Christian life is the life of the "body," not the life of a single, isolated grain of wheat. Paul, in Romans, describes the church the same way: "so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another" (Romans 12:5). We share the same Lord, the same life, and between us there is a real "sharing" — your faith affects me, my love builds you up; one member’s weakness affects the whole body, and one member’s strength supports everyone. How Philemon treats Onesimus is not merely his own private family matter, but concerns the witness of the entire fellowship of faith.

This challenges the modern idea that "my relationship with God is my own private business." Real spiritual life must be lived out in fellowship with brothers and sisters — accepting one another, forgiving one another, bearing one another’s burdens, building one another up. Today, if your faith is truly alive, it will "become effective," flowing to the members around you, becoming a blessing to others.

Meditation: Do I treat faith as "a private matter between me and God," living rather distantly from brothers and sisters? Has my faith lately "become effective," becoming a blessing to others?

Application: Today, proactively take one step of "sharing" toward a brother or sister — share your faith, accept someone who has wronged you, or bear their burden in a concrete need.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for placing me into the fellowship of your body, connected with all the members, not walking alone. Let the faith I share with others become effective, not locking my faith away in a private corner, but letting it flow among brothers and sisters — accepting, bearing, building up one another, living for you together. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 祂能体恤我们的软弱
entries.title_en: He Sympathizes with Our Weaknesses
entries.verse: 希伯来书四章十五节
entries.content:
希伯来书把耶稣描绘为超越天使、超越摩西的至高之主;但就是这位至高的大祭司,却与我们如此贴近:「因我们的大祭司并非不能体恤我们的软弱。他也曾凡事受过试探,与我们一样,只是他没有犯罪」(来4:15)。祂高过诸天,却曾走过我们所走的每一步。以赛亚早就预言了这位受苦的仆人:「他被藐视,被人厌弃,多受痛苦,常经忧患」(赛53:3)。祂的体恤不是理论,而是亲历。

「体恤」意味着感同身受。耶稣不是一位高高在上、对我们的挣扎无动于衷的神;祂曾亲身经历饥饿、疲乏、被弃、被试探——凡我们所受的,祂都受过,只是祂从未跌倒。所以当你软弱、挣扎、被试探煎熬时,你所来到的,不是一位冷漠的审判官,而是一位完全懂你的大祭司。

正因如此,作者接着发出邀请:「所以,我们只管坦然无惧地来到施恩的宝座前,为要得怜恤,蒙恩惠,作随时的帮助」(来4:16)——「坦然无惧」。软弱的时候,我们的本能是躲藏、是远离神;但福音说,恰恰在软弱时,你可以坦然地、放胆地来,因为宝座上坐着的,是那位体恤你、又满有恩典的主。

默想:我软弱、失败的时候,是躲避神,还是坦然来到祂面前?「祂能体恤我的软弱」如何改变我亲近神的方式?

应用:今天把一个你羞于启齿、一直独自硬扛的软弱或试探,坦然无惧地带到主面前,向这位体恤你的大祭司求怜恤与帮助。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你虽是至高的大祭司,却凡事受过试探,被藐视、被厌弃,能体恤我的软弱。求你除去我软弱时躲避你的倾向,叫我坦然无惧地来到你施恩的宝座前,得着怜恤、恩惠,作我随时的帮助。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Hebrews portrays Jesus as the Lord exalted above angels, above Moses; but it is exactly this exalted High Priest who is so close to us: "For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tempted as we are, yet without sin" (Hebrews 4:15). He is higher than the heavens, yet he has walked every step we walk. Isaiah long ago prophesied this suffering Servant: "He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief" (Isaiah 53:3). His sympathy is not theory, but firsthand experience.

"Sympathize" means to feel what another feels. Jesus is not a God lofty and detached, indifferent to our struggles; he personally experienced hunger, exhaustion, abandonment, temptation — everything we suffer, he suffered too, only he never fell. So when you are weak, struggling, tormented by temptation, the one you come to is not a cold judge, but a High Priest who fully understands you.

Precisely because of this, the writer goes on to extend an invitation: "Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need" (Hebrews 4:16) — "with confidence." In weakness, our instinct is to hide, to withdraw from God; but the gospel says that precisely in weakness, you can come boldly, confidently, because seated on the throne is the Lord who sympathizes with you, and is full of grace.

Meditation: When I am weak, when I fail, do I avoid God, or come confidently before him? How does "he can sympathize with my weakness" change the way I draw near to God?

Application: Today, bring a weakness or temptation you’re ashamed to speak of, one you’ve been carrying alone, confidently before the Lord, and ask this sympathizing High Priest for mercy and help.

Prayer: Lord, thank you that though you are the exalted High Priest, you were tempted in every respect, despised and rejected, able to sympathize with my weakness. Remove my tendency to hide from you when weak, let me come with confidence to your throne of grace, receiving mercy, grace, and help in my time of need. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 合乎我们所需要的大祭司
entries.title_en: A High Priest Who Meets Our Need
entries.verse: 希伯来书七章廿六节
entries.content:
希伯来书郑重论证:基督是照着麦基洗德的等次、永远长存的大祭司,远超旧约那些必死、必被更替的祭司。作者总结说:「像这样圣洁、无邪恶、无玷污、远离罪人、高过诸天的大祭司,原是与我们合宜的」(来7:26)。每一个描述,都在宣告祂的全然圣洁与完美。

旧约的大祭司,自己也是罪人,每年赎罪日先要为自己的罪献祭,才能为百姓献祭;他们必死,一个接一个地被更替。但基督不然——祂无罪、无瑕、永远长存。正因祂自己毫无亏欠,祂所献上的赎罪祭才完全有效;正因祂永远活着,祂就「能拯救到底」,并且「长远活着,替他们祈求」(来7:25)。保罗在罗马书里也这样发问:「谁能定他们的罪呢?有基督耶稣已经死了,而且从死里复活,现今在神的右边,也替我们祈求」(罗8:34)——从希伯来书到罗马书,新约反复见证同一个事实:那升天的主,此刻仍在为你我代求。

这给信徒何等的稳妥。我们的得救,不倚靠一位会犯错、会死去的中保,而倚靠一位圣洁、完美、永远长存的大祭司。祂一次献上自己,就永远成就了救赎;祂如今在天上,不住地为你我代求。今天你若为自己的失败而不安,请记得:你的中保是那位「合乎你所需要」的完美大祭司,祂必拯救你到底。

默想:我的确据,是建立在自己的表现上,还是建立在那位圣洁、完美、永远长存、替我代求的大祭司身上?这两者带来的安全感有何不同?

应用:今天当罪咎或失败让你不安时,把眼光从自己转向基督——那位完美的大祭司,默想祂如今正在为你代求。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你是那位圣洁、无瑕、永远长存的大祭司,正合我所需,如今在父的右边也替我祈求。我的得救不靠自己,而靠你一次献上的完全救赎和永不止息的代求。求你叫我安息在你里面,深知你能拯救我到底。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Hebrews solemnly argues: Christ is a High Priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek, far surpassing those Old Testament priests who were mortal and had to be replaced. The writer sums it up: "For it was indeed fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, innocent, unstained, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens" (Hebrews 7:26). Every description proclaims his complete holiness and perfection.

The Old Testament high priest was himself a sinner, needing to offer a sacrifice for his own sin every Day of Atonement before he could offer for the people; they were mortal, replaced one after another. But Christ is not so — he is sinless, spotless, eternal. Precisely because he himself owed no debt, the atoning sacrifice he offered is completely effective; precisely because he lives forever, he is "able to save to the uttermost," and "always lives to make intercession for them" (Hebrews 7:25). Paul asks the same question in Romans: "Who is to condemn? Christ Jesus is the one who died — more than that, who was raised — who is at the right hand of God, who indeed is interceding for us" (Romans 8:34) — from Hebrews to Romans, the New Testament repeatedly bears witness to the same fact: that ascended Lord is, at this very moment, still interceding for you and me.

This gives believers tremendous security. Our salvation does not rest on a mediator who can err, who can die, but on a holy, perfect, eternal High Priest. He offered himself once, and accomplished redemption forever; he is now in heaven, ceaselessly interceding for you and me. If today you are troubled by your own failure, remember: your mediator is that perfect High Priest "exactly fitted to your need," and he will save you to the uttermost.

Meditation: Is my assurance built on my own performance, or on that holy, perfect, eternal High Priest who intercedes for me? What difference in security do these two produce?

Application: Today, when guilt or failure unsettles you, turn your gaze from yourself to Christ — that perfect High Priest — and meditate on the fact that he is right now interceding for you.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for being that holy, spotless, eternal High Priest, exactly fitting my need, now at the Father’s right hand interceding for me. My salvation does not rest on myself, but on your once-for-all, complete redemption and your never-ending intercession. Let me rest in you, knowing deeply that you can save me to the uttermost. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 安息与更新
entries.title_en: Rest and Renewal
entries.content:
安息与更新

「你们要休息,要知道我是神。」(诗篇 46:10)

真正的安息,是停止靠自己去证明、去挣得。基督已在十字架上说了「成了」;你不必再靠今天的表现来换取神的接纳。安息,就是相信祂的工作已经完成。

今天,把想要掌控一切、想要达标的心放下来。你是神所爱、已被称义的儿女——在祂已成就的工作里歇息,让祂的爱更新你。

"Be still, and know that I am God." (Psalm 46:10) Rest is ceasing to earn what Christ has already finished.
entries.content_en:
Rest and Renewal

"Be still, and know that I am God." (Psalm 46:10)

True rest is ceasing to prove yourself, to earn your way, by your own effort. Christ has already said "It is finished" on the cross; you no longer need today’s performance to purchase God’s acceptance. Rest is believing that his work is already complete.

Today, lay down that heart that wants to control everything, wants to measure up. You are God’s beloved, already-justified child — rest in the work he has already accomplished, and let his love renew you.

"Be still, and know that I am God." (Psalm 46:10) Rest is ceasing to earn what Christ has already finished.

entries.title: 祂永不撇下你,所以你可以知足
entries.title_en: He Will Never Leave You, So You Can Be Content
entries.verse: 希伯来书十三章四至八节
entries.content:
希伯来书讲完基督远超旧约的救赎,便转向实际的生活,其中一段谈到知足:「你们存心不可贪爱钱财,要以自己所有的为足;因为主曾说:我总不撇下你,也不丢弃你」(来13:5)。注意这里知足的根据——不是「钱够多」,而是「主永不撇下」。真正的安全感,不在银行的余额,而在神不变的同在。

贪爱钱财的背后,常是一种深层的恐惧:怕将来没保障、怕被撇下、怕不够。我们以为多积攒一点就多一分安稳,于是永远觉得不够。但神在这里釜底抽薪地医治这恐惧:祂说「我总不撇下你」。保罗给提摩太的劝勉,正是这份知足的具体样式:「敬虔加上知足的心便是大利了;因为我们没有带什么到世上来,也不能带什么去。只要有衣有食,就当知足」(提前6:6-8)。若那位掌管万有、又爱你的神应许永不离开,你还需要靠积攒来对抗那份「怕被撇下」的不安吗?

紧接着,作者宣告那位永不改变的主:「耶稣基督昨日、今日、一直到永远,是一样的」(来13:8)。世事变迁、财富起落、人会离开,唯有祂始终如一。把安全感押在会变的东西上,人就永不知足、永在焦虑;把安全感扎根在这位永不改变、永不撇下你的主身上,人才能真正知足、坦然。

默想:我的安全感,更多押在「所拥有的」上,还是押在「主永不撇下我」的应许上?我的不知足,是否正暴露出一份怕被撇下的恐惧?

应用:今天当「不够、想多要」的焦虑升起时,就以「主总不撇下我」向自己宣告,操练在所有的里面知足。

祷告:主啊,你应许总不撇下我、也不丢弃我,你昨日、今日、直到永远都不改变。求你医治我那怕被撇下、总觉不够的心,叫我不再把安全感押在会变的钱财上,而是扎根在你不变的同在里,存敬虔知足的心,以所有的为足。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Having finished explaining how Christ’s redemption far surpasses the Old Testament, Hebrews turns to practical living, one passage speaking of contentment: "Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, ‘I will never leave you nor forsake you’" (Hebrews 13:5). Notice the basis of contentment here — not "having enough money," but "the Lord will never leave." True security is not in a bank balance, but in God’s unchanging presence.

Behind the love of money often lies a deep fear: fear of no security in the future, fear of being abandoned, fear of not having enough. We think that saving a little more gives a little more security, and so we always feel it’s not enough. But God here strikes at the root of this fear: he says "I will never leave you." Paul’s exhortation to Timothy is exactly a concrete picture of this contentment: "godliness with contentment is great gain, for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out of the world. But if we have food and clothing, with these we will be content" (1 Timothy 6:6-8). If the God who governs all things and loves you promises never to leave, do you still need to rely on saving up to fight that anxiety of "fear of being abandoned"?

Immediately following, the writer declares this never-changing Lord: "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever" (Hebrews 13:8). Circumstances change, wealth rises and falls, people leave — only he remains constant. Pin your security on things that change, and you will never be content, always anxious; root your security in this never-changing Lord who will never leave you, and you can be truly content, truly at peace.

Meditation: Is my security pinned more on "what I have," or on the promise that "the Lord will never leave me"? Does my discontent expose a fear of being abandoned?

Application: Today, when the anxiety of "not enough, wanting more" rises up, declare to yourself "the Lord will never leave me," practicing contentment in all things.

Prayer: Lord, you have promised to never leave me, never forsake me, you are the same yesterday, today, and forever. Heal my heart that fears abandonment, that always feels it’s not enough, let me no longer pin my security on money that can change, but root it in your unchanging presence, holding a godly, contented heart, content with what I have. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
entries.verse_text: 婚姻，人人都当尊重，床也不可污秽；因为苟合行淫的人， 神必要审判。你们存心不可贪爱钱财，要以自己所有的为足；因为主曾说：「我总不撇下你，也不丢弃你。」所以我们可以放胆说： 主是帮助我的，我必不惧怕； 人能把我怎么样呢？从前引导你们、传 神之道给你们的人，你们要想念他们，效法他们的信心，留心看他们为人的结局。耶稣基督昨日、今日、一直到永远，是一样的。

entries.title: 管教的果子,是平安的义
entries.title_en: The Fruit of Discipline Is the Peaceful Fruit of Righteousness
entries.verse: 希伯来书十二章十一至十三节
entries.content:
希伯来书的读者正经历患难,作者提醒他们,患难中有神慈爱的管教:「凡管教的事,当时不觉得快乐,反觉得愁苦;后来却为那经练过的人结出平安的果子,就是义」(来12:11)。神管教祂的儿女,不是出于恼怒的惩罚,而是出于慈父的爱,为要我们「在他的圣洁上有分」(来12:10)。

这节经文诚实地承认:管教「当时不觉得快乐,反觉得愁苦」。神没有粉饰痛苦的真实。但祂让我们看见痛苦背后的目的——「后来却……结出平安的义果」。就像运动员经过严格操练才有实力,信徒也是经过神的雕琢、修剪、熬炼,才结出成圣的果子。保罗说得更全面:「我们晓得万事都互相效力,叫爱神的人得益处……因为他预先所知道的人,就预先定下效法他儿子的模样」(罗8:28-29)——管教所结的「义」,最终的形状,是像基督。关键在那个「后来」:管教的果子,往往不在当下显明,而在忍耐经历之后。

所以作者劝勉:「你们要把下垂的手、发酸的腿挺起来;也要为自己的脚,把道路修直了」(来12:12-13)。在管教中,自然的反应是灰心、埋怨、想逃;但神要我们挺起身来,把它当作慈父的雕琢来领受,而非命运的打击来抗拒。今天你所受的熬炼,若是出于神的手,就必不徒然——它正在你里面结出平安的义。

默想:我是否把目前的难处只当作「倒霉、打击」,而没有想过其中可能有神慈爱的管教?我在管教中的反应,是灰心逃避,还是「挺起下垂的手」?

应用:今天为一个正在熬炼你的难处祷告,求神让你看见祂借此要在你里面成就的「义」,并选择挺起身来、领受而非抗拒。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你如同慈父,藉着管教叫我在你的圣洁上有分,叫万事都互相效力,使我效法你儿子的模样。求你在我愁苦、想逃避的时候,帮助我把下垂的手挺起来,把管教当作你爱的雕琢来领受。求你在我身上结出那平安的义果。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
The readers of Hebrews were undergoing hardship, and the writer reminds them that within hardship is God’s loving discipline: "For the moment all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it" (Hebrews 12:11). God disciplines his children, not out of angry punishment, but out of a loving Father’s heart, that we might "share his holiness" (Hebrews 12:10).

This verse honestly admits: discipline "for the moment seems painful rather than pleasant." God does not paint over the reality of pain. But he lets us see the purpose behind the pain — "later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness." Just as an athlete gains strength only through rigorous training, believers, too, bear the fruit of sanctification only through God’s shaping, pruning, and refining. Paul says it even more fully: "we know that for those who love God all things work together for good... For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Romans 8:28-29) — the "righteousness" that discipline produces ultimately takes the shape of Christ. The key is that word "later": the fruit of discipline is often not visible in the moment, but after patient endurance.

So the writer exhorts: "Therefore lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees, and make straight paths for your feet" (Hebrews 12:12-13). The natural reaction in discipline is discouragement, complaint, wanting to flee; but God wants us to stand up straight, receiving it as a loving Father’s shaping rather than resisting it as fate’s blow. If the refining you undergo today comes from God’s hand, it will surely not be in vain — it is producing the peaceful fruit of righteousness within you.

Meditation: Do I treat my current difficulty only as "bad luck, a blow," without considering that it might contain God’s loving discipline? Is my response to discipline discouraged avoidance, or "lifting my drooping hands"?

Application: Today, pray about a difficulty currently refining you, asking God to let you see the "righteousness" he wants to accomplish in you through it, and choose to stand up and receive it rather than resist it.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for, like a loving Father, disciplining me so that I share in your holiness, causing all things to work together, conforming me to the image of your Son. When I am sorrowful, wanting to flee, help me lift my drooping hands, receiving discipline as your loving shaping. Bear in me that peaceful fruit of righteousness. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 清洁没有玷污的虔诚
entries.title_en: Pure and Undefiled Religion
entries.verse: 雅各书一章廿六至廿七节
entries.content:
雅各书素来直白、扎心。论到「真信心」,他毫不客气地拆穿一种自欺:「若有人自以为虔诚,却不勒住他的舌头,反欺哄自己的心,这人的虔诚是虚的。」接着他给「真虔诚」下了一个出人意料的定义:「在神我们的父面前,那清洁没有玷污的虔诚,就是看顾在患难中的孤儿寡妇,并且保守自己不沾染世俗」(雅1:26-27)。

请注意雅各衡量虔诚的标准,不是聚会有多勤、知识有多丰、话讲得多属灵,而是两件极其具体的事:一,「看顾孤儿寡妇」——去关怀那些无依无靠、无力回报你的人;二,「保守自己不沾染世俗」——在价值观和生活方式上不随波逐流。真信心,不是停在头脑和口舌,而是落在手脚和生活。主耶稣在讲绵羊山羊的比喻时,用的正是同一套标准:「我饿了,你们给我吃,渴了,你们给我喝……我在监里,你们来看我」(太25:35-36)——祂衡量的,同样是这些具体、卑微、容易被忽略的关怀。

这对我们是一记警钟。我们太容易把「虔诚」等同于宗教活动,却对身边的孤苦无动于衷;太容易在教会里显得属灵,却在生活方式上与世界毫无分别。雅各提醒我们:能证明信心是真的,不是我们说了什么、信了什么,而是我们的信心有没有走出去,触摸到那些困苦的人。

默想:我衡量自己「虔诚」的标准,是宗教活动的多少,还是雅各所说的——看顾困苦的人、不沾染世俗?我的信心,有没有落到手脚上?

应用:这周具体地「看顾」一个在患难中、无力回报你的人——探访、帮补、或实际的陪伴,让信心长出手脚。

祷告:主啊,赦免我常把虔诚等同于宗教活动,却对身边的孤苦漠不关心。求你叫我的信心不停在口里,而是落在行动上——像你所说的,给饥渴的人吃喝、看顾患难中的人,也保守我不沾染世俗。叫我有真的、清洁没有玷污的虔诚。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
James has always been blunt, piercing. Speaking of "true faith," he candidly exposes a self-deception: "If anyone thinks he is religious and does not bridle his tongue but deceives his heart, this person’s religion is worthless." He then gives an unexpected definition of "true religion": "Religion that is pure and undefiled before God, the Father, is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world" (James 1:26-27).

Notice the standard James uses to measure religion — not how often you attend gatherings, how much knowledge you have, how spiritually you speak, but two extremely concrete things: first, "visiting orphans and widows" — caring for those with no one to depend on, no power to repay you; second, "keeping oneself unstained from the world" — not going along with the crowd in values and lifestyle. True faith does not stop at the mind and the tongue, but lands in the hands and feet, in daily life. The Lord Jesus, in the parable of the sheep and the goats, used exactly this same standard: "I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink... I was in prison and you came to me" (Matthew 25:35-36) — what he measures is likewise these concrete, humble, easily overlooked acts of care.

This is an alarm bell for us. We too easily equate "religion" with religious activity, while remaining indifferent to the lonely and afflicted around us; too easily appear spiritual in church, while being no different from the world in lifestyle. James reminds us: what proves faith is real is not what we say, what we believe, but whether our faith goes out and touches those who are suffering.

Meditation: Do I measure my own "religion" by how much religious activity I do, or by what James says — caring for the afflicted, staying unstained from the world? Has my faith reached my hands and feet?

Application: This week, concretely "visit" someone in affliction, someone with no power to repay you — a visit, some help, or simply real companionship, letting your faith grow hands and feet.

Prayer: Lord, forgive me for often equating religion with religious activity, while remaining indifferent to the lonely and afflicted around me. Let my faith not stop at my lips, but land in action — as you said, giving food and drink to the hungry and thirsty, caring for those in affliction, and keeping me unstained from the world. Give me true, pure and undefiled religion. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.verse: 彼得前书二章九节，三章二十至廿一节，五章七节
entries.content:
彼得写信给一群分散各地、饱受逼迫、觉得自己像「客旅、寄居」的信徒。为要坚固他们,他先提醒他们「你是谁」:「惟有你们是被拣选的族类,是有君尊的祭司,是圣洁的国度,是属神的子民,要叫你们宣扬那召你们出黑暗、入奇妙光明者的美德」(彼前2:9)。在患难中,人最需要的,是重新认定自己在神里的身份。这些称呼并非彼得的新造词——早在西奈山下,神就对以色列说:「你们要归我作祭司的国度,为圣洁的国民」(出19:5-6)。彼得在这里宣告:如今在基督里,这身份临到了教会。

这些身份,没有一样是他们靠自己挣来的——「被拣选」「属神」都是神主动施予的恩典。世界或许轻看他们、逼迫他们,但在神眼中,他们是被拣选、有君尊、圣洁、属神的子民。当我们的处境让我们感到卑微、被弃、不被重视时,福音要我们回到这更深、更真的身份里去站立。

正因这稳固的身份,彼得才能在信末发出那句温柔的邀请:「你们要将一切的忧虑卸给神,因为他顾念你们」(彼前5:7)。你不是无根的浮萍,你是神所拣选、所顾念的儿女;所以你可以放心把重担卸给祂。今天,无论环境多让你觉得渺小,先回到你在基督里那不能被夺去的身份里——你是属神的子民,祂顾念你。

默想:当处境让我觉得卑微、被弃时,我是从环境来定义自己,还是从「被拣选、属神」的身份来定义自己?我有没有把忧虑卸给那顾念我的神?

应用:今天把一件压着你的忧虑,具体地「卸给神」,并以彼得前书二章九节的身份向自己宣告:我是属神、被祂顾念的子民。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你拣选我,使我成为属你、有君尊、圣洁的子民,正如你古时应许要以色列作祭司的国度,这全是你的恩典。当处境让我觉得渺小、被弃时,求你叫我回到这真实的身份里站立,并把一切忧虑卸给你,因为你顾念我。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Peter writes to a group of believers scattered abroad, suffering persecution, feeling like "sojourners, exiles." To strengthen them, he first reminds them "who you are": "But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light" (1 Peter 2:9). In hardship, what a person needs most is to reaffirm their identity in God. These titles are not Peter’s invention — long ago at Sinai, God said to Israel: "you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" (Exodus 19:5-6). Peter is declaring here: now, in Christ, this identity has come to the church.

None of these identities were earned by their own effort — "chosen," "God’s own" are all grace actively given by God. The world may despise them, persecute them, but in God’s eyes, they are a chosen, royal, holy, God-belonging people. When our circumstances make us feel small, forsaken, unvalued, the gospel calls us to stand again in this deeper, truer identity.

It is precisely because of this secure identity that Peter, at the letter’s end, can give that tender invitation: "casting all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you" (1 Peter 5:7). You are not a rootless duckweed — you are a child God has chosen, whom he cares for; so you can confidently cast your burdens on him. Today, no matter how small your circumstances make you feel, return first to your unshakeable identity in Christ — you are God’s own people, and he cares for you.

Meditation: When circumstances make me feel small, forsaken, do I define myself by my circumstances, or by my identity of being "chosen, belonging to God"? Have I cast my anxieties on the God who cares for me?

Application: Today, concretely "cast" one anxiety weighing on you onto God, and declare to yourself, using 1 Peter 2:9, the identity: I belong to God, cared for by him.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for choosing me, making me your own, a royal, holy people, just as you promised ancient Israel would be a kingdom of priests — all of this is your grace. When circumstances make me feel small, forsaken, let me return and stand in this true identity, and cast all my anxieties on you, for you care for me. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 主的宽容,是要人悔改
entries.title_en: The Lord's Patience Is Meant to Lead to Repentance
entries.verse: 彼得后书三章九节
entries.content:
有人讥诮说,主再来的应许怎么迟迟不应验?彼得回应:「主所应许的尚未成就,有人以为他是耽延,其实不是耽延,乃是宽容你们,不愿有一人沉沦,乃愿人人都悔改」(彼后3:9)。神看似「慢」,其实是「忍」——祂的延迟,不是不守信,而是给更多人留下悔改的机会。

这句话把神的心肠向我们敞开:祂「不愿有一人沉沦」。每一天主还未再来,都是恩典的日子,是神仍在耐心等候浪子回家的日子。保罗早已提醒罗马的信徒不要误解这份忍耐:「还是你藐视他丰富的恩慈、宽容、忍耐,不晓得他的恩慈是领你悔改呢?」(罗2:4)神的忍耐从不是纵容,而是带着方向的恩慈——它领人悔改,不是让人心安理得地继续沉睡。我们常抱怨神为何不快些施行审判、了结不公;但若审判今天就来,又有多少我们所爱的人还在门外、尚未预备好?

但这也带来一个催逼:既然神如此宽容、如此不愿一人沉沦,我们岂能对身边未信之人无动于衷?神的耐心不是叫我们松懈,而是叫我们趁着还有今天,去传、去爱、去把人带到主面前。主再来的日子必定临到,「像贼来到一样」;在那日之前,神仍在宽容等候——而我们,是祂用来寻回失丧之人的手。

默想:我是否曾误把神的「忍耐」当作「不管」,甚至藐视这份恩慈?若神此刻仍在宽容等候人悔改,这对我怎样看待身边未信的人,有什么催逼?

应用:趁神仍宽容的今天,为一个未信的人踏出一步——真诚的关心、一次邀请、或一句见证,把握这恩典的时机。

祷告:主啊,谢谢你的宽容——你不愿一人沉沦,乃愿人人悔改,你的忍耐正是失丧之人得救的机会。求你叫我不再藐视这恩慈,也不辜负这恩典的日子,把你对失丧者的心肠放在我里面,趁着还有今天,去传扬、去带人来到你面前。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
Some mockers asked why the promise of the Lord’s coming had not yet been fulfilled after so long. Peter responds: "The Lord is not slow to fulfill his promise as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance" (2 Peter 3:9). God seems "slow," but is actually "patient" — his delay is not unfaithfulness, but leaves more people the chance to repent.

This sentence opens God’s heart to us: he "does not wish that any should perish." Every day the Lord has not yet returned is a day of grace, a day when God is still patiently waiting for the prodigal to come home. Paul had already warned the Roman believers not to misunderstand this patience: "do you presume on the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God’s kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?" (Romans 2:4) God’s patience is never indulgence, but kindness with a direction — it leads people to repentance, not letting them settle comfortably back to sleep. We often complain that God doesn’t hurry to bring judgment, to settle injustice; but if judgment came today, how many people we love would still be outside the door, not yet ready?

But this also brings an urgency: since God is so patient, so unwilling that any should perish, how can we remain indifferent to the unbelievers around us? God’s patience is not meant to make us complacent, but meant to make us, while there is still today, go and preach, go and love, go and bring people before the Lord. The day of the Lord’s return will surely come, "like a thief"; before that day, God is still patiently waiting — and we are the hands he uses to seek and save the lost.

Meditation: Have I ever mistaken God’s "patience" for "indifference," even despised this kindness? If God is still patiently waiting for people to repent right now, what urgency does that place on how I view the unbelievers around me?

Application: While God is still patient today, take one step toward an unbeliever — sincere care, an invitation, or a word of testimony — seizing this window of grace.

Prayer: Lord, thank you for your patience — you do not wish that any should perish, but that all should repent, and your patience is exactly the lost’s chance to be saved. Let me stop despising this kindness, and not waste this day of grace — place your heart for the lost within me, and while there is still today, let me go and proclaim, go and bring people before you. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.

entries.title: 主为我们舍命,爱就在此
entries.title_en: By This We Know Love: He Laid Down His Life for Us
entries.verse: 约翰一书三章十六节，约翰一书三章十七节
entries.content:
约翰一书反复讲论「相交」与「相爱」,而爱的定义与根源,都指向十字架:「主为我们舍命,我们从此就知道何为爱;我们也当为弟兄舍命」(约壹3:16)。世人对「爱」有千百种说法,约翰却把它钉在一个确切的地方——各各他的十字架。要认识什么是真爱,就看那舍命的主。这也正是主耶稣自己下的定义:「人为朋友舍命,人的爱心没有比这个大的」(约15:13)——同一位使徒,把主自己的话,活成了整卷书信的根基。

倪柝声常指出:基督徒的爱,不是从自己里面勉强挤出来的一种情感,而是先领受、再流出的生命。我们「知道何为爱」,是因为先经历了主舍命的爱;这爱进到我们里面,就成了我们能去爱弟兄的源头。离了这源头,所谓的爱不过是天然的好感,时有时无、择人而施;唯有从主的爱里支取,才能爱那不可爱的、爱到「舍命」的地步。

而约翰立刻把这爱拉回极其实际的层面:「凡有世上财物的,看见弟兄穷乏,却塞住怜恤的心,爱神的心怎能存在他里面呢?」(约壹3:17)舍命的爱,不总是轰轰烈烈的牺牲,更多是在日常里,为弟兄的需要打开自己的心、自己的手。今天,让主舍命的爱先充满你,再从你里面,流向一个有需要的弟兄。

默想:我对「爱」的理解,是世人那种「感觉」,还是十字架所定义的「舍命」?我能去爱,是靠自己勉强,还是靠先支取主舍命的爱?

应用:今天为一个「不太可爱」或有实际需要的弟兄姊妹,先默想主如何舍命爱你,再从这爱里流出一个具体的行动。

祷告:主啊,你为我舍命,我才知道何为爱,人的爱心没有比这个更大的。求你叫我不靠自己勉强去爱,而是先被你舍命的爱充满,再从里面流向身边的弟兄。当我看见弟兄的需要时,叫我不塞住怜恤的心,而是以行为和诚实去爱。奉主耶稣的名求,阿们。
entries.content_en:
1 John repeatedly discusses "fellowship" and "love," and the definition and source of love both point to the cross: "By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers" (1 John 3:16). The world has a thousand definitions of "love," but John nails it down to one exact place — the cross of Calvary. To know what true love is, look at that Lord who laid down his life. This is exactly the definition the Lord Jesus himself gave: "Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends" (John 15:13) — the same apostle turned the Lord’s own words into the foundation of this whole letter.

Watchman Nee often pointed out: a Christian’s love is not an emotion forced out from within ourselves, but a life first received, then flowing out. We "know what love is" because we first experienced the Lord’s life-laid-down love; this love enters into us, and becomes the source from which we can love our brothers. Apart from this source, so-called love is merely natural affection, coming and going, dependent on who it’s given to; only by drawing from the Lord’s love can we love the unlovable, love to the point of "laying down our lives."

And John immediately pulls this love back to an extremely practical level: "But if anyone has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God’s love abide in him?" (1 John 3:17) Life-laying-down love is not always a dramatic sacrifice — more often it is, in everyday life, opening your heart and your hand for a brother’s need. Today, let the Lord’s life-laid-down love first fill you, then flow out from you to a brother in need.

Meditation: Is my understanding of "love" the world’s kind of "feeling," or the "laying down of life" defined by the cross? Am I able to love by my own forced effort, or by first drawing on the Lord’s life-laid-down love?

Application: Today, for a brother or sister who is "not very lovable" or has a real need, first meditate on how the Lord laid down his life to love you, then let a concrete action flow from that love.

Prayer: Lord, you laid down your life for me, and only then did I know what love is — no one’s love is greater than this. Let me not love by forcing myself, but first be filled with your life-laid-down love, and then let it flow from within me to the brothers around me. When I see a brother’s need, let me not close my heart, but love in deed and in truth. In Jesus’s name I pray, Amen.
